stories.title: Chaos at Prayagraj Magh Mela after police stop chariot:Avimukteshwaranand's disciple detained, dragged by hair beaten as clash lasts 2 hours
stories.summary: A clash broke out between police and disciples of Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand at the Prayagraj Magh Mela, leading to pushing and shoving and a chaotic situation that lasted nearly two hours. Several disciples were taken into custody following the incident. See the pictures of Avimukteshwaranand's disciple being beaten... Police action on disciple caught on video Police detained one of Shankaracharya’s disciples and took him to a temporary outpost. A video accessed by Dainik Bhaskar shows the disciple arguing with policemen, after which the situation escalated. One policeman is seen pulling his hand, while another grabs his hair and pushes him. Inside the camp, the disciple was shoved to the ground, dragged by his hair and punched repeatedly. Throughout the incident, he could be heard screaming and pleading to be released. The identity of the detained disciple has not yet been confirmed. How the dispute began According to sources, the dispute began when police, citing heavy crowding, asked Shankaracharya to get down from his chariot and proceed on foot. The disciples refused and continued moving forward, leading to an argument that soon turned into pushing and shoving. Police officers attempted to defuse the situation and repeatedly requested cooperation, even folding their hands, but the disciples did not agree. Following this, the police took all supporters of Shankaracharya into custody. Palanquin dragged, Shankaracharya alleges harassment

stories.title: BJP leader’s video with ₹500 note bundles surfaces:District minister Gautam Tiwari denies ownership; claims occult practitioners framed him using fake currency
stories.summary: A video allegedly showing a BJP leader surrounded by bundles of ₹500 notes has gone viral in Maharajganj district of UP. The video was reportedly recorded inside a room, where BJP district minister Gautam Tiwari can be clearly seen standing. In the footage, bundles of ₹500 notes are placed on a red carpet in one corner of the room. Gautam Tiwari is seen examining the bundles using the flashlight of his mobile phone. The person recording the video can be heard asking him to switch off the flashlight, saying that “Minister ji has already made a video.” More than 150 bundles of ₹500 notes More than 150 bundles of ₹500 notes are visible in the 20-second clip. However, the BJP leader has strongly denied that the money belongs to him. First 2 pictures- Money in video fake After the video surfaced, Gautam Tiwari spoke to journalists and rejected all allegations. He claimed that the incident was the result of a conspiracy involving people practising tantra-mantra (occult rituals). According to him, a group of five to six people cheated him of around ₹1.5 crore in the name of a land deal. He alleged that when he demanded the return of the money, they began blackmailing him by making a video using fake currency bundles, which he claimed were actually made of paper. However, he failed to clearly explain when and where the video was recorded. What Gautam Tiwari told media Reporter: A video is going viral showing bundles worth crores of rupees. You are also seen in it. What is the truth? Gautam Tiwari: The video was made by someone from Banaras. The money is fake and made of paper. This is the work of occult practitioners. Reporter: Are you being questioned or interrogated in the video? Gautam Tiwari: No, there was no interrogation. I have applied to an FIR. The money is fake. Reporter: You are claiming that about ₹1.5 crore was taken from you? Gautam Tiwari: Yes. Five or six people together took the money. I have filed a complaint at the police station. Reporter: What was the money given for? Gautam Tiwari: It was for a land deal. We are involved in the vegetable business. The money is stuck in Banaras, but it is not related to our business income. Reporter: Social media users are linking this money to hawala operations. Gautam Tiwari: That is completely false. There is no hawala case. The money shown in the video is not real. Reporter: Can you tell when and where the video was recorded? Gautam Tiwari: I cannot say exactly. I can only say that the money shown is fake. Reporter: Do you believe the matter is now clear? Gautam Tiwari: Yes. I have applied to an FIR. The police will investigate and take action. I want to live my life peacefully now. No complaint received yet When contacted, Kotwali Inspector Nirbhay Singh told Dainik Bhaskar that no formal complaint or application has been received so far regarding the matter. He said that if any written complaint is submitted, the police will investigate the case and take action as per the law.

stories.title: Mother clings to Major son’s coffin in Meerut:Says, 'My groom son is leaving'; brother sister cry uncontrollably
stories.summary: The body of Army Major Shubham Saini, who lost his life in a road accident near Dehradun, reached his home in Meerut on Sunday. The tragic incident occurred when his car lost control and plunged into a nearly 50-metre-deep gorge in Uttarakhand. After several hours of rescue efforts, Major Saini was pulled out of the gorge and rushed to the Dehradun Military Hospital in a critical condition. Doctors later declared him dead. The 27-year-old officer was posted in Chakrata, Uttarakhand, and was travelling to Dehradun on Saturday morning for official work. See 3 photos... Family Background and Personal Life Major Shubham Saini hailed from Ghasouli village in Meerut. He was the second of three siblings. His elder brother, Tushar Saini, works in an IT company, while his younger sister, Nidhi Saini, is a teacher at an Army School. His father, Satyendra Saini, is a retired Subedar from the Indian Army. The family was preparing for a wedding, as Major Saini’s elder brother was due to get married on February 18. Speaking to the media, his father said that Shubham had called him just a day before the accident to ask about the wedding preparations and mentioned that he would apply for leave to come home. Army Career Major Saini came from a family deeply connected to the armed forces. After completing his intermediate education from an Army School, he was selected for the National Defence Academy (NDA) in 2015. His passing-out parade was held in Dehradun in 2019. He was commissioned as a Lieutenant and later promoted to the rank of Major. His first posting was in Bathinda, Punjab. His father recalled that Shubham had dreamt of joining the Army since childhood and worked hard both physically and mentally alongside his studies to achieve his goal. Mourning in Village and City Following the news of his death, a wave of grief swept through his village and his residence in Saraswati Vihar on Rohta Road, Meerut. Large numbers of people gathered to pay their respects and offer condolences to the bereaved family. Several social and political figures, including former MLA Jitendra Satwai, Hindu Mahasangh president Mange Sharma, Dr Vikas Khatik, Ankit Rathi and David, expressed deep sorrow over the untimely death of the young Army officer.

stories.title: 6 criminals hold retired clerk's family hostage in Sitapur:Loot jewellery worth ₹50 lakh cash, escape through roof, police forensic team investigates
stories.summary: Criminals took the son and daughter-in-law of a retired Lekhpal hostage and looted jewellery and cash worth 50 lakhs in UP's Sitapur. 6 criminals entered the house through the roof. They held 6 family members hostage at gunpoint. They snatched everyone's mobile phones. Women and men were locked in separate rooms. After this, they kept searching the entire house for an hour. The criminals broke all the boxes and cupboards in the house and looted jewellery worth 45 lakhs along with 5 lakhs in cash. After the robbery, the criminals threatened to kill the family members and fled from the scene. After the criminals left, the victim's family somehow managed to come out. They called the police and informed them about the incident. Police arrived at the scene with a forensic team and dog squad. Evidence was collected by questioning nearby residents. The incident took place in Rasulpur village of the Talgaon police station area. Robbery in house built between fields Amar Singh Verma, a resident of Rasulpur village, was a revenue department clerk. He retired 5 years ago. He owns 45 bighas of land in the village. He had built a house right in the middle of fields, some distance from Basti. There are fields all around. After retirement, Amar moved to his house built in Sitapur. His two sons, Pushkar and Amar, stayed in the village with their families. Both are involved in buying and selling paddy. 6 criminals entered through roof, held hostage at gunpoint Pushkar said that on Saturday, all family members were sleeping after having dinner. Around 3 AM, 6 criminals entered the house through the roof. After this, they went to everyone's rooms one by one and removed their blankets, taking all family members hostage at gunpoint. Took jewellery worth 45 lakhs and 5 lakhs cash The criminals locked the men of the house in one room and the women and children in another room. They took everyone's phones and kept them outside so that no one could contact the police or nearby people. After this, they broke open the almirah and looted my wife's jewellery and my younger brother's wife's jewellery worth about 45 lakhs. They also took 5 lakh rupees cash kept in the almirah. Police-forensic team and dog squad engaged in investigation Upon receiving information, the Talgaon police station reached the spot and started an investigation. The forensic team and dog squad have also reached the spot and are gathering evidence. People in the surrounding area are being questioned, and possible escape routes of the criminals are being investigated. SP Ankur Agrawal said- In Rasulpur village, 5 to 6 miscreants entered the victim's house and committed robbery at gunpoint. In this incident, approximately 4 to 5 lakh rupees in cash and jewelry were looted. Police teams have been deployed and the case will be solved soon. Terror among villagers, demand for increased patrolling Police officials say that the case will be solved soon and the criminals will be arrested. Meanwhile, after the incident, there is an atmosphere of terror in the village and the surrounding areas. Villagers have demanded increased night patrolling and strengthening of security arrangements.

stories.title: Prayagraj student preparing for JEE, dies by suicide:Records apology video before hanging himself; police probe stress factors
stories.summary: A student preparing for the Joint Entrance Exam (JEE) in Prayagraj committed suicide. His body was found hanging from a press wire noose. Before dying, he recorded a video on his mobile. In it, he was crying and saying, "Sorry Papa... I can't study anymore." The incident came to light when the student didn't come out of his room at 11 AM on Saturday. Fellow students knocked on the door but got no response. Then, looking through the window, they found Kuldeep Vishwakarma's body hanging. Police broke down the door to retrieve the body. 25-year-old Kuldeep was from Hamirpur. He had been staying here for a year, preparing for the exam. The entire incident took place in the Saloori area of Colonelganj. Police are investigating whether Kuldeep was under exam pressure or any other kind of stress. The student's family members arrived in Prayagraj today. After this, a post-mortem of the body will be conducted. Kuldeep Vishwakarma lived in a rented room in Salori's Badi Bagiya. He lived alone in the room. According to police, on Saturday morning, Kuldeep did not come out of his room for a long time. At 11 AM, a young man living next door knocked on his room's door, but there was no response from inside. After this, the youth looked inside through the window. Kuldeep was seen hanging from the fan inside the room. After this, the youth immediately informed the students living nearby. People informed the police. Police arrived at the scene and broke down the door to enter the room. Police, with the help of people, brought down student Kuldeep's body from the noose and took him to a nearby hospital. Doctors at the hospital declared him dead. 1-minute video found on mobile Kuldeep's phone was not locked. When police checked the mobile, they found a 1-minute video. In the video, Kuldeep is emotionally apologizing to his parents while crying. Police informed the family about this. The family has asked police not to share the video with anyone. Karnalganj Station In-charge Sanjay Kumar Singh said - Kuldeep hanged himself using a press wire. The body has been kept safely in the postmortem house. The family has been informed, postmortem will be conducted on Sunday after they arrive. Police is investigating the entire matter.

stories.title: From feasts to Rashtrakatha, caste signals grow louder:Alongwith Thakur and Brahmin strength shaping strategies, ahead of UP Assembly Elections in 2027 cycle
stories.summary: Recent events in Uttar Pradesh, from family meetings to Brahmin MLAs’ feasts and Rashtrakatha in Awadh, may appear different, but their core aim is the same: retaining political power. The spotlight is increasingly on influential Kshatriya leaders, with frequent comparisons between figures like Raja Bhaiya, Brij Bhushan Singh, Abhay Singh, Brajesh Singh, and Dhananjay Singh. Brij Bhushan Singh dismisses such comparisons as attempts to divide the Rajput community, saying Union minister Rajnath Singh stands above all. With the 2027 Assembly elections approaching, caste politics is intensifying. Brahmins and Thakurs together account for 101 of UP’s 403 MLAs, almost every fourth legislator, prompting Kshatriya leaders to assert and consolidate their political influence. Kshatriya is the third-largest caste group in UP UP politics cannot be understood separately from caste. Whenever there are elections here, the caste factor remains at the top. Political parties lay out their electoral strategy around this factor for electoral success. Among UP's castes, Brahmins are the largest vote bank. There are 9 to 11 percent Brahmins in the state. Yadavs are second with 8 to 9 percent population, and Kshatriyas are third with 7 to 8 percent population. Despite this, in election results, the number of Kshatriya MLAs often remains considerable. In the current assembly, after 52 Brahmin MLAs, there are 49 Kshatriya MLAs. While the number of Yadav MLAs is at fourth place after Kurmi MLAs. In UP, there are 70-80 assembly seats where the Kshatriya vote bank is 10 to 20 percent. This includes districts like Gorakhpur, Gonda, Ayodhya, Ballia, Azamgarh, Mirzapur, Sonbhadra in eastern UP, Jalaun, Hamirpur in Bundelkhand, and Meerut, Muzaffarnagar, Saharanpur, Ghaziabad, Bulandshahr in the west. Additionally, Kshatriyas are influential in 20 Lok Sabha seats. What's happening in UP politics regarding Kshatriya leaders In UP's monsoon session, 40 Kshatriya MLAs from different parties sat together in a hotel after a long time. This unity happened in the name of the family community. The discussion focused on the current state and direction of the Rajput community. Later, all MLAs were gifted with Lord Ram's idol, Maharana Pratap's picture, and a brass trident. After this, the codeine cough syrup case emerged in the state. Some close associates of Jaunpur's strongman Dhananjay Singh were arrested in this case. Dhananjay Singh's name was heavily publicized regarding this. Then, statements by Abhay Singh against him were given significant attention. In the new year, Gonda's strongman leader, Brij Bhushan Singh, organized a Rashtrakatha on the occasion of his birthday. Through this katha, Brij Bhushan Singh demonstrated his dominance. Amid these discussions, a video of Brij Bhushan Singh emerged, in which he is seen giving a strong reaction to being compared with Raja Bhaiya. Brij Bhushan Singh begins his statement with the Ramcharit Manas couplet-'As one's feelings are, so does one see the Lord's image,' and says- Seeing a post on social media made me very sad. It asked who is the bigger leader of Kshatriyas - Raja Bhaiya or Brij Bhushan Singh? So let me clarify that those who want to know Raja Bhaiya's history should first read about his father Maharaj Uday Singh's history. He is a symbol of struggle, and I consider him my idol. Raja Bhaiya is his son. By age, he is my younger brother and also a friend of my children. Please don't talk such nonsense. Before this, it was Abhay Singh bigger or Dhananjay Singh? What do you get by determining who is bigger and who is smaller? I request you with folded hands not to make such comments about anyone. The national narrative was meant to unite, not divide. Let's say Raja Bhaiya is bigger. What's your problem with that? Right now, Rajnath Singh is there; he is senior to all of us. Don't try to divide society. Don't try to create conflicts. Are Kshatriya MLAs uniting These developments have sparked a discussion in UP politics about whether Kshatriya MLAs and leaders are trying to unite by putting aside their differences. Senior journalist Suresh Bahadur Singh says - Kshatriya MLAs can never unite. Every Kshatriya MLA considers himself superior to others. If this wasn't the case, what was the reason that the united meeting of Kshatriya MLAs happened after 35 years? Before this, Jagdambika Pal had called such a meeting in the 80s while being in Congress. At that time, Kshatriya MLAs from all parties had gathered at the Clark Avadh Hotel in Lucknow. Anyway, Kshatriyas have never remained bound to one party. During Congress time, they were with them, then during VP Singh's time, they became part of Janata Dal. Later, SP became their base. Now in the present time, the BJP has the maximum number of Kshatriya MLAs. BSP was the only party where Kshatriyas never joined in large numbers. However, when several Kshatriya MLAs won from BSP, Kshatriya voters also played a role in their victory. Due to the Raja Bhaiya incident, Kshatriyas maintained a certain displeasure with BSP. BJP gave maximum tickets to Kshatriyas in 2022 BJP gave the most tickets to Kshatriyas in the 2022 assembly elections. One reason is that 43 Kshatriya MLAs from the BJP won and reached the assembly, the highest number. BJP had fielded 71 candidates. While SP fielded only 23 and BSP fielded only 28 Kshatriya candidates. According to the Lokniti-CSDS survey, the BJP received 87 percent of Kshatriya votes in 2022. SP was in second place, which received 7 percent support from Kshatriyas. When were the major Kshatriya leaders in UP Vishwanath Pratap Singh from Ghazipur and Chandrashekhar Singh from Ballia, both from UP's Purvanchal region, became Prime Ministers of India. Vishwanath Pratap Singh also served as CM of UP from the Congress. Before him, Veer Bahadur Singh from Gorakhpur was the Congress CM. Senior journalist Sharad Pradhan says about the characteristics of these three leaders - they never did caste politics. Veer Bahadur Singh remained very popular among both upper castes and backward classes. Similarly, Chandrashekhar's entire politics remained purely socialist. He was equally popular among upper castes, backward classes, Dalits, and Muslims. It is well known that Vishwanath Pratap Singh was the one who gave rights to backward classes in this country by implementing the Mandal Commission. When he became CM of UP for the first time, most people didn't even know him. His only identity then was that he was the paternal uncle-in-law of Sanjay Singh of Amethi. Senior journalist Suresh Bahadur Singh says about VP Singh - Had he not implemented the Mandal Commission, Ram Vilas Paswan, Nitish Kumar, Mulayam Singh Yadav, and many other backward leaders in the country would never have been able to create their separate identity. BJP senior leader Rajnath Singh, who has been active in politics since the 90s, also comes from Purvanchal. He is also a Kshatriya, but never did caste politics. Rajnath Singh is popular among all sections. Sharad Pradhan says that Rajnath Singh was never labeled as a Thakur-centric leader. Nor did all the Kshatriyas of UP ever accept him as their sole universally accepted leader. How much benefit does a community leader get from caste vote bank Kshatriya voters make up around 10–20% in 70–80 assembly seats in Uttar Pradesh, but experts say no leader can win on the strength of one caste alone. Senior journalist Harshvardhan Shahi explains that on any seat, at least 80% voters belong to other castes, making broad social support essential. This is why Akhilesh Yadav shifted from the MY formula to PDA, realising power cannot be gained without including all sections. Even when caste support exists, voters often back the more dominant candidate within the same community. Historical examples, like BSP’s 2007 win linked to Brahmin outreach, show that lasting success comes only when parties secure majority support across communities, not from a single caste vote bank. What is the history of the one whom Brij Bhushan called ideal? Brij Bhushan Singh has described Raja Uday Pratap Singh as his ideal, stressing the importance of knowing one’s history. Senior journalist Suresh Bahadur Singh says that although the Constitution recognises no kings today, people in Kunda still respectfully call Uday Pratap Singh “Raja Saheb” or “Baba Saheb”. Born in 1933, Uday Pratap Singh was adopted by his uncle, Raja Bajrang Bahadur Singh, a freedom fighter. Bajrang Bahadur Singh later founded Pantnagar Agricultural University, served as its Vice Chancellor, and went on to become the second Lieutenant Governor of Himachal Pradesh. He shared close ties with Jawaharlal Nehru, while his wife Rani Girija Devi was close to Indira Gandhi. Uday Pratap Singh, who succeeded his father, stayed close to the VHP and RSS rather than Congress and donated several properties to them. He played a key role in banning plastic bags in Uttar Pradesh and founded Prakriti, an organisation working for environmental protection. He also established and supported many schools and colleges. During Indira Gandhi’s tenure as Prime Minister, he declared Bhadri an independent state, forcing the Centre to deploy forces in Kunda. In 2002, when Mayawati was UP Chief Minister, Uday Pratap Singh and his son Raja Bhaiya were jailed under POTA for nearly a year, drawing strong support from the Kshatriya community across the state.

stories.title: Man kills his 32 year younger girlfriend brutally in Jhansi:Cut her body, burned parts for 7 days, then fled carrying her in a blue box
stories.summary: In Jhansi, a boyfriend murdered his girlfriend. He dismembered the body. A retired railway employee had been burning one body part daily for 7 days with the intention of disposing of the body. Later, he was going to throw away the remaining half-burnt parts, bones, and ashes packed in a blue box. Accused Brijbhan booked an auto late Saturday night. He got into it with the box. Then, halfway through, he made an excuse, got off, and fled. The auto driver became suspicious when he noticed a foul smell and water dripping from the box. He informed the police at 2 AM. When the police arrived at the scene and opened the box, they were shocked. Inside the box was a half-burnt body. Police reached the accused's house based on the auto driver's information. They took the accused into custody from there and started interrogation. The deceased was identified as Preeti (40). She lived in a live-in relationship with Brijbhan in Brahm Nagar, Sipri Bazaar.

stories.title: 'There's a bomb on the plane':Indigo flight makes emergency landing in Lucknow; note stuck on bathroom napkin
stories.summary: There was a major commotion after a bomb threat was received on an Indigo flight. The aircraft, en route from Delhi to Bagdogra (West Bengal), was made to make an emergency landing in Lucknow at short notice. According to airport sources, ATC received information about a bomb on Indigo flight 6E-6650 on Sunday at 8:46 am. The aircraft landed at Lucknow Airport at 9:17 am. Passengers were disembarked and the aircraft was parked in the isolation bay. Threat written on napkin According to reports, a threat was found written on a napkin inside the aircraft’s bathroom. It read, “There is a bomb on the plane.” A passenger noticed the napkin and informed a crew member. Subsequently, the flight was immediately diverted to Lucknow. Here, the bomb disposal squad, fire brigade, medical team and other security agencies surrounded the aircraft. Search operation by bomb squad Bomb Threat on Indigo Flight; Emergency Landing in Lucknow An Indigo flight from Delhi to Bagdogra was forced to make an emergency landing in Lucknow after a bomb threat. ATC received the alert at 8:46 am on Sunday, and the aircraft landed at Lucknow Airport at 9:17 am. Passengers were safely disembarked and the plane was moved to an isolation bay. Bomb Threat Found in Aircraft Washroom A napkin with a bomb threat was found in the aircraft washroom. The message read: “There is a bomb on the plane.” A passenger noticed it and alerted the crew, following which the flight was immediately diverted to Lucknow. The bomb disposal squad, fire brigade, medical team and other security agencies reached the aircraft and began an investigation. Radioactive Material Also Reported on Board Airport sources revealed that, besides the bomb threat, information was received that packed radioactive material was being carried in the aircraft’s luggage compartment. Considering the seriousness of the situation, a Bomb Threat Assessment Committee (BTAC) has been formed to evaluate the case. Aircraft Under Security Watch for Over 4 Hours The plane has been parked in the isolation bay. The Quick Response Team (QRT) has fully cordoned off the aircraft and is conducting a thorough security check. The aircraft remained at the airport even after 4.5 hours, as of 2 pm. IndiGo Statement: Safety Is Priority IndiGo Airlines stated the emergency landing, saying, On January 18 2026, IndiGo flight 6E 6650 from Delhi to Bagdogra reported a security concern, following which the aircraft was diverted to Lucknow. As per protocol, we immediately informed the relevant authorities and are fully cooperating with the required security checks.We are doing our best to minimise inconvenience to passengers, including providing refreshments and regular updates. As always, the safety and security of our passengers, crew and aircraft remains our top priority. Earlier Bomb Threat on Star Air Flight (19 October 2024) On 19 October 2024, a Star Air flight travelling from Lucknow to Kishangarh (Ajmer) received a bomb threat. The aircraft was immediately grounded and a thorough search was conducted, including the cargo area. No suspicious item was found. 30 October 2024: Bomb Threat on Two IndiGo Flights Just 11 days later, on 30 October 2024, two IndiGo flights — 6E-518 (Delhi–Lucknow) and 6E-1416 (Abu Dhabi–Lucknow) — received bomb threats. Security personnel took control of both aircraft and conducted thorough checks, but nothing suspicious was found. 7 November 2025: Three IndiGo Flights Made Emergency Landings at Lucknow

stories.title: Babri demolition tests Kalyan Singh’s leadership in UP:Refusal to order firing, resignation, President’s Rule, and jail term shape his lasting political legacy
stories.summary: In politics, some leaders make history, and some themselves become historical figures. A farmer's son who emerged from the soil of fields reached the pinnacle of power. A leader who was known for speaking directly and remaining firm on decisions, his name is Kalyan Singh. Today in 'Political Arena' is the story of that leader who balanced 'Mandal-Kamandal' politics to form the BJP's first full majority government in UP. Changes came, paths changed, but Kalyan Singh's identity always remained... Year 1991 11 Ashok Road, New Delhi Evening had fallen, but political activity was intense at the BJP office. For the first time, the BJP had won a full majority in Uttar Pradesh. This was not just an electoral victory, but a major turning point in Indian politics. The meeting was going on till late at night in the party office room. This was not celebration time, but the time to determine power and responsibility. A leader said in a low voice, "This victory is not ordinary. For the first time in UP, we have got a full majority." Another immediately added - "We don't just have to form a government, we also have to give a social message." All senior BJP leaders were present at the meeting. Lal Krishna Advani, Atal Bihari Vajpayee, and National President Murli Manohar Joshi. UP BJP President Kalyan Singh was also in the room. Face calm, eyes down. A leader looked at Joshi and said, "The question is who should be made CM?" Silence prevailed for a moment. Then someone brought up the Mandal Commission. "UP has changed after Mandal. Caste, class, forward-backward all stand in new places." A voice came from the other side - "The temple movement also has to be taken forward. In changed equations, all this won't be easy." Just then, someone said, "The responsibility should be given to the one whom the public has already accepted." Many eyes fixed on Kalyan Singh at once, but he remained calm. Just then came the sound of a chair moving. Atal Bihari Vajpayee stood up. Sudden silence deepened in the room. Atal ji smiled and moved towards the box of sweets kept on the table. He picked up a laddu and went to Kalyan Singh. Kalyan Singh tried to stand up. Atal ji said, "Please remain seated." He extended the laddu with his hand, smiled, and said, "Congratulations." Kalyan Singh hesitated for a moment, then ate the laddu. No proposal was presented, no voting took place. One laddu made everything clear. The message was clear about who would now take command of Uttar Pradesh. Just a few days later, on June 24, 1991, Kalyan Singh took oath as Chief Minister at Lucknow Raj Bhavan. The Gandhi Hall of Raj Bhavan was packed. After taking the oath, Kalyan Singh folded his hands and said, "This is not just a position, it's a responsibility." Whispers began in the corridors of power - "From today, UP politics will move in a new direction." This became visible within a few hours. After taking the oath, Chief Minister Kalyan Singh reached Ayodhya with his entire cabinet. A minister quietly asked, "Is it necessary to go to Ayodhya so soon?" Kalyan Singh said - "It is necessary to remind of the resolution on which the government was formed." Upon reaching Ayodhya, a sage said, "Now the path for the temple is clear." Kalyan Singh said, "Whatever happens will happen within the bounds of law." Days began to pass. Meetings intensified in villages and towns. Posters started appearing on walls - "If kar seva stops, useless seva will begin." Only one thing echoed in the meetings. "What remained incomplete in 1990 must now be completed." July of 1992 arrived. Tensions increased across the country, including in Ayodhya. Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) started kar seva on July 9 to build the platform. The situation was heating up. On July 15, the Allahabad High Court ordered an immediate stop to the Kar Seva. The saints and seers remained adamant, saying, "We will not stop. This is a matter of religion." VHP chief Ashok Singhal was assured that Prime Minister Narasimha Rao would personally look into the matter. A solution would be found through discussions within three months. After much persuasion, the kar seva was stopped on July 26. The talks began, but Hindu leaders were accusing the government - "The stance changes in every meeting." Three months passed quickly, and October arrived. Ashok Singhal clearly stated, "Kar seva will resume in Ayodhya from December 6." Now there was no question of backing down. The situation became so heated that there was unrest even in Delhi. In the Supreme Court, the judge asked sternly, "If violence occurs in Ayodhya, who will take responsibility?" There was chaos in Lucknow. In the secretariat, only one question echoed in the minds of officials. "What answer should be given to the court...?" Kalyan Singh softly said, "Whatever happens, it will be written in history." November 28, 1992 The Kalyan Singh government submitted an affidavit in the Supreme Court. The government's lawyer said, "Nothing will happen to Babri Masjid. We fully guarantee this." The court read the paper. There was silence for a moment. Then the judge's voice echoed - "If the government is giving guarantee, then it's fine..." Then, in a stern voice, a warning - "The Chief Minister will be responsible for the security of Babri Masjid. If even a stone falls, there will be accountability." Meanwhile, efforts continued to stop the VHP or at least divert its direction regarding the kar seva. Dialogue was attempted, and assurances were given. Still, nothing worked. From December 3rd, thousands of kar sevaks started arriving in Ayodhya. By December 5th, BJP-VHP leaders like Lal Krishna Advani, Ashok Singhal, Murli Manohar Joshi, Vinay Katiyar had reached Ayodhya. December 6th, exactly 7:30 AM. 5 Kalidas Marg, Lucknow. There was silence in the guest room of the Chief Minister's residence. Anxiety was clearly visible on Chief Minister Kalyan Singh's face. While flipping through the newspaper, he muttered, "Ayodhya is on every page. The crowd of kar sevaks shows no sign of decreasing." Then he looked at his PA and said - "Get me the Faizabad DM on the line." As soon as the phone connected, Kalyan Singh asked directly, "How is the situation?" The DM replied, "Sir, the situation is under control. Please don't worry." The phone got disconnected. Kalyan Singh took a deep breath. Softly said- "It's under control, but my heart is not accepting it." Glanced at the clock. It was 10 o'clock. Just then, the door opened. Health Minister Suryapratap Shahi entered the room- "Namaste brother..." Revenue State Minister Baleshwar Tyagi was also with him. Upon seeing them, Kalyan Singh said, "Come, let's go upstairs. We'll talk in some open space." All three sat in the tin shed built on the first floor. There was mild December sunlight. Suryapratap said, "The crowd is more than expected." Kalyan Singh said, "The news has been troubling since morning." The conversation was ongoing when two other ministers, Rajendra Gupta and Lalji Tandon, also arrived. Upon seeing the CM, Gupta said, "Brother, serious news is coming in." Lalji Tandon said in a low voice- "Heard that some kar sevaks have climbed on the dome." For a moment, everyone fell silent. Kalyan Singh stood up. "Is it confirmed news or just a rumor?" During the Babri Masjid crisis, Kalyan Singh received multiple calls from officials and leaders, including Atal Bihari Vajpayee and L.K. Advani, warning him to handle the situation carefully. Reports came in that kar sevaks had climbed the mosque with hammers and rods, and vandalism was spreading. DGP S.N. Tripathi urged the CM to take immediate action, even suggesting firing. Kalyan Singh firmly refused, instructing that the crowd be controlled without opening fire. He documented his order in writing and signed it, directing officials to act accordingly. This decision, taken amid escalating tension, became a pivotal moment in the events leading to the Babri Masjid demolition. Around 1 PM On the day the Babri Masjid demolition began, Home Minister S. B. Chavan called Kalyan Singh, demanding action as kar sevaks were atop the mosque. Kalyan Singh firmly refused to fire on the devotees, stating he would not take action against them. As news came that one dome had been demolished, Kalyan Singh, feeling deceived by senior BJP leaders who seemed to act without informing him, decided to resign. He consulted his ministers about what reason to give, and it was agreed that no reason should be mentioned. He began drafting his resignation, just as news arrived that a third dome had also fallen, marking the height of the crisis. On December 8, Kalyan Singh, along with his cabinet, resigned as Uttar Pradesh CM, and shortly after, the Central government dismissed his government, imposing President’s rule. He declared to the press that the government’s purpose related to the Ram temple was fulfilled and accepted responsibility for any legal consequences. Later, Mohammad Aslam filed a petition alleging contempt of court in the Ayodhya case. On October 24, 1994, the Supreme Court found Kalyan Singh guilty of contempt, sentencing him to one day in jail and a fine of ₹20,000. Following the court order, he was arrested from UP Bhawan and sent to Tihar Jail under DG Kiran Bedi’s supervision, serving the sentence until the next morning, marking a historic moment in Indian politics. *** Story Edit - Krishna Gopal *** References Books - Yuddh Mein Ayodhya - Hemant Sharma | Jo Bhula Na Saka - Baleshwar Tyagi | Jo Yaad Raha - Baleshwar Tyagi Senior Journalists - Brajesh Shukla, Rajendra Kumar Kalyan Singh's Associates - Baleshwar Tyagi (Former State Minister), Shyam Nandan Singh (Former MLC) Creative liberty has been used to make the story interesting.

stories.title: Sadhvi Harsha claims she received offers to convert religion:Mahakumbh sensation says saints avoid meeting her, gets threats after her announcement to quit preaching
stories.summary: Harsha Richhariya, who is in the news because of a viral social media video, says she is getting threats and abusive messages after announcing that she is leaving the path of religion. Harsha said that ever since she spoke about quitting religious work, people have been abusing her and making vulgar comments. She also said that people from different religions are sending her messages and asking her to read about their faith and adopt it. In the video, Harsha said with a heavy heart that she is ending her work of religious propagation and returning to her old profession as an anchor. While speaking to Bhaskar, Harsha said that when a girl moves forward on the path of religion, some people try to stop her and pull her down. She shared more about the threats and pressure she is facing since her announcement. Seen with saints in the Peshwai procession at Mahakumbh Harsha Richharia's name became a topic of discussion across the country when, on January 4, 2025, during the Prayagraj Mahakumbh, she was seen riding on a chariot with saints in the grand Peshwai procession of Niranjani Akhara. Her photos and videos quickly went viral on social media. People started calling her 'the most beautiful Sadhvi of Mahakumbh,' and she became an overnight internet sensation. Along with this fame, controversy also became associated. Some religious gurus, like Shambhavi Peethadhishwar Swami Anand Swaroop Maharaj, objected to this, saying, 'This is not appropriate. It spreads a wrong message in society. Making religion a part of a performance is dangerous.' It was from here that a period of difficulties began for Harsha, which she had never even imagined. Harsha said - When her own people started attacking Harsha says that after gaining fame, she did not receive acceptance in the saint community. Whenever she went to meet a saint, she was made to wait for hours. Her old anchoring profession was viewed with a dirty eye and she was made to feel as if she had committed a great sin in the past. Harsha says, 'I am proud of my old profession. It gave me my identity. I left everything and chose the path of religion, but here I found doubt instead of support. Our own religious leaders suspect us and we have to give explanations. There is a lack of unity in our religion; everyone is filled with ego.' Threats are being received and she is being incited to convert After her announcement to quit religious preaching, this harassment intensified. Harsha stated that she is receiving threatening messages not only from people of other religions but also from some contractors of her own religion. She is being incited to convert. Additionally, an endless stream of obscene messages and abuses has begun. She says, "People are saying that I've gained fame and recognition, so now I'm leaving everything. The very people who claim to be protectors of sisters are standing against me today. They are even showing people of other religions how to abuse and threaten me." Harsha clarified that she is a Sanatani and will always remain one, but she cannot bear this mental anguish any longer. 'Land not given for camp in Magh Mela' The biggest setback for Harsha came during the Magh Mela in December 2025. She applied for land allocation to set up her camp at the fair. Initially, the concerned officials assured her and even approved the process. But as soon as some influential saints got wind of it, they started pressuring the officials. Harsha says, 'Some saints threatened the officials not to give me the land. After this, the officials stopped answering my calls and stopped meeting me. I did not get the land. This incident proved to be the last straw for her. She says that she never took a single penny from devotees, managing everything at her own expense.' 'If circumstances change, I will return to this path' Learning from her experience, Harsha has given important advice to youth and women. She said, "If you want to connect with religion, limit yourself to your family and home temple. Don't blindly follow anyone. " Finally, Harsha clarified that she has only given up preaching religion, not Sanatan Dharma. She also said that if a miracle happens in the future and circumstances change, she will not hesitate to return to this path again.

stories.title: Cold wave, fog wreak havoc in Uttar Pradesh:15 vehicles collide in Amroha; 12 dead in 22 accidents, 75 injured statewide
stories.summary: Severe cold and dense fog continue to wreak havoc across Uttar Pradesh. For the second consecutive day, more than 50 districts, including Lucknow, Barabanki, Prayagraj and Ayodhya, remained under a thick blanket of fog. Visibility in many areas dropped to between zero and 50 metres, with conditions so poor that roads were virtually invisible and even vehicle headlights could not be seen. On Sunday alone, 22 road accidents were reported across the State, involving 70 vehicles. At least 12 people were killed and 75 others injured. In Amroha, a dozen vehicles piled up, leaving a long trail of damaged cars on the highway; one person died in the crash. Two deaths each were reported from Kanpur and Amethi, while one person each lost their lives in Barabanki, Amroha, Kasganj, Muzaffarnagar and Mainpuri. Earlier on Saturday, seven people were killed in road accidents across 16 districts. Low visibility has also badly hit rail and air services. More than 100 trains are running late at several stations, including Gorakhpur and Varanasi. At Lucknow airport, flights arriving from Ras Al Khaimah in the UAE and Mumbai circled in the air for nearly half an hour. As landing permission was not granted, the flights were diverted to Delhi. In the last 24 hours, Hardoi recorded the lowest temperature at 3.5°C. The Meteorological Department said snowfall in the hills has intensified the cold spell. Cold conditions are expected to persist for another three days, with dense fog likely to continue. stories.title: Magh Mela emerges as livelihood hub for young Indians:Made living by offering photos with guitar at ₹5; some dress, and act as Pushpa
stories.summary: Before Mahakumbh-2025, the Magh Mela was mainly religious, but Mahakumbh created jobs and recognition for many people. Its impact is now visible at Magh Mela-2026, where many youths have arrived seeking work and opportunities. Some are earning well, while others are still struggling or trying to gain popularity using their skills. Inspired by this, Shivam, who is preparing for competitive exams in Kanpur, came to Prayagraj with his guitar after seeing employment possibilities at large fairs. Shivam set up a small stall at the Magh Mela, offering photos with a guitar for ₹5. Inspired by online videos, he earned around ₹1,000 on the first day and plans to stay if the response continues, while preparing for Group D exams in Kanpur. At VIP Ghat, Ravikishan Mishra from Madhya Pradesh was seen dressed as Pushpa. Visiting Prayag for the first time, he believes in the city’s reputation for turning opportunities into success and says he is receiving a positive response so far. Ravi says, 'I come from a poor family'. I like acting. I want to pursue this line. Once, I went to Varanasi dressed as Pushpa. People there also appreciated it a lot. During school days, I played the role of an illiterate MLA in an interview. Since then, I got the idea to pursue acting. Ravi spends the whole day embodying Pushpa's character and speaks dialogues in his style. Crowds gather around him, and people are taking photos with him. Business of selling perfumes and toothbrushes did not work out 22-year-old Ashish is pursuing a lab technician course. He lives in Prayagraj. He came to the fair to earn money and started selling perfumes. Ashish says - I got this idea from Mahakumbh. That's why I came here to sell perfumes, but I haven't received any response yet. No one is buying. This has been the situation for 2-3 days. If it continues like this, I will go back home. I won't do any other work. Avadh Kumar Yadav has come from Sonbhadra. He sells toothbrushes at Sangam Ghat. He says - After watching people's videos, I brought toothbrushes from home. It's been a week, but no one is asking. No one at the ghat is even mentioning toothbrushes. If this continues, we will leave soon. After this, Avadh Kumar sang a song related to Prayagraj. He said that singing is my hobby, and I want people to know me through this. Earnings in Chandan Tika business, police stopping Young people earned the most money in the Kumbh Mela by applying sandalwood tilak. That's why the maximum number of youth have arrived at the Magh Mela. Deepak Mishra has come from Manda in Prayagraj itself. He says, 'There are good earnings in sandalwood tilak', but the administration is stopping it. They don't let us stand in one place. Some earn ₹ 500, some ₹ 1000, while others earn up to ₹ 2500 on main bathing days. Paramhans Tiwari has come from Saidabad in Prayagraj. He says - I came this year. Father used to do this work before; now I am doing it. There is profit. I come at 8 in the morning, then do the work of applying sandalwood-tilak. When my bag gets full, I take it and go back. Abhishek Upadhyay has come from Meja (UP) just to apply sandalwood, but he hasn't been able to earn yet. Youth riding bikes where vehicles are restricted Like the Kumbh Mela, vehicles are restricted in the Magh Mela area and surrounding areas on special bathing days. People can come and go by bike. Many youths preparing in the city have started the work of bringing and taking people on bikes at such times. Through this, they are earning more than ₹500 per day. However, the number of bikers is less this time compared to the Kumbh. But it is likely to increase in the coming days. A young man named Khesari has come from Gorakhpur to the fair. He is entertaining people by mimicking the voice of Bhojpuri film star Khesari Lal. Khesari's voice is so accurate that people are amazed after hearing it. Khesari can also mimic Pawan Singh's voice. Employment of 3 thousand crore rupees expected from the fair The Magh Mela will run for a total of 44 days. An estimated 15 crore people are expected to attend this fair. According to estimates, there is a possibility of a business worth ₹3 thousand crore. More than 5 lakh people are getting employment. This includes employment in tents, pandals, hotels, dharamshalas, travel operators, restaurants, dhabas, fruits and vegetables, flowers-garlands, worship materials, sweets and snacks, water and beverages, handicraft artisans, boatmen, and sandalwood-tikka vendors. According to the Confederation of All India Traders (CAIT), business worth ₹3 lakh crore was conducted during Mahakumbh-2025. CAIT Secretary General Khandelwal had said that a total of 66 crore people attended. More than 10 lakh people got employment.

stories.title: Man brings girlfriend from MP to UP to murder her:Kills her with pan over money, jewellery dispute; dumps body in fields, arrested after 21 days
stories.summary: A woman's body was found in Shankargarh near Prayagraj on December 27. There were deep wounds on her face and neck, and it was clear that she had been murdered. After 18 days, police discovered that the woman was from Madhya Pradesh. The brother-in-law with whom the woman was living in a live-in relationship had brutally murdered her. Most shocking was the weapon he chose for the murder. He used a roti cooking pan (tawa) to commit the murder, so that the woman wouldn't suspect anything. The brother-in-law remained hidden for 21 days after the murder, but finally police tracked him down. The motive behind this murder was 2 lakh rupees and jewelry worth about 4 lakh rupees, which he had acquired from the woman through emotional blackmail. Now the woman was asking for them back. The brother-in-law told police- Lalita was pressuring me that if her jewelry and money were not returned, she would go to the police. After this, the killer made a foolproof plan to execute the crime. He brought the woman living in Chakghat of MP to Dhavaiya village near Shankargadh at the UP border, 15 km away, under the pretext of going for a walk. Then, after killing her there, he dumped the body in a field and fled. He thought that since the woman was from MP, no one would be able to identify her here. However, when the police started connecting clues, they reached the killer after 21 days. Read the complete story from love story to murder... Body was found in bushes along the field This story began on December 27, 2025. When a blood-soaked body of a woman was found in Daroga Singh Bhadauria's field in Dhavaiya village of Shakargadh. The entire area was shocked. Looking at the woman's injuries, police understood it was a murder. The body wasn't too old, so police thought identification would happen quickly, but until January 13, no information about the woman could be found. No one contacted the police regarding the woman's identity. Shankargadh police put up posters with the woman's pictures in UP's Prayagraj and MP's Rewa and Satna. Police got their first clue in this murder case on January 14, when Ramadhar from Dabhaura in Madhya Pradesh's Rewa arrived at Shankargadh police station. Brother reached the police, said - This is my sister... At the police station, he said that the woman whose body was found in Dhavaiya village is my sister Lalita (42 years). I saw my sister's picture on the notice board of Chakghat police station in Rewa. He narrated the marriage story of his sister to the police. Said - Lalita was married 21 years ago to Kamlesh, who lived in Chakghat, Rewa. 3 years ago, Kamlesh died of a heart attack. Since then, Lalita started feeling lonely. Then her sister-in-law's husband, Dheeraj, became her support. He is a resident of Kudi Gouhani village in the Bara area. The brother also said that on December 26, 2025, his sister left home, saying she would return shortly, but never came back. Her mobile phone also got switched off. Inspector said - Dheeraj was the prime suspect This was a big clue for the police. Police tried to talk to Dheeraj, but his mobile was also found switched off. This deepened the suspicion. When the team reached his house, he wasn't there either. His wife was there, but she said that he had gone out for a few days for work. Where did he go? She said she doesn't know that either. Station in-charge Yashpal Singh said - After this, we became doubtful of Dheeraj. Three teams were activated with his details. We knew that the real story of Lalita's murder would only come out after finding Dheeraj. Police caught Dheeraj as soon as he came home A police team was also deployed in plain clothes near Dheeraj's house. On January 17, he reached his home. After this, the police surrounded the house and arrested Dheeraj. He was brought to the police station. Here, he was asked why he killed Lalita. Dheeraj started saying - I don't know about where Lalita is. After this, he was asked about living in a live-in relationship with Lalita. Mobile CDR (Call Detail Records) were shown, in which he was continuously talking to Lalita. He had also called Lalita on the night of December 26. After this, Lalita's mobile phone was switched off. Then he started telling the whole truth. He said - After the death of Lalita's husband Kamlesh, she received an accident compensation of 2 lakh rupees. Lalita started feeling lonely. Whenever I went, she would talk to me for hours and lighten her grief. This way slowly, we got into an affair. I was a plumbing contractor by profession. Often worked on large construction sites. I started taking Lalita with me, too. We lived together there, we were living life just like husband and wife. She was happy. Threatened, so plotted murder Gradually, Lalita started trusting me. Lalita had 2 lakh rupees in compensation in her account, which we spent on traveling and dining. I needed money, so I sold Lalita's mangalsutra and all her jewelry one by one. Everything went well for a few months, but then she started asking for her money and jewelry back. One day, when she got very angry, she threatened that if I didn't return her jewelry and money, she would go to the police. That day, I decided that I would kill Lalita. Now the story of the murder night on December 26... Attacked face and neck with iron griddle Dheeraj told police - On the evening of December 26, I told Lalita, let's go somewhere for a ride, we both went on a bike about 15km away to Dhavaiya village in Shankargarh. On the way, the village people were selling iron items at one place. From here, I bought a griddle. Didn't buy a sickle or sharp object, so that Lalita wouldn't feel that I want to kill her. Lalita asked - Why did you buy this? I said - The griddle at home has become old, so I bought another one. Then, while keeping Lalita engaged in conversation, I reached a deserted place. Stopped the bike, said that it seems to have broken down. Then she sat down in one place. As soon as I got the chance, I struck her head from behind with a griddle. When she fell to the ground, I kept striking her face and neck repeatedly until she stopped breathing. After this, I dragged the body to a field some distance away and dumped it. I also hid the griddle in the bushes and returned to my house. Since I was scared that the police might trace me, I started hiding here and there. I had told my family members that I got a big contract and would need to stay there for a few days. Shankargarh Police Station in-charge Inspector Yashpal Singh said- 20 days had passed since the woman's body was found. It seemed like solving this case had become a challenge. But through police efforts, we have reached the real killer. The accused brother-in-law has been arrested and is being sent to jail.

stories.title: Mauni Amavasya snan draws massive crowds to Triveni:3 crore expected at Magh Mela ghats; security tightened, traffic diversions enforced citywide
stories.summary: Today is Mauni Amavasya. It is estimated that 3 crore people will take a holy dip at the Magh Mela in Prayagraj. Special arrangements have been made at the ghats. Diversions have been implemented across the city. On January 17, one day before Mauni Amavasya, 1.5 crore people have already taken a bath at Triveni. Last year, during Mauni Amavasya, the Mahakumbh was going on. At that time, about 10 crore people took a holy dip at Triveni. A stampede incident also occurred. Therefore, security has been increased at the ghats this time. It is believed that taking a bath in silence on Mauni Amavasya fulfils one's wishes. Know the auspicious time of Mauni Amavasya This year, Mauni Amavasya will last from 11:52 PM on January 17 (Saturday) to 1:08 AM on January 18 (Sunday). According to the priests, since Amavasya tithi will remain throughout the day on January 18, devotees can take a holy dip in the Ganges at any time. Full benefits of bathing, charity and worship will be received during both special auspicious times and normal hours. Auspicious time for bathing Observing silence is penance On this new moon day, the Brahma, Padma and Vayu Puranas mention observing a vow of silence. According to these, observing silence along with worshipping Lord Vishnu and ancestors on the new moon day of Magha month brings great merit. In the Srimad Bhagavad Gita, silence is called penance. It is believed that observing silence on this date brings merit equal to penance. The vow of silence has been practised for ages to control one's desires. This vow improves mental health. It helps reduce depression, anxiety and stress. It also increases self-control and patience. Religious and Spiritual Importance of Holy Bath

stories.title: Accused in assault on Muslim students surrenders laughing, video surfaces:Reaches Bareilly court with companions amid loud sloganeering
stories.summary: Twenty days after Muslim students were beaten up at a café in Bareilly, the main accused evaded police and surrendered in court on Saturday. He reached the court comfortably and was seen laughing with his companions, showing no fear of police action, as captured in a video that has surfaced. While police had jailed his associates and were searching for him, he surrendered before the ACJM-5 court and was sent to 14 days of judicial custody. Pictures of the surrender 5 associates arrested, police searching for Rishabh Full case in detail Love Jihad allegations found false in police investigation As soon as information about the commotion in the cafe was received, Dial 112 and Premnagar police station personnel reached the spot. The police investigated the allegations made by Bajrang Dal activists, but all allegations turned out to be false. The student told the police - it was just a birthday party. No objectionable activity was taking place. After this, the police pacified the Bajrang Dal activists and brought the situation under control. The student had alleged that Bajrang Dal workers misbehaved with her. They falsely accused her of 'love jihad' and brutally beat her friends. Expelled from Bajrang Dal Meanwhile, Bajrang Dal's city convener, Kewala Nand Gaur, expelled the accused Rishabh Thakur from the organization on December 27, upon learning of the incident. He stated that they cannot keep a person in the organization who cannot follow its principles. In the future, if he does anything, Bajrang Dal will have nothing to do with it. Case registered against Bajrang Dal workers Restaurant owner Shailendra Gangwar also complained to Premnagar police station against Bajrang Dal workers. In the FIR, he stated that Rishabh Thakur and Deepak Pathak, along with 20–25 workers, entered the restaurant, raised slogans, assaulted people celebrating birthdays and the staff, and carried out vandalism inside the premises. Even while absconding, he remained active on social media After the video of the ruckus went viral and the matter gained national attention, the police initiated action. In this case, 6 accused, including a minor, had already been sent to jail. However, Rishabh Thakur was absconding. Surprisingly, despite being on the run, Rishabh was continuously active on social media. He was sharing his location and thoughts. Taking advantage of the police's 'slowness', he surrendered on Saturday at his convenience. Meanwhile, the police found in their investigation that Bajrang Dal activists took the law into their own hands and spread terror merely based on suspicion. Currently, the court has taken accused Rishabh Thakur into judicial custody.

stories.title: Couple found hanging from single noose in Jhansi:Suspected of performing symbolic marriage before act; interfaith relationship faced opposition
stories.summary: A young couple in Jhansi allegedly died by suicide after being unable to marry due to religious differences. The bodies of the 23-year-old man and his 18-year-old girlfriend were found hanging from a tree with the same rope in an animal enclosure. Police believe the couple performed symbolic marriage rituals before ending their lives. The incident took place in Patti Kumharra village under Chirgaon police station limits. Bodies found hanging from tree The incident came to light on Saturday morning. Villagers found the bodies of the couple hanging from a neem tree in an animal enclosure. Police, with the help of locals, brought the bodies down and sent them for post-mortem examination. Deceased identified The deceased were identified as Riyajul Khan (23), son of Raj Mohammad, and Muskan Pal (18). Both lived in Patti Kumharra village. Riyajul managed a DJ business, while Muskan had studied up to Class 8. Family learnt of relationship after death Muskan’s family said they were unaware of the relationship. Her uncle Sunil Pal said the family was busy preparing for her wedding. Muskan’s younger sister noticed she was missing around 3 am and began searching. During the search, family members found slippers and shoes under the neem tree in the enclosure. When they shone a torch, they saw both bodies hanging from the tree. Villagers and police informed Muskan’s uncle informed Riyajul’s family. Villagers gathered at the spot and later informed the police. The bodies were then taken down for post-mortem. Riyajul’s elder brother Qadir Khan said Riyajul had been working as a DJ for four years. He usually slept in the garage where his DJ equipment was parked. On Friday, Riyajul had returned home after attending a cricket match and a condolence ritual. Police statement Chirgaon police station in-charge Rahul Rathore said the couple were in a relationship and were distressed after Muskan’s marriage was fixed. Police are awaiting post-mortem reports, but preliminary investigation points to suicide. Childhood friends turned lovers Police said Riyajul and Muskan were neighbours and studied in the same school during childhood. Their friendship turned into a romantic relationship around two years ago. However, they were unable to marry due to their different religions. Girl’s marriage fixed elsewhere Muskan’s family had fixed her marriage in Paras village of Tahrauli. The engagement took place about eight months ago. On Friday, the wedding date of 30 April 2026 was finalised. Police said this deeply upset both Muskan and Riyajul. Last meeting on Friday night On Friday night, Riyajul and Muskan met in the animal enclosure near Riyajul’s garage. Police believe they tied a rope to the tree and hanged themselves together. Signs of marriage rituals When police recovered the bodies, Muskan’s hair parting was filled with vermilion, and she was wearing toe rings. This led police to believe the couple symbolically performed marriage rituals before dying.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:PM accuses TMC of registering infiltrators as voters; CM Yogi blames Congress for Manikarnika ghat row more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest updates from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. PM accuses TMC of registering infiltrators as voters Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday accused the Trinamool Congress (TMC) government in West Bengal of being “cruel” and alleged that funds sent by the Centre were being misused by the ruling party. Addressing a public gathering in Malda, Modi said TMC leaders had become “enemies of the poor” by denying them the benefits of central welfare schemes. 2. Ahilyabai statue row: AI-generated video, Congress behind conspiracy—CM Yogi In Kashi, CM Yogi Adityanath on Saturday blamed the Congress for the controversy over the alleged damage to Queen Ahilyabai’s statue at Manikarnika Ghat. He said the statue is completely safe and claimed Congress circulated an AI-generated video showing it broken to defame Kashi. Calling it a conspiracy, Yogi said he visited personally to expose it, adding that work at the ghat has been halted. 3. Meerut murder case: lawyer reveals Paras–Ruby love story New details have emerged in the Meerut Sunita murder case, with accused Paras Som’s lawyer claiming Paras and Ruby were in love and wanted to marry, but fled from home. Paras, currently in jail, denies killing his mother. On January 15, his lawyer and uncle met him in district jail and discussed the sequence of events for over an hour. 4. Trump threatens countries regarding Greenland President Donald Trump has openly threatened to annex Greenland into the United States. According to the BBC, Trump threatened to impose tariffs on countries that did not support his plan to annex Greenland. Trump made the statement during a meeting at the White House on Friday. 5. Bajaj finance manager found dead in Lucknow’s Hyatt Regency A senior Bajaj Finance manager, Mohammad Fahimuddin (47) from Thane, Maharashtra, was found unconscious in his room at Hyatt Regency Lucknow on Friday morning and later declared dead at a government hospital. He had flown in from Mumbai for an official meeting. Police said liquor bottles were found in the room. 6. 4 friends from UP survive snowstorm after 36-hour ordeal Four friends from Uttar Pradesh survived a deadly snowstorm after their car fell into a valley amid minus 25°C temperatures. Stranded for 36 hours, they tried shouting, honking, and banging utensils for help. On January 12, a helicopter passed overhead, but failed to spot them despite their signals. They were later rescued by police. 7. Toll plazas to go cashless from April 1: Payments will be accepted only via FASTag or UPI From April 1, toll plazas across the country will become completely cashless. Once the new rules come into effect, vehicle owners will be able to pay toll charges only through FASTag or UPI, with cash payments being discontinued. This was announced by V. Umashankar, Secretary, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, during an interview with TV news channel Aaj Tak. 8. Worst fog of season in UP: 40 vehicles collide, 5 dead Uttar Pradesh witnessed the densest fog of the season on Saturday, with near-zero visibility in 53 districts, including Lucknow and Kanpur. Around 40 vehicles collided, killing five people, including an 18-month-old girl. Over 100 trains were delayed, road, rail and air traffic were disrupted, and schools were closed in nine cities. 9. Brijbhushan Singh prepares for Faizabad poll battle Former MP and strongman Brijbhushan Sharan Singh has begun preparations to contest the next Lok Sabha election from Ayodhya’s Faizabad seat. With Vinay Katiyar already active, speculation is rife over whether BJP will give Brijbhushan a ticket. Political circles are also discussing his future role after passing on his legacy to his son. 10. B Praak receives death threat demanding ₹10 crore ransom Popular singer B Praak received a serious death threat from someone claiming to be connected to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. stories.title: 'Google Golden Baba' grabs attention at Magh Mela:Wears crown worth ₹5cr; calls CM Yogi an incarnation of Hanuman
stories.summary: This year’s Magh Mela has become a platform for many unique sadhus, saints and kalpvasis. While some have drawn attention due to unusual attire and others because of distinctive spiritual practices, one figure has emerged as a major attraction - Google Golden Baba, whose real name is Swami Shri Manojanand Maharaj. Golden Baba is known for his extravagant appearance, as he is adorned with gold and silver jewellery from head to toe. His striking look has made him one of the most talked-about saints at the Magh Mela. First know about Google Golden Baba... Gold and Silver From Head to Toe Golden Baba eats and drinks using silver utensils. His hands are decorated with gold bracelets and chains, and all ten fingers wear gold rings engraved with images of gods and goddesses. Around his neck, he wears gold and silver Shankar pendants, along with rudraksha malas studded with gold. On his head, Baba wears a heavy silver crown, which has a picture of Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath embedded in it. According to Baba, he wears around five kilograms of gold, collectively worth approximately ₹5 crore. He also always carries a pure gold idol of ‘Laddu Gopal’, which he believes is the source of his spiritual protection. Swami Manojanand Maharaj, a resident of Kanpur, has been living this lifestyle for nearly 20 years and has been attending the Magh Mela continuously for the past eight years. ‘Strict Vow’ for CM Yogi Golden Baba is not only in the headlines for his wealth, but also for his unwavering devotion to CM Yogi Adityanath. He describes himself as a “huge admirer” of the Chief Minister and has taken a strict vow related to him. Baba has pledged to remain barefoot until Yogi Adityanath becomes the Prime Minister of India. Earlier, he used to wear silver slippers worth ₹5 lakh, but after taking this vow, he completely gave up footwear. The silver crown he wears prominently displays Yogi Adityanath’s photograph, symbolising his devotion. Golden Baba is currently staying at his camp in Sector-2 of the Magh Mela area. Faith Over Ash When asked why he wears gold instead of ash like many saints, Baba explained that this is simply his personal hobby. He compared it to other hobbies people have, saying there is nothing spiritual or symbolic attached to it beyond personal preference. Asked about the exact quantity of gold he wears, Baba said he does not measure it, adding that such details can be found “on Google”. Devotion to Yogi Adityanath Golden Baba explained that his devotion to CM Yogi stems from the Chief Minister’s work during the Covid-19 pandemic, when he personally visited villages to distribute medicines while many leaders stayed indoors. He credited Yogi Adityanath for governance during the Ram Mandir Pran Pratishtha in Ayodhya, claiming that Lord Ram’s return symbolised a “saintly rule”. Baba even described Yogi as an incarnation of Hanuman, stating that Ram’s arrival followed Hanuman’s presence. Why Baba wears gold Explaining the reason behind his golden attire, Baba said that wearing gold is not a religious vow but a personal choice and tradition. He described himself as a Kshatriya, stating that historically, Kshatriyas have had an affinity for weapons and gold. Referring to the Mahabharata era, he said that warriors like Karna also wore gold ornaments, and he sees this as a way to honour and continue Kshatriya traditions, without pride or arrogance. No security, only faith Despite wearing valuables worth crores, Golden Baba does not use any security. He said he believes God is his ultimate protector. He revealed that there have been four attack attempts on him in the past, but he escaped unharmed due to his faith and devotion. Authorities offered him security twice, but he declined. According to Baba, divine signs always guide and protect him. Reason behind name ‘Google Golden Baba’ Explaining his unique title, Baba smiled and said that anyone who searches for him on Google will immediately find him, which led people to call him “Google Golden Baba”. With his golden appearance, strong beliefs and bold declarations, Google Golden Baba has once again become one of the most talked-about figures at this year’s Magh Mela.

stories.title: Clashes erupt at Lucknow University over Rohit Vemula march:BAPSA, ABVP face off after slogan row; police detain students to restore order
stories.summary: Tension gripped Lucknow University on Saturday after student groups clashed during marches held in memory of Rohit Vemula. What began as slogan shouting soon turned into physical fights, forcing heavy police intervention and leading to detentions and complaints from rival student organisations. Memorial march sparks tension Students of the Birsa Ambedkar Phule Student Association (BAPSA) took out a march on the university campus to mark Rohit Vemula’s death anniversary. They gathered near the Ambedkar statue and raised slogans demanding justice and an end to harassment of students. Police were already present to maintain security. See 3 pictures - Argument over slogans turns violent During the march, a debate broke out between BAPSA students and another group over slogan shouting. Within minutes, loud slogans were raised from both sides, creating a tense atmosphere. Soon, BAPSA members and ABVP workers came face to face, and the argument turned into a physical clash. Police struggle to control clash The fight escalated quickly. Police had to work hard to separate the two groups and calm the situation. For some time, officers appeared overwhelmed as students continued sloganeering and pushing each other inside the campus. Slogans raised during protest BAPSA students shouted slogans such as, “Rohit, we are ashamed, your killers are alive.” They said strict action should be taken to prevent similar incidents in future and to ensure students are not harassed. BAPSA alleges attack by ABVP Later, BAPSA issued a written statement. It said that a peaceful “Rohit Smriti Yatra” began around noon but was allegedly attacked by ABVP and RSS workers. The group claimed students were assaulted and one student suffered serious injuries. Despite this, the march ended with slogans of Jai Bhim. Complaint filed by ABVP-linked scholar On the other hand, ABVP-linked research scholar Radheshyam Pandey filed a complaint at Hasanganj police station. He alleged that BAPSA workers attacked him while he was heading towards the university’s administrative building. He said the march was held without permission and involved a deadly assault. Allegations over objectionable slogans According to the complaint, slogans referring to Brahmanism, Thakurism and opportunism were raised. Pandey claimed he was targeted because of his association with ABVP and his caste. Police said vehicles were stopped during the clash and others nearby were also injured. Police probe and named accused Police confirmed that a case is being examined based on the complaint. Allegations have been made against BAPSA president Shikhar Das, Ram Sharan, Ravi and around 20 others. The investigation is ongoing. Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha march halted Separately, the Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha also organised a memorial march for Rohit Vemula. Police tried to stop the students to prevent further unrest. This led to fresh tension between students and police on campus. Students detained by police Police dragged several students into buses and detained them. This action angered students and caused chaos for some time. Academic activities in the university were also disrupted during the unrest. Samajwadi student wing’s allegation Atul Kumar Shukla, secretary of the Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha, alleged that the government was acting against Dalit interests. He claimed students were peacefully marching but police from four stations were called in to forcibly stop and detain them. Students raise democratic concerns Student leaders said they wanted a better academic environment and resolution of student issues. They accused the government of violating democratic rights by stopping peaceful protests. Heavy security deployed After the clashes, police increased security across and around the campus. The administration said forces remain deployed to prevent further trouble. Officials confirmed that the situation is now under control.

stories.title: Famous Bollywood actor Pradeep Kabra reaches Varanasi:Seen in simple attire; sits on ghat steps barefoot; writes, 'I am lost somewhere'
stories.summary: Actor Pradeep Kabra, known for his powerful negative roles in Bollywood films, arrived in Kashi. During this time, he made an emotional video at the Ganga Ghat, which is going viral rapidly on social media. In the video, Pradeep Kabra is saying that I have lost something. When asked what is lost, he smilingly replies that my mind is lost somewhere. After this, the video shows beautiful glimpses of Kashi's Ganga ghats. During this time, he appeared in simple attire. He also sat on the ghat steps without slippers or shoes. During this time, no tourist was able to recognise him. First see 2 pictures.. Harsha Richariya, who became famous from Mahakumbh, commented During this journey, Pradeep Kabra presented himself as a regular tourist. He explored the streets of Banaras and closely experienced the culture and spiritual atmosphere here. Along with this, he also performed darshan and worship at major temples. There have been many reactions on social media to this video of Pradeep Kabra, in which Harsha Richaria, who became famous from Mahakumbh, also replied to the video writing, "Deep Message". Seen touring the Ganga ghats of Varanasi Actor Pradeep, sharing a video from Hanuman Ghat in Varanasi, said - There can be many ways to live life, but the right way is one that gives satisfaction to oneself without causing pain to others. During this time, he was seen touring the Ganga ghats of Varanasi. Also news of Harishchandra Ghat, for the past two days he has been sharing videos of different Ganga ghats of Varanasi. Tourists are passing by him at the Ganga ghat, but they are unable to recognize him. Dressed like a regular tourist, he can be seen enjoying Kashi. Salman Khan's film gave recognition Pradeep Kabra is among those artists who have created their special identity in Bollywood by mostly playing negative characters. He got his real recognition from the negative role played in Salman Khan's film 'Wanted'. After this, he appeared as villains and goons in big films like 'Bang Bang', 'Dilwale', 'Suryavanshi' and 'Simmba'. Acted in South and Rajasthani Films Pradeep Kabra entered Bollywood in 2004 with the film 'Run' starring Abhishek Bachchan and Bhumika Chawla. After this, he worked in popular films like 'Delhi Belly', 'Bang Bang!' and Shah Rukh Khan's film 'Dilwale'. His acting was not limited to Hindi cinema. He has also appeared in Tamil superstar Rajinikanth's film 'Darbar'. Additionally, Pradeep Kabra played an important role in the Rajasthani film 'Taawdo: The Sunlight', which was praised at several film festivals. This video that emerged during his Kashi visit shows that behind the screen image of a dangerous villain lies an artist who is sensitive and in search of peace.
