stories.title: Female teacher found dead in Barabanki school:Body found hanging in Headmaster’s office; husband alleges harassment
stories.summary: The body of a female teacher was found hanging in the headmaster’s office of a government school in Barabanki district on Saturday. The incident has sent shockwaves through the local education community, with the victim’s husband accusing the school headmaster of harassment. The incident occurred at the Composite School in Udhwapur village, under the jurisdiction of Satrik police station. The deceased has been identified as Uma Verma, also known as Mala (40), a resident of the Jalalpur locality in Barabanki city. See two images related to the incident... Sequence of Events at the School According to information, Uma Verma’s husband, Rishi—who is also a teacher posted at a school in Sidhaur block—dropped her at the school on Friday morning before leaving for his own workplace. After arriving, Uma reportedly kept her bag in her classroom and then went to the headmaster’s office. When she did not return for a long time, fellow teachers became concerned and called out to her. Receiving no response, they opened the office door and found her body hanging from a noose inside. Police and Forensic Investigation The school staff immediately informed the police. Officers from Satrik police station arrived at the scene, and a forensic team was called in to examine the site and collect evidence. The body was taken into police custody and sent for post-mortem examination. Allegations and Ongoing Probe Uma Verma is survived by her husband and their two children. Her husband has alleged that she was being harassed by the headmaster, though police have not yet confirmed these claims. Police officials stated that the matter is being investigated from all angles. The exact cause of death will be determined after the forensic analysis and post-mortem report. Meanwhile, statements from family members and school staff are being recorded as part of the ongoing investigation. The news is being continuously updated...

stories.title: Video of Ahilyabai’s broken statue AI-generated- Yogi:UP CM calls it conspiracy of Congress, says queen’s statue safe; work halted at Manikarnika Ghat
stories.summary: In Kashi, Chief Minister Yogi on Saturday blamed the Congress over the controversy surrounding the alleged damage to Queen Ahilyabai’s statue at Manikarnika Ghat. He said the queen’s statue has been kept safe. The Congress created a video showing the statue broken using AI. He called it a conspiracy to defame Kashi, which is why he had to come here personally. He said the conspiracy must be exposed. The Chief Minister said claims that temples have been demolished are completely false. He said Ahilyabai Holkar’s statue has been properly preserved. Once the renovation work is completed, the statue will appear in a new form. He alleged that the Congress is misleading the public by spreading AI-generated videos of temple demolition, calling it a criminal act. The Chief Minister said the Congress never respected Ahilyabai. He said the comments made by its leaders deserve laughter and pity. He compared it to a cat going on a pilgrimage after eating a hundred mice. He warned those creating images using AI, saying this will not be accepted under any circumstances. The controversy began on January 10, when the Holkar Trust of Indore claimed that the statue of Devi Ahilyabai Holkar at Manikarnika Ghat had been broken. It also alleged that several religious symbols were damaged and some statues were broken and buried under debris. After this, some images surfaced. At that time, the Varanasi District Magistrate described them as AI-generated. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Priyanka Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav had also held the BJP responsible for the issue. At present, new construction work at Manikarnika Ghat has been halted. Meanwhile, the district administration and BJP leaders have denied allegations of any temple demolition. They have stated that an idol mounted on a wall was carefully removed and preserved, and it will be reinstalled with due respect once the ghat construction work is completed. Nothing is hidden from you… The Chief Minister said, “Whenever worship takes place at Kashi Vishwanath, the cremation grounds are also discussed, whether it is Manikarnika Ghat or Harishchandra Ghat. Even today, if you go to Manikarnika Ghat, you will see the conditions in which last rites are performed. How can it be acceptable that someone is unable to give their loved one a dignified farewell? For this, a programme is being launched. It is not being funded by government money, but through CSR funds of a company, made possible by the efforts of the Prime Minister. Even then, the same people have started their complaints again. What is happening at present is not hidden from you.” Congress did not honour Ahilyabai Holkar The Chief Minister said Aurangzeb had demolished the Baba Vishwanath temple. The first effort to rebuild the temple was made by Ahilyabai Holkar. Congress did not honour her, but Prime Minister Modi did. However, for the last three to four days, some people have been misleading the public by circulating false pictures. These are the same people who did not take these heritage sites forward during their time, but even now they refuse to stop. They make irresponsible statements and even comment on boatmen. Before 2014, their steamers ran on diesel and kerosene. Now CNG has been introduced and their income has increased. To divert attention from all this, as soon as new work begins, these people start spreading misleading propaganda. See few pics of dismantling of parts of Manikarnika Ghats

stories.title: Woman thief bites off ₹4.5 lakh chain in Jhansi:Incident caught on CCTV at Bhagwat Katha, 4 women lose jewellery amid stage crowd chaos
stories.summary: A female thief cut a chain worth 4.5 lakhs with her teeth in Jhansi. During the Bhagwat Katha, as soon as there was pushing near the stage, the female thief approached the retired inspector's wife. She surrounded them with her friend. One placed her hand on the woman's shoulder. The other pressed her mouth to the neck and stole the chain by cutting it with her teeth. The incident was executed in just 10 seconds. During this time, BJP MLA Ravi Sharma had also come to listen to the katha. The incident occurred in Ayodhyapuri Colony of Sipri Bazar police station area on January 14, but the video emerged today. The two female thieves have not been identified yet. See 3 pictures of the woman's chain theft- Ayodhyapuri Colony resident Dayashankar Vyas said, 'I am a retired inspector. My wife, Gyan Devi, is a member of the Satsang Sunderkand Committee. A Bhagwat Katha is being organized in the colony. My wife used to go daily to listen to the katha. On January 14, BJP MLA Ravi Sharma and his wife were going to honor my wife. Wife came to the katha with daughter-in-law and children. Here, fruits, flowers, and toys were being distributed from the stage during Krishna's birth celebration. Many women reached the stage of receiving these. This led to pushing and shoving. At that time, two female thieves surrounded my wife and snatched her chain.' One placed hand on shoulder, other committed theft Dayashankar further said, 'One female thief put her hand on my wife's shoulder, and the other woman cut and stole the gold chain with her teeth. Both disappeared with the chain. Later, when the daughter-in-law and son saw, then we came to know. The chain was 35 grams. Its value is approximately Rs 4.5 lakhs.' That day, four women's chains were stolen. There was no police arrangement on the day of the incident, but the police were deployed after the MLA's reprimand. We have submitted an application to the police station demanding action. Both female thieves can be seen in the video.'

stories.title: Man reaches police station after killing wife in Kanpur:Confesses by saying, 'Sir, I strangled her body is wrapped in blanket'
stories.summary: A shocking incident has emerged from Kanpur, where a 22-year-old man allegedly strangled his wife just four months after their love marriage. After the crime, the accused walked into a police station and confessed. Accused surrenders at police station On Saturday morning around 10 am, Sachin Singh arrived at Maharajpur police station and surrendered. Speaking to the inspector, he reportedly said, Sir, I strangled my wife. Her body is wrapped in a blanket at home. His confession caused immediate commotion at the police station, following which officers took him into custody. Stayed on the run for four hours According to police officials, Sachin appeared distressed and tearful while confessing. During questioning, he revealed that after killing his wife, he wandered around for nearly four hours. He initially attempted to flee but later decided to surrender to the police. See 3 photos... Crime scene and recovery of body Sachin told the police that he lived in a rented room above Muskan Hospital in New Hitech City, Ruma. Police teams, along with the accused, reached the location where they found the woman’s body wrapped in a blanket and placed on a cot inside the room. Investigation underway The police took possession of the body and sent it for post-mortem examination. A forensic team was also called to the spot to collect evidence. Further investigation is underway to ascertain the motive behind the murder and the circumstances leading up to the incident.

stories.title: Doctors not found in 45 Agra hospitals:License suspended, paramedical staff and fire safety equipment found lacking during verification
stories.summary: The Health Department has taken a strict stance on the negligence of medical standards related to patient safety in Agra. License renewals have been suspended for 45 private hospitals due to deficiencies found in essential standards such as deployment of specialist doctors in ICU, trained paramedical staff, medical waste management, and fire safety. Hospital operators have been issued notices with instructions to rectify the shortcomings within a week. A total of 1317 medical institutions are registered with the Health Department. These include 537 hospitals, 513 clinics, 149 pathology labs, and 108 diagnostic centers. The department is renewing licenses based on physical verification of institutions according to 17 prescribed medical standards. During inspection, 45 hospitals were found to have incomplete standards, while complaints of negligence in treatment have also emerged against 27 hospitals. During physical verification, the health department team found several serious deficiencies. Many hospitals did not have specialist doctors deployed in ICUs for 24 hours. There was also a shortage of trained paramedical staff. Life-saving equipment was found incomplete, and fire safety equipment was non-functional at many places. Some hospitals did not even have a fire NOC. Negligence was also found in medical waste management. Biomedical waste was not being collected and disposed of according to standards. Additionally, CCTV cameras were not installed at the doctors' chambers and entrance gates. Information boards at many hospitals did not display details like doctors' names, fee details, affidavits of serving physicians, and records of admitted and discharged patients. Playing with Patients' lives Health department officials say that ignoring medical standards directly puts patients' lives at risk. The presence of a specialist in the ICU is mandatory 24 hours. Due to the absence of specialist doctors for surgeries other than cesarean, serious patients often lose their lives. Without systems like CCTV, it becomes difficult to identify the responsible doctor. CMO's Statement CMO Dr. Arun Srivastava said that medical standards were found incomplete in 45 hospitals. Affidavits of doctors providing services in these hospitals were also not found. Notices have been issued to fulfill necessary standards, including ICU, medical waste management, and other requirements. Verification will be done again after the fixed time. If facilities are not found complete, licenses of the concerned hospitals will be suspended. IMA's Position IMA President Dr. Pankaj Nagaich said that the organization has directed all its members to mandatorily fulfill medical standards in hospitals. A meeting has also been held with health department officials on this issue. Most of the hospitals that do not meet the standards are run by non-medical operators. This information has also been given to the CMO.

stories.title: From Charan Singh’s protégé to Samajwadi founder leader:Mulayam’s journey shows ambition, risk-taking and survival skills in decades of shifting alliances and power struggles
stories.summary: The soil of Uttar Pradesh has produced not just crops, but also iron-willed leaders. One such name is Mulayam Singh Yadav. His father's teaching was - 'If you can't fly, then run, if you can't run, then walk, if you can't walk, then crawl, but don't stop.' Mulayam did politics this way. He rose from opposing Congress, but joined hands with them several times when needed. He fought against the Ram Mandir movement, then later stood with its leader, Kalyan Singh. He emerged from Chaudhary Charan Singh's legacy, but became Chief Minister by opposing his son Ajit Singh. In Dainik Bhaskar's series Political Arena, the story of a leader who was called 'Little Napoleon'. Who remained the flag bearer of experimentalism in politics and stayed relevant in every era due to political maneuvering... Year 1980, Saifai village of Etawah The Congress flag had already waved at Jaswantnagar's political gathering. Mulayam Singh had lost the election. Congress's Balram Singh Yadav had defeated him. Mulayam had already gone to the assembly three times from this seat. This was the reason they were quite disappointed with this defeat and were sitting with some colleagues in the election office. He suddenly got up and said, "See you tomorrow." A colleague said, "What's done is done. Sit for a while, then everyone will leave." Mulayam didn't say anything, just got up and left. He reached home and went straight to his room and lay down on the cot. His only sister, Kamla, saw him coming but didn't say anything. Everyone at home was sad. Khichdi was made for dinner. After a while, Kamla went to Mulayam's room with food. There were tears in Mulayam's eyes. Standing at the door of the room, Kamla spoke up- "Is life over?" Mulayam said with a choked voice- "Chaudhary Sahab had so much faith in me... Hope he doesn't break down from this defeat." Kamla said, "Something good must be written. Don't try to win just Jaswantnagar, try to win the country. You'll win here automatically." Mulayam Singh’s political rise gained momentum when Chaudhary Charan Singh appointed him state president of the Lok Dal, a moment that filled his family with joy. At the same time, Congress made VP Singh the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, where the fear of dacoits was widespread. VP Singh launched aggressive police encounters to project a tough image, but Mulayam opposed this approach, arguing that Dalits and backward classes were being harassed in the name of law and order. Mulayam raised the issue with Charan Singh and later mobilised leaders like George Fernandes and Karpoori Thakur to build opposition against VP Singh’s policies. The movement created strong anti-Congress sentiment among backward classes, forcing VP Singh to resign and strengthening Mulayam’s image in UP. National politics soon shifted dramatically with Indira Gandhi’s assassination, the anti-Sikh riots, and Rajiv Gandhi becoming Prime Minister. Though VP Singh joined Rajiv’s cabinet as Finance Minister, the Bofors controversy split the Congress, bringing former rivals VP Singh and Mulayam together. On October 11, 1988, several socialist parties merged to form the Janata Dal. VP Singh became the National president, while Mulayam emerged as UP president. With simultaneous national and state elections approaching, Mulayam had become the key political force in UP and the most influential backward-class leader after Charan Singh’s death. One day, Rajiv Gandhi called the then Congress state president, Balram Singh Yadav, to Delhi. Rajiv said, "Mulayam Singh must be stopped by any means." Balram said, "When I had defeated him, I didn't expect he would become so big." Rajiv Gandhi- "What should be the strategy? If we don't stop him, we will lose." Balram Yadav- "His hold among the backwards has increased. Ajit Singh is still inexperienced, and Mulayam is taking Charan Singh's place. We will have to play the backward card." As per the decision taken in the meeting, to counter Mulayam Singh Yadav, the 'Yadav Trio' - Balram Yadav, Chandrajeet Yadav, and Ramnaresh Yadav were fielded. Chandrajeet was close to Indira and Sanjay Gandhi. Ramnaresh Yadav was UP CM during the Janata Party time. He had joined Janata Dal but was unhappy with Mulayam Singh becoming the state president, and came to Congress. Still, Congress's strategy didn't work. A slogan started echoing across the state- "Thakur's wisdom, Ahir's strength, this is what Janata Dal is named." Mulayam's stature grew even more. Congress faced heavy defeats in both the UP Assembly and the Lok Sabha. VP Singh became PM, but he had a grudge against Mulayam. He didn't want Mulayam to become CM. He wanted to make Ajit Singh, son of former Prime Minister Chaudhary Charan Singh, the CM. December, 1989. Tilak Hall, Lucknow. A meeting of Janata Dal MLAs was underway. The name for CM was to be finalized. Inside and outside the hall, supporters of Ajit and Mulayam were raising slogans. Then Mulayam stood up and said - "Be quiet..." The sloganeering increased - "Name is Mulayam, work is like steel." Mulayam said again - "Listen to me. Be quiet. There will be opportunities for slogans." The sloganeering stopped. Two observers from Delhi, Madhu Dandavate and Surendra Mohan, were also present there. Madhu had a slip in his pocket, on which VP Singh had endorsed Ajit Singh for CM. Madhu stood up and put his hand in his pocket. Mulayam became suspicious. He also stood up and said loudly- "Wait, wait..." Whispers started in the hall. Mulayam said, "Don't take out the slip. You have come here to conduct fair elections. Just do that." When the election happened, most MLAs supported Mulayam Singh. This is how Mulayam Singh Yadav became the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh for the first time. January 1, 1990 The Lucknow bench of the Allahabad High Court ordered mapping photography and a structural survey of the disputed land in Ayodhya. Both the Center and State had Janata Dal governments. BJP was supporting both governments from outside. Despite this, through the Ram Janmabhoomi movement, they had made life difficult for the government. The country's politics were changing. Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP), Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), and BJP started raising the Ram temple issue at every corner and intersection. Mulayam Singh was worried. He went to Delhi to meet VP Singh - "Prime Minister, BJP people are fueling communal politics. The mosque siege could begin anytime. Why don't you talk to them?" VP Singh didn't give much reaction. Just said - "Okay, I will talk." August 7, 1990 Prime Minister VP Singh implemented the Mandal Commission recommendations. 27% reservation was provided for backward classes. Mulayam held a meeting with his people in the state. Someone said- "VP Singh will become the god of backwards. We will be left behind." Mulayam said, "Nothing will happen. I have a move." Everyone fell silent. Everyone knew Netaji would make such a move that would destroy everyone's plans. Mulayam said, "We will implement reservation at the panchayat level." Mulayam became the first chief minister in the country to do this. This further strengthened Mulayam's image among backward castes. Meanwhile, the BJP was restless. The Mandal move had turned everything upside down. A large part of the country started mobilizing towards the opposition. On the other hand, violent fires against the reservation erupted across the country. August 8, 1990, Patna A Janata Dal rally was underway. Mulayam Singh Yadav was accompanied by Lalu Yadav and Sharad Yadav. After securing the backwards, now it was time to win the trust of minorities. Mulayam Singh thundered- "If one Muslim's life is threatened, a hundred Yadavs will be ready to give their lives." BJP became restless. The whole country was stuck in the politics of 'Mandal and Kamandal'. On August 13, BJP President LK Advani held a meeting with Muslim leaders. He proposed, "If Muslims withdraw their claim from Ram Janmabhoomi, we won't press our demands for Mathura and Varanasi." Muslim leaders rejected this offer. Advani started the Rath Yatra from Somnath Temple, Gujarat, on September 25, 1990. The Rath Yatra was receiving tremendous support. Mulayam held another meeting with his associates - "The atmosphere is building in BJP's favor. Muslims are scared. Muslim leaders are pressuring me to do something." Someone said, "If the chariot reaches Ayodhya, something terrible will happen." Mulayam - "What if I don't let the chariot enter UP?" Silence fell in the meeting. One person said - "How will this happen...?" Mulayam said, "I will arrest Advani." And the meeting ended with this decision. VP knew that if Mulayam stopped the Rath Yatra, minorities would also stand behind him. Backward castes were already in Mulayam's favor. To counter this, VP called Bihar CM Lalu Yadav and said- "Stop the Rath Yatra in Bihar. Arrest Advani." Lalu Yadav got Advani arrested in Samastipur, Bihar, on October 23. Sporadic violence occurred in many places. Curfew was also imposed in areas around Ayodhya. Mulayam also got many VHP leaders arrested. Mulayam Singh began to be portrayed as a villain across the country. BJP pressured VP Singh to make Mulayam release VHP leaders. VP Singh sent his close associate, Farrukhabad MP Santosh Bharatiya, to Lucknow to convince Mulayam. Mulayam Singh became angry. He said in an angry tone, "I cannot release them." Santosh was expecting such a response. He threatened Mulayam - "If you don't release them, the BJP will withdraw support. The government will fall." Mulayam said, "I am not worried about that." October 28, 1990 National and international media were in Lucknow. Time magazine's journalist Robert Nickelsberg asked Mulayam, "What will you do to save the mosque?" Mulayam said, "Whether the government survives or not, the mosque will fall only over my dead body." The journalist fired a second question- "Is Ram not a matter of faith for you?" Mulayam replied- "I believe in the Ram who considers everyone equal. I believe in the Ram that Gandhi believed in." Just then, another journalist said, "Advani is coming to Ayodhya." Mulayam smiled and said, "He has never come to Ayodhya till today. Why has he suddenly developed a love for Ayodhya? If he comes, we'll see." October 30, 1990 There were about 10 barricades along the 126-kilometer route on the Lucknow-Faizabad Road. Early in the morning, crowds of thousands of kar sevaks were moving towards the Babri Masjid. Seeing the huge crowd, security forces started sweating. Phones started ringing in Mulayam Singh's office- "The crowd is growing. The situation is getting out of control." In no time, some kar sevaks climbed the mosque's dome and started waving saffron flags. It was afternoon. Suddenly, the police opened fire. Within moments, the field filled with thousands of people emptied, but the scene ahead was horrific. Blood splattered everywhere... A similar scene appeared again on November 2. According to government figures, 16 kar sevaks were killed in police firing over two days. As a result, the BJP withdrew support. VP Singh's government at the center fell. Socialist leader Chandra Shekhar broke away from the Janata Dal and formed the Samajwadi Janata Party with 64 MPs. Mulayam Singh Yadav joined him and remained Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister with Congress support, even though he had earlier opposed the Congress. When Congress withdrew support, both the central and UP governments fell, leading to fresh elections. During this period, the BJP rose sharply by pushing the Ram temple issue, damaging Mulayam’s image and branding him as anti-Hindu. Even in his home district, Etawah, public sentiment turned against him. In the 1991 elections, the BJP won 221 seats and formed the government in UP under Kalyan Singh. Facing political isolation and declining influence, Mulayam realised the need to rebuild his base independently. His faith in Chandra Shekhar weakened, and in October 1992, he announced the formation of the Samajwadi Party in Lucknow. Soon after, the Babri Masjid demolition triggered riots across UP. The Kalyan Singh government was dismissed, President’s Rule was imposed, and mid-term elections were announced. In this changing political climate, BSP leader Kanshi Ram described Mulayam as secular and pro-Dalit. For the 1993 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the Samajwadi Party (SP) and BSP formed an alliance and came to power. However, the alliance broke in 1995, leading to the fall of the government. Mulayam Singh Yadav then shifted his focus to national politics and won the 1996 Lok Sabha election from Mainpuri. At the Centre, non-Congress and non-BJP parties formed the United Front, of which SP was a part. Mulayam was a strong contender for the Prime Minister’s post, but internal opposition from leaders like Lalu Yadav and Sharad Yadav blocked his rise. During this period, Mulayam grew close to Amar Singh, who became his key political strategist. Amar Singh advised Mulayam to broaden his social base and keep channels open with the Congress. Their partnership strengthened SP, and Amar Singh rose quickly within the party. In 2002, SP emerged as the largest party in the UP Assembly with 143 seats but lacked a majority. Through Amar Singh’s political negotiations, Congress extended outside support, and several BSP MLAs backed SP. Even former rival Kalyan Singh supported Mulayam. With this support, Mulayam Singh Yadav became Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh for the third time. Year 2007-08 As allegations grew against Mulayam Singh Yadav, the Samajwadi Party began losing backward class votes to the BSP and faced criticism as a party of strongmen. Mulayam sought advice from Amar Singh, who warned that SP was losing support among backward classes, Muslims, and farmers, and suggested making a bold political move. Mulayam then met Kalyan Singh, a former BJP leader sidelined by his party. They decided to work together to counter the BJP in Uttar Pradesh. However, this alliance proved costly. Muslims grew angry, the Congress attacked SP, and Mayawati called the move a betrayal of secularism. The strategy backfired badly in the 2007 elections, leading to SP’s defeat. After the loss, Mulayam publicly admitted that allying with a leader linked to the Babri Masjid demolition was a serious mistake and apologised to his party. Despite criticism and failed experiments, Mulayam remained a central figure in Indian politics. He served three times as UP Chief Minister, once as Defence Minister, was elected MP seven times and MLA ten times, and came close to becoming Prime Minister twice. *** Reference Creative liberty has been used to make the story interesting.

stories.title: 4 friends from UP survive deadly snowstorm:Car fell into valley, minus 25°C cold, 36-hour survival fight ended with cops rescue; read their sagacious story
stories.summary: -25 °C temperature...there was snow everywhere. No one else was visible there except us. We called out, honked the car horn, banged utensils, shouted and screamed, but there was no one there to hear us. On January 12th, during daytime, a helicopter passed over us. We showed a red cloth, waved our hands, and even called out, but the people in the helicopter didn't see us. This is what Shivam Chaudhary, who returned from Leh, has to say. Due to Google Maps, 4 friends from Agra who lost their way fought a 36-hour battle for survival in the snowfall. The last 3 hours of this were particularly terrifying. They say that at one point, it felt like they wouldn't survive. Tears were flowing from their eyes as they remembered their families. After much struggle, they managed to return home alive. Dainik Bhaskar spoke with Shivam Chaudhary and Yash Mittal. Learned about their story of 2 nights and 3 days spent in terror. Read the report... Car slipped in snow, fell 20 feet down into valley Four friends met at Shivam’s house and left for Leh by car on January 9. After staying in Pang on January 10, they headed towards Manali on January 11. Near Nakila, around 2:30 am, the car skidded on the snow and fell about 20 feet into a valley. With no help in sight, they spent the night inside the car using the heater to survive the freezing cold. Even after daylight, no one was visible nearby, and extreme cold forced them back into the car. They remained trapped for nearly 36 hours. Eventually, the diesel ran out, the heater stopped, there was no food, phones shut down, and all four began to suffer serious effects of the cold. Then we decided that instead of staying here, it's better to fight for life. Because if we remain stuck here, survival would be difficult. Due to the blocked road, no one would come here, nor would anyone hear our voice. Then we planned that we had no choice but to walk on foot. After walking 20 km, around 12:30 PM on January 13, we saw an abandoned factory near Whiskey Nala. We spent the night there. We were inside when we heard some people outside. When we looked outside, we found that they were police officers who had arrived there searching for us. Now it felt like our lives would be saved. Seeing them brought tears to our eyes. It felt like God had sent angels to help us. We hugged them and started crying. Shivam explained - The closed factory where we stayed was a little off the road. There was a signboard outside. We wrote 'Help Us' on it. After this, we came into the factory and tried to protect ourselves from the cold. Sudhanshu was unwell, so he had gone to sleep. Seeing our message on the roadside signboard, Neuma police station officers arrived at the scene in the afternoon. As soon as we heard the jeep's sound, I, Jayveer and Yash ran outside. Our hearts were overwhelmed seeing the police officers in front of us. Tears welled up in our eyes. Had video call with family, then lost contact The families of all four reached Leh searching for them. Yash, Shivam and Sudhansu arrived in Agra on Thursday night, while Jayveer arrived on Friday evening. Their car is still in Leh. It couldn't come due to road blockage. After reaching Ladakh, Shivam and his friends got a new mobile number. Then they stayed continuously connected with family, and conversations continued. On January 9, everyone was at Pangong Lake in Leh. From there, they also talked to home via video call. Since then, their contact was lost. Family members tried to contact the same number many times but could not get through. Worried, the family filed a missing person complaint at Sadar Police Station on January 11. Car location found through satellite Shivam Chaudhary, Jayveer Singh, Yash Mittal and Sudhanshu Fojdar went from Agra to Gulmarg. From there, they reached Pangong Lake via Sonamarg. On January 9th, around 5:30 PM, all four made a video call to show their families the scenery there. After this, contact with them was lost. Shivam's father, Daulatram, says - We all got worried when there was no information for 2 days. I contacted the local police as well as the local MP and other public representatives. After that, help was sought from the Defence and Home Ministries. The army also became active upon receiving the information. The youth's vehicle was located via satellite. The vehicle was in Pang, about 125 kilometres from Leh, near the Manali route. Then the army and police reached these young men. Now know what happened between January 9 to 13... January 9: At 5 PM, all four youths talked to their families. After this, they left for Leh. There, they saw the Manali board near Kharu. They started walking on that route. January 10: Stopped at Pang itself. January 11: Left for Manali. The road ahead was closed. After going ahead from Sarchu, we had to return. Near Nakila, around 2:30 at night, the car slipped on the snow and got stuck in a 20-foot deep ditch. Spent the night in the car with the heater on amidst the snow. January 12: The next day was also spent relying on the heater. After the car's diesel ran out, the heater - our only support - also stopped working. Then planned to walk on foot. January 13: At around 12:30 in the afternoon, after walking about 20 kilometres, reached a closed factory near Whisky Nala. Spent the entire night there. Meanwhile, Ladakh Police also reached there while searching for them. Everyone was rescued and brought back to Leh.

stories.title: Worst fog of the season in UP, 40 vehicles collide:5 dead, including an 18-month-old girl, 100 trains delayed; schools closed in 9 cities
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh is reeling under a double spell of severe cold and cold wave conditions, with the state witnessing the densest fog of the season on Saturday. Dense fog was reported from 53 districts, including Lucknow and Kanpur, since morning, reducing visibility to near zero at several places. The fog severely disrupted road, rail, and air traffic across the state. In many areas, visibility dropped to such low levels that commuters struggled to see even a few metres ahead. Icy winds added to the chill, forcing people travelling in vehicles to cover their hands and faces, while bonfires were seen across residential areas. According to official data, Azamgarh, Kanpur, Ayodhya, and Hardoi were the coldest districts in the past 24 hours, recording a minimum temperature of 4 degrees Celsius. In view of the prevailing cold wave, district administrations in Noida, Greater Noida, Saharanpur, Badaun, and Sambhal have ordered the closure of schools up to Class 8. Train services were hit hard, with over 50 trains on the Gorakhpur–Lucknow–Prayagraj route running late by one to ten hours. Even premium services, including Vande Bharat and Shatabdi Express trains, failed to maintain schedules. Flight operations were also affected, with passengers reporting long delays at airports. The India Meteorological Department said snowfall in the higher reaches has led to a sharp drop in temperatures across Uttar Pradesh. Most districts are currently under a ‘cold day’ alert, and cold wave conditions are likely to continue for the next four to five days. Now the weather pictures- Why did the weather take a sudden turn? According to the India Meteorological Department, a powerful jet stream is currently active over west–north India, leading to a sharp change in weather conditions across Uttar Pradesh. Meteorologists said jet stream winds — fast-flowing air currents that move like a river in the upper atmosphere are blowing at a speed of around 232 kmph at an altitude of 12.6 km above mean sea level. The impact of these high-speed winds is being felt at lower levels, resulting in intensified cold conditions, dense fog, and strong surface winds in the plains, including UP. In addition, recent snowfall in the higher reaches has further strengthened cold northerly winds, pushing temperatures down across the state. Weather outlook for the next two days January 18: Light rain or drizzle is likely at isolated places in western Uttar Pradesh. Cold winds are expected to continue, increasing the chill factor across most districts. January 19: Drizzle may persist in parts of western UP, while cloud cover is likely to increase over several districts in eastern UP. Cold winds will remain active, keeping day temperatures low. The Meteorological Department has warned that cold day conditions may continue in many districts over the next few days.

stories.title: Meerut murder case reveals Paras and Ruby love story:Lawyer says, 'couple wanted marriage, fled home, while accused insists he did not kill mother'
stories.summary: The truth of Paras-Ruby's love story has come to light in the Meerut Sunita murder case. Paras Som, accused of Sunita's murder, is in jail. On January 15, Paras's lawyer went to meet him in the district jail with his uncle. For 1 hour, they discussed the entire sequence of events with Paras alone around 3 points. First- How did the love story with Ruby begin, and why did it come to running away? Second- If they were running away from home, how did Sunita die? Third- If Ruby loves him, why is she giving statements against Paras now? After returning from the district jail, Dainik Bhaskar team understood the complete love story from Paras's lawyer, Balram Som. Read the report... Read the conversation from the jail meeting room... We studied together in school; she was in 12th, and I was a 9th-grade student Paras was introduced to the lawyer in the district jail's meeting room. The lawyer asked - When did you first meet Ruby? Recalling, Paras explained, Ruby and I both studied at the village's Janta Inter College. We first saw each other in college. Since we were in the same school, we would often run into each other. Once I was going to drink water, Ruby was coming from the front. She smiled when she saw me, so I smiled back. She was studying in 12th grade, and I was a 9th-grade student. There was nothing like love at that time. Normal conversations would happen, I would ask about her studies, and she would talk about me. After leaving school, we started talking on mobile The lawyer asked - Then when did love happen? Paras started narrating the story further - We were from the same village, studying in the same school. My house was also just 1km away from her house. That's why we started meeting while coming and going in the village. About 3 years ago, we met at a village wedding. Ruby was also there. We both smiled at each other. From that day, a new story of our friendship began. We would meet daily at school and talk. Our conversations kept growing, and we didn't even realize when we started liking each other. We met daily at school. Spent a lot of time together. Had lunch together too. All the kids at our school would often tease us. They all knew that our friendship was of a different type. That's when we decided that we would stay together for life. Ruby is older than me. After passing 12th grade, she went to college for graduation. After leaving school, we started having difficulty meeting. But we would talk on the phone. Ruby also had a mobile phone. Sometimes she would call me, sometimes I would call her. We have sent many messages to each other. I have saved those messages too. When needed, I will show those messages in court. We would talk for long hours on the phone. Paras said - Ruby was troubled by the marriage being fixed In 2024, our families found out about our affair. Not just them... the whole village came to know about it. Then there was a fight between our families. Ruby's family said about me that I had misled their daughter. My family was angry, and they took away my mobile. It became difficult for us to meet. Then I would often talk to Ruby from my mother's phone. Sometimes we would also talk through friends' phones. But then Ruby would be the one calling me. Then one day, I found out that Ruby's family had arranged her marriage; she was very worried while talking on the phone. She said that she would only marry me and did not want to marry anyone else. Ruby told her family - I won't marry anywhere else I learned from my friends that Ruby had told her parents that she would not marry anyone except me. Her family members were quite angry about this. They said that wherever we go, you will have to marry there. Ruby said that if they force her to marry, she will run away from home. She had told me on the phone that my family won't let me marry you, so we will have to run away from home. She used to send me love letters, too Ruby has written me many letters. When we couldn't talk on mobile, Ruby would send me letters with help from two village friends. Both those girls knew me, too. This way, we started communicating through letters as well. Through those letters, we would sometimes meet up. I still want to marry Ruby Lawyer Balram told us - After reaching jail, Paras would keep asking about Ruby in between telling his story. We told him that Ruby was not feeling well. Then he asked if we could arrange a conversation with his Ruby. Then we told him that it was not possible to arrange the conversation. He told the lawyer - I still want to marry Ruby today. If possible, please arrange my marriage with Ruby. Because when we were coming back home, Ruby had said that her family members won't leave me now. I will be kept as a hostage in the house, and later will be forcefully married. Paras told his lawyer, Balram Som - I have kept many records of conversations between Ruby and me. I have saved those messages and chats. Which will reveal our truth in front of the court. He also said that he has some photos of him and Ruby together, in which they are together. Paras's mobile was taken away after compromise in the panchayat The lawyer also says that Paras did not have a mobile for the last 3 months. In 2024, after the dispute between Paras-Ruby's families was settled in a compromise a few days later, Paras's family members took away his mobile phone. Due to not having a phone, Paras was unable to communicate with Ruby. Then Paras would secretly talk to Ruby from his mother's phone. Ruby would also call Paras. These details will also be included in their case. What happened on the day of murder? Paras said - I did not kill her mother When the lawyer asked Paras what happened on the day of the murder? Then Paras couldn't say much. He only said that I did not commit the murder... I am innocent. He also said that I did not kidnap Ruby. Ruby came with me on her own will. Ruby had also planned the escape. I had thought about where we would go, what we would do. I hadn't thought so much would happen. Ruby had said that her family was arranging her marriage somewhere else, which she didn't want to do, so let's run away from home. Paras said - After running away from Kapsad, we jumped into a canal (small channel). My shoe got washed away in the water. I became barefoot. Then Ruby gave me her shoes. She said - You wear these. She kept walking barefoot with me. Then, moving ahead, we took a lift from a truck driver. Sitting in that truck, we reached Saharanpur. That truck driver gave a slipper, which Ruby wore. When Ruby and I were caught, Paras was still wearing Ruby's shoes. After running away from Meerut, we didn't stay anywhere for long; we just kept moving around while traveling by train, so that the police couldn't trace us. Paras said - I don't understand why she is lying The lawyer said that Paras is not in a condition to reveal much right now. He is stressed and sad. He kept saying that Ruby cannot lie. We both love each other very much. We have had a relationship for 3 years. We want to live together. Paras is unable to tell much about the murder and murder weapon. Right now, Paras is also anxious and troubled. Now we will gradually arrange his meetings with his family members. When he becomes normal, we will get more information from him, and evidence related to Ruby-Paras's conversations and relationship will also be found.

stories.title: Bajaj Finance manager found dead at Hyatt Regency in Lucknow:Had flown in from Mumbai for meeting, alcohol bottles found in room
stories.summary: A senior manager of Bajaj Finance was found unconscious in his hotel room at a five-star hotel in Lucknow on Friday morning and later declared dead at a government hospital, police said. The deceased has been identified as Mohammad Fahimuddin (47), a resident of Thane district in Maharashtra. He had travelled from Mumbai to Lucknow to attend an official meeting and was staying at Hyatt Regency Lucknow. Colleagues raised alarm after calls went unanswered According to police, Fahimuddin was scheduled to attend a meeting with the Bajaj Finance team on Friday morning. Around 8 am, his colleagues tried calling him several times, but there was no response. When the calls remained unanswered till around 9.30 am, a few team members went to the hotel and informed the reception that Fahimuddin was not responding. Door locked from inside, staff alerted reception Hotel staff sent a service worker to check the room. The door was locked from inside and did not open despite repeated knocks. The worker then looked through a side window and saw Fahimuddin lying unconscious on the bed. The matter was immediately reported to the hotel reception. The door was opened using a master key in the presence of staff. Police said his pulse was still present at the time. He was taken to Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Institute of Medical Sciences in a 108 ambulance, where doctors declared him dead. The body has been kept in the hospital mortuary for post-mortem. Alcohol bottles, cigarette packets found in room ACP Vinay Dwivedi said alcohol bottles and several cigarette packets were recovered from the hotel room. “Prima facie, his health condition appears to have deteriorated due to excessive consumption of alcohol and smoking. Other angles are also being investigated,” the officer said. Police said the post-mortem examination will be conducted after the arrival of the deceased’s wife, who has left Mumbai for Lucknow. Further action will be taken based on the post-mortem report.

stories.title: Brijbhushan Singh prepares to contest election from Faizabad:Vinay Katiyar already active; will BJP give ticket to Bahubali?
stories.summary: After Rashtra Katha in Gonda, these two questions are being discussed in UP's political corridors. Former MP from Kaiserganj and strongman Brijbhushan Singh has started preparations to contest elections. Meanwhile, BJP's firebrand leader Vinay Katiyar has become active in Ayodhya after a long time. In a special conversation with Bhaskar, Katiyar said, " We will contest assembly elections first, then Lok Sabha elections. In such a situation, will the BJP hand over the Ayodhya seat, considered a symbol of Hindutva and nationalism, to Brijbhushan Sharan Singh? To know the answers to all these questions, read... The case of sexual harassment of women wrestlers is still ongoing BJP did not give a ticket in 2024 to Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, who was a six-time MP from Gonda, Balrampur and Kaiserganj, and was accused of sexual harassment of women wrestlers. In his place, his younger son Karan Bhushan Sharan Singh was fielded in the election from Kaiserganj. Karan Bhushan is currently an MP from Kaiserganj. In the sexual harassment case, Brij Bhushan has been acquitted under the POCSO Act section, but the sexual harassment case is still under consideration. Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh organised a grand Rashtrakatha in his Nandani Niketanam this month. Many personalities from the political, film, sports and social world participated in Rashtrakatha. Brij Bhushan recently gave an emotional statement- There was a conspiracy against me, I was removed as part of a plot. If I remain alive till 2029, I will definitely go to Parliament once with full respect. Brij Bhushan Singh's MP son Karan Bhushan announced that in 2029, both he and his father will go to Parliament. Supporting this, Brij Bhushan said - 'Both will contest Lok Sabha elections, if BJP gives a ticket, then good, otherwise will contest from somewhere else.' After this statement by Brij Bhushan, discussions have started in political corridors that Brij Bhushan will field his son Karan Bhushan from his Kaiserganj seat, while he himself will contest from the Faizabad seat. Want to know why Brij Bhushan wants Faizabad seat? Even after the construction of the grand temple at Sri Ram Janmabhoomi and the Pran Pratishtha ceremony, BJP's Lallu Singh lost the election from Faizabad in 2024. This is why Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh is looking for political possibilities there. He and his close associates believe that the BJP will be looking for a strong alternative to Lallu Singh in 2029. In such a situation, Brij Bhushan could become the party's choice. Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh studied at Saket College in Ayodhya. He also served as the general secretary of the student union in the college. However, he went across the Saryu to Gonda to contest the assembly and Lok Sabha elections. Hoardings put up in Ayodhya during Rashtrakatha During the Rashtrakatha, Brij Bhushan and his supporters put up a large number of hoardings and banners in Ayodhya. His supporters also privately believe that if given the opportunity, Netaji could try his luck from the Faizabad Lok Sabha seat. Brij Bhushan himself has said that, keeping in mind the insistence of supporters, he may contest the election. Vinay Katiyar big challenge before Brij Bhushan Political analysts believe that in Ayodhya, bigger than Lallu Singh, BJP's fiery leader Vinay Katiyar is the major obstacle in Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh's path. After meeting with BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary, Katiyar has openly declared that Faizabad is his seat and he will contest from that seat only. Faizabad, Ambedkar Nagar and nearby seats have a large number of Kurmi voters. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP did not get the Kurmi vote, resulting in defeats in Ayodhya and surrounding seats. Learning from 2024, the BJP has devised a strategy to cultivate the Kurmi vote bank for 2027 and then 2029. Vinay Katiyar's active involvement in politics is also part of that strategy. If Vinay Katiyar announces his candidature for the Lok Sabha elections, it will be difficult for Brijbhushan to get a chance from Ayodhya due to caste equations. In terms of caste equations, handing over Faizabad to Brijbhushan will not be beneficial for the BJP. Brij Bhushan is playing pressure politics Political analysts believe that Brij Bhushan and his son have adopted a pressure strategy by announcing their intention to contest elections in 2029. After Gonda MP Kirtiwardhan Singh became a minister at the centre, his political stature and influence in the region have become greater than Brij Bhushan's. Meanwhile, he also has an ongoing political rivalry with CM Yogi Adityanath. In such a situation, to ensure there are no obstacles for his family's politics in 2027 and 2029, he is creating pressure through statements from now itself. So, whether he gets a new seat or not, at least the current legacy remains intact. Take a look at the political history of Faizabad After independence, Congress started its winning streak in Faizabad in the 1957 general elections. So far, 17 Lok Sabha elections have been held on the Faizabad seat, out of which Congress has won 7 times. SP won four times, while BJP won five times, and CPI won once. In this way, after the Emergency, no single political party has dominated Faizabad. The people of Faizabad have chosen their MP according to the time, circumstances and caste equations. Senior journalist Triyug Narayan Tiwari believes that Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh has an old connection with Faizabad. He studied at Saket College and started student politics from there. He learned wrestling at Hanumangarhi. His and his supporters' gestures indicate that Brij Bhushan wants to contest the upcoming Lok Sabha elections from Faizabad. He is also quite active among the saints and sages here, participating in religious programs and supporting them. But the Ayodhya ticket is decided by the RSS. RSS would want its own cadre to contest the election. In such a situation, it will be difficult for Brijbhushan to get a ticket from Ayodhya. Due to PDA, SP will also not consider it appropriate to cut Awadesh Prasad's ticket and give it to Brijbhushan. Moreover, it will be difficult for Brijbhushan to win by contesting as an independent.

stories.title: Fresh currency notes sold openly on Kanpur roads:Bank staff accused of diverting wedding season cash bundles to black market for huge profits
stories.summary: 'A bundle of 100 fresh (new) 10 rupee notes will cost 1370 rupees... 20 rupee bundle is more expensive... it will cost 2480 rupees... 100 notes of 1 rupee bundle costs 2700 rupees... need 10 lakhs... need 5 lakhs... just make the payment... will give right now... You won't get new note bundles in the bank... bank officers deliver here... we buy from them by paying extra money...' The fresh notes that you should get from banks are being sold on UP roads after going black from the bank. The centre point is Kanpur's Ghantaghar area. Here, a bundle of 100 fresh 1-rupee notes is being sold for 2,700 rupees. This means for 1 US dollar, you will get only 3 fresh 1 rupee notes and 35 paise, while the dollar is worth 90 rupees. Similarly, fresh notes of 5, 10, and 20 rupees are being sold with extra charges. Actually, the wedding season has begun. In such a situation, the demand for crisp notes for the groom's garlands and other rituals has increased. When common people go to banks for fresh notes, they don't get them. Bank staff turn them away, saying there are no new notes. While the RBI (Reserve Bank of India) has strict orders that banks cannot refuse if fresh notes are available. How did fresh notes from RBI to banks end up being sold in the market? To find the answer to this question, Dainik Bhaskar's team conducted an investigation in Kanpur. Read the full revelation... Are there fresh notes in the market? Our investigation started with this question. We reached Shastri Nagar in Kanpur. Here, fresh notes are strung into garlands and sold. We met Ruby. She told us that if we take bundles of fresh notes from her, an extra charge of Rs 500 will be taken, because she also buys fresh notes at higher prices from shops in the Ghanta Ghar area. Reporter: Want to get a garland of notes made...? Ruby: Which one... 10 rupee or 20 rupee...? Reporter: How much will it cost for 10 rupee notes...? Ruby: Will you provide the bundle of notes... or do we need to arrange from our side...? Reporter: Tell me both options... Ruby: One garland uses 500 rupees worth of 10 rupee notes... how many notes do you want to use...? Reporter: Let's say... if we use a bundle of 1000 rupees (100 new notes) of 10 rupee notes then...? Ruby: If you provide the bundle, we'll charge 300 rupees for making it... Reporter: How much will it cost for two bundles...? Ruby: Then the total will be 1800 rupees... Reporter: Meaning... why so much... bundle of 1000 rupees... and 300 rupees charge... that's 1300 rupees... then why 1800 rupees...? Ruby: 500 rupees will be charged for fresh notes... Ruby's statement made it clear that an extra charge is taken in the name of fresh notes. Now we needed to find out where these new notes were being sold. To get this answer, we continued the conversation. They bring bundles of fresh notes bought in black market Reporter: Where do you get bundles of new notes from...? Ruby: We buy them in black market... Reporter: Where do you get bundles of new notes from...? Ruby: They are sold at Ghanta Ghar... we buy from there... Reporter: If we go there to buy, how much would it cost...? Ruby: You go there and find out... how much it costs... Reporter: Still, how much will it cost...? Ruby: The rates there change daily... rates change immediately... Reporter: Oh... there's no fixed rate there...? Ruby: No... there's no fixed rate... From here, we learned that bundles of fresh notes are being sold in black in Kanpur's Ghantaghar area. The rates keep changing here daily. Now let's go to the fresh notes market and understand the black marketing... After this, we reached Ghantaghar. There were shops along the road. Most shops had no names. The shops only had written, torn, old notes exchanged here. We reached Anil Brothers. Here we met the shopkeeper Vijay. Vijay said that bank employees come and sell us bundles of fresh notes, we add our percentage and sell them to you. Reporter: Uncle... we are wedding planners... need bundles of new notes... Vijay: Yes, you people must need it... You'll get it... Reporter: How much will one bundle of 10 rupee notes (100 notes) cost...? Vijay: The 10 rupee one... will cost you 1370 rupees... Reporter: How much will the 20 rupee one cost...? Vijay: The 20 rupee one is more expensive... will cost 2480 rupees (100 notes of 20 rupees). Reporter: Will I get a bundle of 1 rupee notes...? Vijay: Yes... You'll get everything here... Reporter: How much will a bundle of old 1 rupee notes (100 notes) cost...? Vijay: 1 rupee bundle... you'll get it for 1400 rupees (100 notes of 1 rupee)... and 5 rupee bundle will cost 1300 rupees (100 notes of 5 rupees)... Reporter: Will I also get bundles of 100 rupees and 50 rupees...? Vijay: 100 rupee bundle... you'll get it by paying 120 rupees extra... 50 rupee bundle will cost 5170 rupees (100 notes of 50 rupees)... From Vijay's words, it became clear that this market has all kinds of fresh notes. Just need to pay an extra price for all of them. Now we wanted to know how many fresh notes are here? How do they come here? When we talked to Vijay for the answer, he told us that you can get as many as you want. Bank employees themselves come and give them. 10 lakhs... 5 lakhs... you can get as many fresh notes as you want Vijay: Rates go up and down daily... less-more... Reporter: But we need it in bulk... meaning we need more... Vijay: How much more do you need... need 10 lakhs... need 5 lakhs... you'll get it now... just count the payment... Reporter: Actually... we went to the bank... submitted applications too... but they said... it's not available now... Vijay: You won't get bundles in the bank... You can get bundles of 100 rupees in the bank... Reporter: We went to the bank and got very troubled... but didn't get it... they said - will give when it comes... Vijay: They'll give when it comes... here commission will be charged... everything will be available... those b@$#@#$ give everything here... all bank officials give it here... no outsider gives it... when we are buying from bank people here by paying them more money, why would they give it to you...? The shopkeeper Vijay's words exposed their collusion with bank officials. Now we wanted to know how much bank officials earn in this black mailing? When we continued the conversation with Vijay, he said - Bank officials also earn good money. He also said that online transactions don't work here, all transactions are done in cash. Bank officials charge 3500 rupees extra for 1000 fresh notes Reporter: How much will bank officials get for 1 bundle (100 new notes)...? Vijay: If bank officials give you a bundle of fresh notes (10 bundles), they won't get anything... here they get Rs 350 for 1 bundle of 100 notes, meaning they get Rs 3500 extra for 1 bundle (10 bundles = 1000 new notes)... so why would they give it to you...? Reporter: Is this why they don't give it to us...? Vijay: Bank officials don't give it to customers... they all bring it here... Reporter: Well... Do you need to be informed in advance, or will it be available immediately...? Vijay: Will get it immediately... Tell me now... What all do you need... Will give right now... What will we do with so many notes... Reporter: We take wedding contracts... Client demands.... Vijay: Then what's the problem... Take 50 thousand extra from them... Everything will be arranged... Reporter: Okay... Will you accept online payment...? Vijay: Cash payment works here... Online doesn't work here... Reporter: It's used in garlands too, right...? Vijay: Garland... Jaymala... Notes are used in everything... Show the money... You'll get all the goods... Whatever you want... You'll get it... Vijay's words made it clear that there is no shortage of fresh notes in the market. Now we wanted to know which is the most expensive fresh note? In response, Vijay showed us a 1-rupee note. Said- these 100 notes will cost 2700 rupees. Old bundle of 1 rupee costs 1500 rupees, new bundle will cost 2700 rupees Reporter: For 1 rupee... will you get a bundle of old notes... or new notes...? Vijay: Both are available... old note bundle costs 1500 rupees... new note bundle costs 2700 rupees... Reporter: Hey... 2700 rupees... it will only have 100 notes in it, right...? Vijay: Yes... It will only have 100 notes... Reporter: Okay... now new ones won't be coming, right...? Vijay: The bank has no stock... clerks and officers keep everything at their homes... Reporter: Oh... bank clerks keep it at home...? Vijay: All officers keep it at their homes... when they're getting the money, why would they give it to anyone else...? Vijay claims that bank officers keep fresh notes at their homes instead of in banks. They are bringing these to the market and selling them. Now let's go to the bank, are fresh notes available here or not? After leaving the fresh notes market, we reached the bank. We wanted to know if fresh notes were available here or not. We reached HDFC Bank in Kalyanpur, Kanpur. Here we told the bank employee that there's a wedding at home and we need fresh notes. To this, the cashier said - Fresh notes are not available immediately. Come after January 14th with the wedding card and application. If bundles are available, we will give them. You won't get too many. We will try to give you one bundle. Meanwhile, when the Bhaskar team went to the State Bank of India Swaroop Nagar branch and demanded bundles of crisp notes, the bank employee said, go to your home branch and talk about it there. If bundles are available at the branch, you will get them. Banks are giving fresh notes, will take action if bank employees are selling notes in market Kanpur Lead Bank Manager Aditya Chandra said - So far, no such complaint has been received where bank employees were found selling fresh notes in the market. If such a case comes up, action will be taken against the bank employee. If customers demand fresh notes while withdrawing large amounts for weddings, bundles of new notes are provided. It depends on the rapport between the customer and the bank on how many fresh notes they receive.

stories.title: Assembly speakers meet in Lucknow for discussion:Om Birla says law-making is losing time and asks members to work faster and stay focused
stories.summary: The fourth conference of presiding officers is taking place in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. Many top political leaders are attending, including Governor Anandiben Patel, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, and Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman Harivansh. Prime Minister Narendra Modi sent a message for the event, which was read out during the conference. During the conference, Uttar Pradesh Assembly Speaker Satish Mahana, while delivering the inaugural address, highly praised Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla. Mahana said, "Om Birla has created a new identity in the world with his parliamentary innovations." He reminded that this conference was held in Uttar Pradesh in 2015, and at his request, Om Birla has given UP this opportunity once again 'out of turn'. Mahana also praised Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, who has completely changed the image of the state. He said, "Politics had been given a negative perception. It was believed that one who knows nothing becomes a leader, but now that perception has changed. Only one who knows everything becomes a leader." Parliamentary democracy is the most correct method of democracy Addressing the conference, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla said that the land of UP is the land of political consciousness. It is the largest state in the world, its population is more than the population of many countries in the world. Presiding officers from different states have come to this conference, whose responsibility is to enhance the dignity of the legislature. We should leave here with new energy, and the prestige and dignity of our democratic institutions should increase. The conference held in 2015 deliberated on making the assembly paperless, the use of IT, and ensuring that information about institutions reaches the public. Today, when we are holding this conference again, the outcome of that deliberation has been implemented everywhere. We face many challenges in maintaining public trust and authenticity, and this responsibility lies with the presiding officers as well as the public representatives. When we are elected, the public expects us to present their problems and needs in the house. The voice of an individual should reach the government, and whatever reaches the government should yield results. From this perspective, our institution works to make laws and deliberates on policies. We are the world's largest democracy. We have shown the world that parliamentary democracy is the most correct method of democracy. In this assembly, public representatives continuously discussed the vision of a developed India for 28 hours. Through such deliberation, we form shared policies. Consensus and dissent are the strengths of democracy; only when everyone's opinion comes forward can we establish a democratic system. We have introduced many innovations to increase public trust in democratic institutions. We formed parliamentary standing committees, made proceedings live, created rules and procedures, discussed with presiding officers of states within the framework of the constitution, and made changes while respecting the sanctity of the constitution. Our endeavor is to increase public trust in the legislature. Our work culture has been democratic. We will strive to incorporate everyone's suggestions and implement the best practices of the assembly. It is also the responsibility of the presiding officer to ensure everyone gets an opportunity if democracy is to be strengthened, the house must function. The longer the house functions, the better the discussions will be. In this very house, there have been discussions on sustainable development goals for a continuous 36 hours. It is in the house that the problems of the entire state, the voice of the people, and their opinions are heard. When we sit in the presiding officer's chair, we should treat everyone equally because the country watches us. Through this conference, we will make ourselves stronger and more accountable. The Governor said, if solutions are hindered, problems increase Addressing the conference, Governor Anandiben Patel said that this conference will give a new direction to legislative conduct. There should be no conflict here; our common goal is to strengthen constitutional institutions. Democracy has its own challenges important issues cannot be discussed due to disruptions, and when solutions are obstructed, problems increase. Legislative bodies are also playing a new role in society along with their traditional work. MLAs do not get a chance to speak for four or five days. When the Lok Sabha Speaker himself says that the House should run for more days, I hope that the House will run for more days. Deliberations will be held on strengthening the legislature Mahana emphasized the role of the Constitution, stating that it has fixed the accountability of the legislature. Today, doctors, engineers, retired IAS-IPS officers, and various professionals are present as members in the House. In the three-day session, there will be an in-depth discussion on strengthening the legislature, along with accountability towards the public and responsibilities towards the country and society. He expressed confidence that its echo, emanating from Uttar Pradesh, would reach all state assemblies of the country. Prime Minister Narendra Modi's message was a major attraction at the conference. Satish Mahana read it out, in which the PM emphasized the strengthening of democracy and the role of the legislature. Additionally, a short film based on the development of Uttar Pradesh was also screened. The film stated that under the leadership of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, the state has made unprecedented progress in every sector over the past nine years. UP has now become the 'growth engine' of the country's development, where significant progress has been made in investment, infrastructure, and social development. It is the government's duty to adhere to constitutional decorum Leader of Opposition Mata Prasad Pandey also addressed the conference. He said that the Uttar Pradesh Assembly and the state have given many Prime Ministers to the country. This conference is an important platform for the introspection of Indian democracy. Pandey emphasized, "How can the journey from the platform of power to the temple of the people be made better? Democracy is not just about forming a government. It is the duty of the government to adhere to constitutional decorum. It is an institution of wisdom, not opposition." He reminded that the Constitution is greater than power and the people are supreme. Appealing to the presiding officers, he said that only when the ruling party and the opposition are viewed equally, does the House become a true temple of democracy. Pandey questioned the executive, stating that the House is run for fewer days than it should be. He urged that the sessions of the House be extended according to the rules, so that issues related to the public can be adequately discussed. He specifically appealed to Om Birla to deliberate on this matter at the conference. Need for innovation in legislature in line with changing times Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman Harivansh, in his address, described the conference as a platform for lively dialogue among presiding officers. He praised Om Birla's efforts, due to which conferences of parliamentary committees are being held regularly. Harivansh highlighted the contributions of Satish Mahana, whom he had the opportunity to know for the past few years. He said, "Mahana has innovated. The capacity building of members is done by communicating with them in different groups. The vision document was discussed and the rules of the assembly have been prepared." Emphasizing the need for innovation in the legislature in line with changing times, Harivansh said that Uttar Pradesh is continuously progressing under the guidance of Prime Minister Modi and the leadership of Yogi Adityanath. Once considered a 'problem state', UP is now on the path of development. He proudly stated that this assembly has given four Bharat Ratnas to the country.

stories.title: Protests erupt at Manikarnika Ghat over Ahilyabai Holkar statue damage:Police officer’s uniform torn; baton charge to disperse crowd; 17–18 taken into custody
stories.summary: Members of the Pal community gathered at Manikarnika Ghat on Monday following reports that a statue of Ahilyabai Holkar had been damaged. The protest escalated into a confrontation when police attempted to disperse the demonstrators, leading to a brief scuffle in which a police uniform was torn. Police later resorted to a baton charge to restore order. As many as 17–18 protesters were detained and taken to a police station, while cases have been registered against 18 people, officials said. Members of the Pal community said they wanted to assess the extent of the alleged damage at the ghat, describing the incident as an affront to the State and the country. Separately, police registered FIRs against eight individuals for allegedly circulating misleading posts and photographs related to Manikarnika Ghat on social media. Those named include Aam Aadmi Party Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh, Congress leader Pappu Yadav, and others. The administration has directed the accused to appear before the police within 72 hours to record their statements. Earlier in the day, members of the Pal community also raised slogans outside the Ahilyabai Holkar temple, demanding enhanced security for the temple and other heritage structures. First see the pictures... In a related development, FIRs were registered against eight people for allegedly circulating misleading content on social media. Those named include Aam Aadmi Party Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh, Congress leader Pappu Yadav, and others. Police said some of the accused were also booked for allegedly using artificial intelligence tools to spread misinformation on social media platforms. All the accused have been directed to appear before the police within 72 hours to record their statements, failing which coercive action may follow. Meanwhile, Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav took a swipe at the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party, saying that BJP leaders would dismiss even visual evidence by claiming it was generated using artificial intelligence. The police said they were closely monitoring social media platforms and warned that strict action would be taken against those spreading rumours or provocative content that could disturb public order.

stories.title: Former IPS Amitabh Thakur gets bail:Deoria court says custody not necessary in land fraud case; wife Nutan Thakur’s relief denied
stories.summary: Former IPS officer Amitabh Thakur has been granted bail by a district court in Deoria in a fraud case linked to land registered in his wife’s name. He will be released once the bail warrant reaches the jail authorities. However, the court rejected the anticipatory bail plea of his wife, Nutan Thakur, in the same case. Thakur was arrested late on December 9 from Shahjahanpur railway station. Following his arrest, he went on a hunger strike in jail, alleging police misconduct, which led to a deterioration in his health. He was initially admitted to a hospital in Gorakhpur and later shifted to Lucknow’s PGI for further treatment. Court said - custody not necessary On Monday, the bail application filed by former IPS officer Amitabh Thakur was heard in Deoria court. His lawyer Praveen Dwivedi argued that this case is quite old. No criminal intent is proven in this. This matter is related to errors in documents, not any planned fraud. Meanwhile, the prosecution opposed the bail and emphasized the seriousness of the case. The District Judge passed an order granting bail to Amitabh Thakur. The court said - the accused has been in judicial custody for a long time. His continuous custody is not necessary for investigation. However, in the same case, the court rejected the anticipatory bail application of Amitabh's wife Nutan Thakur. This means it is now clear that Nutan Thakur will have to knock on the High Court's door for relief. Because if she doesn't do so, she can be arrested anytime. Now know the case in which the former IPS was arrested This land fraud case dates back to 1999, when Amitabh Thakur was posted as SP in Deoria. A plot in the industrial area of Deoria was purchased in the name of his wife Nutan Thakur. It is alleged that during the plot's registry, in the documents Nutan Thakur's name was recorded as Nutan Devi, while the husband's name was recorded as Abhijat instead of Amitabh Thakur. Based on these facts, the case was described as related to fraud and forgery. It is alleged that false information regarding name and identity was deliberately recorded in documents, which later led to legal disputes. However, this case remained dormant for years. But in September 2025, a case was registered at Talkatora police station in Lucknow. Police began the investigation. Considering Amitabh Thakur's role suspicious, he was made an accused. After this, on December 10, 2025, the police arrested Amitabh Thakur and sent him to Deoria jail. Read the complete script of the 26-year-old plot allotment case Forcibly Retired 7 Years Before Regular Retirement The words 'Forcefully Retired IPS' are written at Amitabh Thakur's residence. Actually, his retirement was due in 2028. However, he was caught in several departmental investigations during his service. On the recommendation of the state government, the Central Home Ministry gave him forced retirement. Due to the allegations, the central government had conducted a screening of IPS officer Amitabh Thakur's service. The screening report stated that Amitabh Thakur was not fit to remain in government service. After this, he put up a board outside his house - "Forcefully Retired IPS Amitabh Thakur". He later became active in politics and continued his confrontation with the government on several issues.
