stories.title: CJM changed twice in 48 hours in Sambhal:Aditya Singh transferred, replacing judge who ordered FIR against ASP Chaudhary
stories.summary: A new Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) has been appointed for the second time in 48 hours in UP's Sambhal. Now, Kaushambi's CJM Deepak Kumar Jaiswal has been made the new CJM of Sambhal. Meanwhile, Sambhal CJM Aditya Singh has been sent back as Civil Judge (Senior Division), Chandausi. Additionally, Naved Akhtar has been appointed as Additional Senior Division Civil Judge, Chandausi, from Junior Division Judge, Sambhal. Aditya Singh was promoted just two days ago. He was made CJM Sambhal in place of Vibhanshu Sudhir, but lawyers were quite unhappy with this decision. It was Aditya Singh who had ordered the survey on the Shri Harihar Temple versus Shahi Jama Masjid claim in Sambhal. Vibhanshu was sent to Sultanpur as a Civil Judge, Senior Division. Let us tell you that the Allahabad High Court made a major reshuffle on Tuesday evening by transferring 14 judges. The shocking name in the list was Vibhanshu Sudhir. Vibhanshu had ordered the filing of an FIR against 20 policemen, including ASP Anuj Chaudhary, on January 9. It is alleged that during the Sambhal violence, ASP Anuj Chaudhary and other policemen shot a young man. Lawyers angered by judge's transfer, protested saying - murder of justice Where was Vibhanshu deployed? Now, let's understand why FIR orders were issued against the police personnel? In Sambhal's Nakhasa police station area, Yameen, who lives in Mohalla Khaggu Sarai Anjuman, filed a petition in the CJM court on February 6, 2025. Yameen had stated that his son, Alam, left home on November 24, 2024, to sell rusk (toast). When he reached the Shahi Jama Masjid area, the police shot him. Yameen had named 12 policemen, including the then CO Sambhal Anuj Chaudhary and Sambhal Kotwali Inspector Anuj Tomar, as accused. The case was heard in court on January 9, 2026. The Chief Judicial Magistrate had ordered an FIR to be registered against all police officers. Yameen's lawyer, Chaudhary Akhtar Hussain, said that his client's son got treatment while hiding from the police. The court was requested to file an FIR against former CO Anuj Chaudhary, former Inspector Anuj Tomar, and unknown police personnel. SP had said - Will appeal against the decision SP Krishna Kumar Bishnoi had said - Judicial inquiry into the violence has been completed. Therefore, this FIR will not be registered. We will appeal against the court's decision. 4 died in violence during survey on November 24, 2024 The Hindu side had claimed that Sambhal's Jama Masjid was previously the Harihar Temple. Babur had it demolished in 1529 and built a mosque. A petition was filed in the Sambhal court regarding this on November 19, 2024. On the same day, Civil Judge Senior Division Aditya Singh ordered a survey inside the mosque. The court had appointed Ramesh Singh Raghav as Advocate Commissioner. That same day at 4 PM, the team reached the mosque for the survey. The survey was conducted for 2 hours. However, the survey was not completed that day. After this, on November 24, the survey team reached Jama Masjid. The survey was being conducted inside the mosque. During this time, a large number of people gathered. The crowd threw stones at the police team. After this, violence erupted. Four people died from gunshot wounds. SP Krishna Kumar Bishnoi, prominent CO Anuj Chaudhary, Deputy Collector, along with 29 policemen, were injured. 3 women among 79 rioters were arrested After the violence, police arrested 79 rioters, including 3 women. A total of 12 FIRs were registered at Sambhal Kotwali and Thana Nakhasa. FIR was registered against 40 people, including SP MP Ziaur Rahman Barq, SP MLA Iqbal Mahmood's son Suhail Iqbal and 2750 unknown people. On June 18, SIT filed a chargesheet of 1128 pages in court against 23 people, including MP Barq. However, SP MLA's son Suhail Iqbal's name is not included in the chargesheet. CJM Vibhanshu issued several orders against police personnel On December 24, 2025, CJM Vibhanshu Sudhir ordered an FIR against 13 police personnel, including then Inspector Pankaj Lawania, in the fake encounter case in Sambhal. These included 2 inspectors, 4 sub-inspectors and constables who were posted at the time of the incident. The court directed the Station House Officer of Bahajoi to register a case immediately and submit a report to court within 3 days. In the Thana Bahajoi area on July 7, 2022, Omvir, Dhirendra and Avnesh were arrested during an encounter. In the case presented before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Omvir had accused then CO Gopal Singh of staging a fake encounter. The court ordered that he should not be included in this case.

stories.title: 2 crore cash, 62 kg silver found in Kanpur:Police got tired counting notes, had to call for machine; 5 arrested
stories.summary: Police found 2 crore cash and 62 kg silver from a house in Kanpur. The situation became such that police officers were sweating while counting such a large amount. Police had to call in machines to count the notes. The counting of notes went on for about 4 hours. Police officers got tired of collecting the silver. Actually, the police raided a house late at night. An international betting and hawala network was being run from the house. Police have arrested 5 people from the gang. Nepalese currency was also recovered from them. Police are gathering information about other gang members by interrogating the accused. Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal reached the spot to investigate based on the information. The raid was conducted in the Dhankutti locality of Collectorganj. Had been receiving hawala complaints for many days ADCP Sumit Sudhakar Ramteke of the Special Operation Group said - For the past several days, complaints of hawala, betting business and illegal share trading were being received in the city. Based on this, a raid was conducted at the house of Ramakant Gupta, a resident of Dhankutti, around 9 pm on Thursday. The police surrounded the house from all sides and went inside. Inside the house, they found a stash of notes and a significant amount of silver. When the police interrogated the suspects, they couldn't give proper answers. Police removed money stored in cartons. These contained bundles of 500-rupee notes. There were 500-rupee notes worth 1.80 crores. The rest were bundles of 200 and 100 rupees. Due to such a large amount, police also brought machines to count the notes and weigh the silver. Pen drives, modems, computers, laptops, etc., were recovered from the accused. Police have taken into custody Rahul Jain from Kidwai Nagar, Shivam Tripathi, Sachin Gupta from Yashoda Nagar Gangaganj, Vanshraj, and one other person. All five were reported to be friends. In the preliminary investigation, the names of some people from Delhi, Aligarh, Varanasi, Indore, Mumbai, Noida, and Jaipur have come up. More information about them is being gathered. ADCP Sumit Sudhakar Ramteke said- The accused were involved in cricket betting, hawala business and illegal stock market trading. The accused have connections with gangster and international cricket bookie Ankush Agarwal. Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal said- The gang's connections lead directly to Delhi and Noida. Deals have been made with several influential people. The arrested accused have named some influential people. Information is being gathered.

stories.summary: In Prayagraj, the conflict between Avimukteshwaranand and the Magh Mela administration is escalating. In this context, Avimukteshwaranand said, I will not take the Basant Panchami snan until the administration apologises. They are only playing the game of issuing notices. My Mauni Amavasya snan has not yet taken place, so how can I take the holy dip? Meanwhile, CM Yogi Adityanath, without naming Avimukteshwaranand, stated, No one has the right to disrupt tradition. There are those who, under the guise of religion, are plotting to weaken Sanatan Dharma. We must remain vigilant against such people. At the same time, Deputy CM Keshav Maurya in Azamgarh said, ‘I bow at the feet of Jyotishpeethadhishwar Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand and request him to take the holy dip and bring this matter to a close.’ On the day of Basant Panchami, devotees have been taking a dip in the Magh Mela since 4:00 AM. There is a huge crowd at the Sangam ghat. On Thursday evening, Baba Ramdev also took a holy dip with Satua Baba. What happened on Mauni Amavasya? On January 18, during the Magh Mela, Avimukteshwaranand was heading for a holy dip in his palanquin. The police stopped him and asked him to proceed on foot. When his followers protested, there was a scuffle. Angered by this, Avimukteshwaranand staged a sit-in outside his camp.

stories.title: Saint community divided over Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand dispute:Urges ending politics in religious issues, condemns violence, insists apology from admin for sanctity of Mela
stories.summary: The saint community is divided over the Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand dispute in Prayagraj. Some support him, while others oppose. Aniruddhacharya Maharaj criticized the administration for allegedly assaulting sadhus, while Ravindra Puri said anyone abusing the CM cannot be a saint. Shankaracharya Sadanand Saraswati said - Batuk Brahmins were beaten, this is wrong Shankaracharya Sadanand Saraswati of Dwarka's Sharda Peeth says that the administration does not understand the meaning of Shikha, by grabbing which they beat the saints. The Shikha is where Brahma resides. It is wrong that Shankaracharya and Batuk Brahmins were beaten for taking a bath in the Ganges. This is the arrogance of governance. One should never misuse their power. Those who prevent bathing in the Ganges incur the sin of cow slaughter. This is the word of scripture. Therefore, such acts should not be done. If we have been given any power, we should not misuse it. We strongly condemn this act of the administration. Aniruddhacharya said - Administration should apologize Storyteller Aniruddhacharya Maharaj said - The administration has made a mistake. They grabbed Brahmins and sadhus by their hair and beat them. Why isn't the administration apologizing? Why is there such a delay in apologizing? Saints are compassionate; they will forgive immediately. What is the administration's ego in asking for forgiveness? Who gave you the right to grab someone's hair and beat them? Did the Constitution give you this right? Go to the feet of saints, if a mistake was made, apologize. The administration should not drag this out. When one seeks refuge, saints forgive. Nischlanand called Avimukteshwaranand 'Favorite' Govardhan Math's Shankaracharya Swami Nischalanand Saraswati of Puri said - Avimukteshwaranand's decision is irrefutable. Even the Supreme Court recognizes his decisions. He showed affection towards Avimukteshwaranand by calling him his 'favorite'. Shankaracharya said - Any dispute can only be responded to when it is officially brought to their attention. This is like inviting a terrible war. Until our blood boils, all this will continue. Ravindra Puri said - A saint who calls CM son of Humayun is not a saint Mahant Ravindra Puri, President of Akhil Bharatiya Akhada Parishad, said - Mini Mahakumbh is going on in Prayagraj. Regarding calling the Chief Minister the son of Akbar and Humayun, he said that this cannot be the language of a saint. If he had any complaint, he should have complained to the Chief Minister or gone to court. Why is he directly targeting the Chief Minister? We, the saint community, strongly condemn this. Strict action should be taken against Avimukteshwaranand. If anyone is working to advance Sanatan, it is the Prime Minister, Chief Minister, and Home Minister who are doing it. Ravindra Puri said - When the Ram temple was being built in Ayodhya, you (Avimukteshwaranand) asked why the Ram temple was being built? Wherever work happens, they oppose it. We cannot hear such things against the Prime Minister and the Chief Minister. Chief Minister Yogi himself is a saint and a Peethadheeshwar. We will not tolerate such a conspiracy against him. Will talk to the saints of the council. Shringverpur Peethadheeshwar said - Shankaracharya should not do politics Shringverpur's Peethadheeshwar Jagadguru Ramanujacharya Shandilya Maharaj said - The administration should not have gotten saints killed; this is wrong. Also, Shankaracharya should not do politics. He said - Some political people also want to enter among saints, which is wrong. There is no need for politics among saints. Shandilya Maharaj's target was on SP chief Akhilesh Yadav and Congress state president Ajay Rai. Ramanujacharya said - Nothing is spoiled yet, should apologize Jagadguru Ramanujacharya said - What good has Rambhadracharya done? Holding a staff in hand, we do not worship broken idols. If a Brahmin's body is broken, worship does not happen. 4 Shankaracharyas, 13 Akhadas, and 5 Vaishnacharyas saints are worthy of worship and veneration. They should have been respected; the administration should have arranged for them to come by palanquin. They should have requested that Maharaj give up the palanquin. Come walk with us, we will ensure your safe bathing. Nothing is ruined yet; apologize and put an end to the dispute. Not just in Prayagraj, if there is a need for protest in Delhi, the saint community is ready to do it. Devaki Nandan Thakur - Violence against saints is not right In Agra, Devakinandan Thakur said - This is a time of moral dilemma for me. Both sides are our own. On one side, there is Shankaracharya, who is like God; on the other side, there are those people who were concerned about the large number of people who came for bathing. I will only say that such a situation should not be escalated. Forgetting mutual differences, every Sanatani should resolve issues with love by sitting together in one voice, not complicate them. The administration should also ensure that those who wear a tilak on their forehead, have a shikha on their head, and wear saffron robes should be treated with respect. Such beating is not right. Now about the saints of Mathura Mahant Ramdas said - Insulting Batuk Brahmins is condemnable Mahant Ramdas Maharaj says - Shankaracharya Maharaj's position is high; he is our Simhastha. Similarly, Yogi Maharaj is also in a high position. He takes care of the entire UP. However, the insult to Batuk Brahmins is very condemnable. They are servants of Sanatan. Why were they insulted? The administration must explain this. In our religion, fingers are easily pointed. Try pointing at Maulana Sahib, Haji Sahib in Islam. This position of Shankaracharya is Lord Shiva's position. This is a Brahmin who serves, practices celibacy, is a lord of earth, and has knowledge of the Vedas. They have their own beliefs. Shankaracharya's fast is not appropriate, but using batons on Brahmins is also wrong Mahant Atul Krishna Maharaj of Parikrama Marg in Vrindavan said - I just want to say that saints, mahants, and householders should not be divided. What is happening on the land of Prayagraj seems to be going towards a different kind of politics. The fast undertaken by Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand was not appropriate. The police administration's use of batons on their Brahmins was also wrong. We request Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath to completely end this tug of war. Words of Kashi's Saints Swami Chakrapani said - Young priests should be worshipped, not oppressed Swami Chakrapani Maharaj said - Kumbh and Magh Mela are not the contribution of any single person; they are the invaluable heritage of sages, seers, and saint tradition. Maintaining its dignity is the collective responsibility of the government, administration, and the saint community. He described the incident of fighting with the boys and pulling their hair as a condemnable and heinous crime. Said that the boys should be worshipped and served, not subjected to atrocities. The braid is a symbol of the Sanatan tradition. An attack on it is an attack on the dignity of Sanatan. He said that the people of Prayag and Kashi are known for sin-redemption, charity-virtue, and service to saints. Every wrong deed committed at such holy places cannot escape divine justice. He asked the administration to apologize to the saints and priests. Jitendranand said - Such evidence in court, cannot consider him Shankaracharya Swami Jitendranand Saraswati, National General Secretary of Akhil Bharatiya Sant Samiti, gave a strong statement. Said - There is such evidence present in court, based on which Avimukteshwaranand cannot be considered Shankaracharya. They get beaten every time, this time they were creating disorder during the bath. According to the document, until a final decision is made regarding the Shankaracharya position, neither Swami Avimukteshwaranand nor any other person can be appointed or enthroned as Shankaracharya. The order also states that providing any facilities to Avimukteshwaranand as Shankaracharya will be considered contempt of court. This matter is pending in the Supreme Court as a civil appeal. In 26 years, they have engaged in violence at the fair multiple times. Now the words of Ayodhya's saints Hanumangarhi's priest Tulsidas said - He is conspiring at the behest of Congress Acharya Pandit Rakesh Das of Ayodhya's Jyotish Bhavan said - Swami Avimukteshwaranand is a symbol of faith and respect. He was going for a Ganga bath, not by any vehicle but by palanquin. There were 100 people with him. Under these circumstances, stopping him from taking a Ganga bath was not appropriate in any way. Hanumangarhi's priest Tulsidas says - Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand is conspiring against the government at the behest of Congress. Mahant Ramkumar Das said - Swami Avimukteshwaranand's going for a Ganga bath while sitting on a palanquin should not be called appropriate at all. This is Kalpvas's Magh Mela, not Mahakumbh's bath. Such behavior is not appropriate in any way in the world. Senior Naga Shatrughna Das of Hanumangarhi's Ujjainia Patti said - Swami and Avimukteshwaranand lack knowledge; they should chant Sitaram Sitaram. Read what happened on Mauni Amavasya On January 18, Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand was going for a bath in a palanquin during Mauni Amavasya at the Magh Mela. The police stopped Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand's palanquin. Police asked him to walk to Sangam on foot. Shankaracharya's disciples did not agree and started moving forward with the palanquin. This led to pushing and shoving between the disciples and the police. Police took several disciples into custody. Police also beat up a sadhu at the police station. This angered Shankaracharya, and he insisted on getting his disciples released. Officers tried to reason with him, folded their hands, but he did not agree. After this, the police took several more supporters of Shankaracharya into custody. Shankaracharya's palanquin was pulled and taken 1 km away from the Sangam. During this, the palanquin's canopy also broke. Shankaracharya could not even take a bath.

stories.title: Killer of businessman’s son dies in encounter:Abducted and murdered for not paying ransom in Chitrakoot; body found in a box within 24 hours
stories.summary: In Chitrakoot, UP, police have encountered two accused who kidnapped and murdered a businessman's son. Police killed one accused in the encounter, while the other was shot in the leg. Both criminals had kidnapped businessman Ashok Kesarwani's 13-year-old son 24 hours ago. They had demanded ransom. When they didn't receive the ransom, both murdered the businessman's son late Thursday night. Police surrounded both criminals on Friday morning. As soon as they saw the police, both started firing. In retaliatory action, police killed a criminal named Kallu, while his accomplice Irfan was shot in the leg. See pictures... Now know the full case in 4 pointers.... Trader's son abducted in broad daylight, then ransom demanded: In the Bargad police station area, in broad daylight, miscreants abducted Ayush Kesarwani, son of trader Ashok Kesarwani, a resident of Bargad market. Shortly after the abduction, a ransom was demanded from the family. The police and family were engaged in negotiations and search, but when the ransom was not paid, the miscreants brutally murdered the child. Body found in a locked box, people stunned upon breaking the lock: During the search, the police found a locked box. When the lock of the box was broken, Ayush's body was recovered inside. The sight was so horrific that the people present at the scene were stunned. As soon as the news of the body's discovery spread, a sensation and outrage spread throughout the Bargad area. One kidnapper killed in police encounter: During police action in the kidnapping-murder case, one accused was killed in an encounter. The deceased accused has been identified as Kallu alias Sahve Iman (about 70 years old), resident of Katra Chauraha, Karma, Ghurpur police station. According to the police, he was killed by a bullet in the encounter. Identification of the second accused, continuous raids in search Police have apprehended the second accused involved in this heinous crime by shooting him in the leg. He has been identified as Irfan Ansari, son of Aftab Alam, resident of Katra Chauraha, Karma, Ghurpur Police Station. Security has been increased in the district regarding the entire matter and the investigation has been intensified. News is being updated....

stories.title: Birthday girl creates ruckus on Kanpur highway:Sits on car window while driving at 100 km/h; cuts 10 cakes placed on vehicle's bonnet
stories.summary: On Aligarh Highway in Kanpur, the birthday girl and her friends created a huge ruckus. The girl cut 10 cakes on the car's bonnet. Then set off fireworks on the highway. After that, she sat on the car window and drove at 100 kmph on the highway. Two cars kept following behind her. The incident happened on Tuesday at 12 midnight, its video surfaced on Thursday. In which two girls are seen celebrating a birthday on the highway with 6 boys. The birthday girl's name is Mayra Thakur. She is a resident of the Barra police station area. Earlier, on December 29, a video of Mayra had surfaced. In it, she was seen beating a young woman on the highway for her boyfriend. She had grabbed her hair and dragged her on the road. Girl said - It's 12 o'clock, see what we do A video surfaced on social media on Thursday. This video is from Kanpur Aligarh Highway. It was shared from a social media handle named Sakshi Mishra. In the video, a girl named Mayra Thakur is seen wearing a birthday belt. She is accompanied by her female friend. Her friend can be seen saying in the video, You know today is my sister's birthday. It's 12 o'clock at night, and we are going. Now see what we do? More than 6 youths in three cars, who were part of the girl's birthday celebration, parked their cars on the highway. Fireworks on highway after cutting cake One of these cars has about 10 cakes placed on the bonnet, which the birthday girl cuts. After cutting the cake, massive fireworks are set off on the highway railing. After this, everyone gets into all three cars. A girl can be seen sitting on the driver's side window in the leading car. While a young man is sitting in the left side window of the car, he is shooting her video. Both cars are racing at high speed on the highway from behind. Car passengers are making videos from behind. Mayra beat up a girl over boyfriend Another video of Mayra went viral on December 29, 2025. The video was from the Yashoda Nagar bypass. In it, Mayra and a girl were seen fighting over a boyfriend. Mayra slammed the other girl on the road. She grabbed her hair and dragged her on the road. Then she slapped her 11 times while pulling her hair. After that, she rained kicks and punches on her chest and head. During this time, Mayra's female companion kept making a video of the incident. Mayra was saying that you had left Abhishek. Now that he has become mine, you will call him babu. Tell me, will you call him Babu? While the other girl kept apologizing by holding her feet.

stories.title: Rain in Noida Ghaziabad, hail alert in 18 districts:Cold to return as chilly winds blow from the hills; temperature drops to 4.8°C
stories.summary: The weather has changed once again in UP. It rained early Friday morning in Noida-Ghaziabad. The drizzle with strong cold winds escalated the chill and people were seen huddled in their homes. Roads remained deserted, besides a rain alert across the state has been issued for today. Hail may fall in 18 districts. Meanwhile, the weather department said that rain and snowfall have begun in the hill states. As a result, cold winds coming from there will increase the cold. In the coming days, the temperature may drop by 3-4°C. Many districts may also experience fog. Visibility could be reduced to 100 meters. Talking about the last 24 hours, Muzaffarnagar was the coldest, where the night temperature was recorded at 4.8°C. This was followed by Bareilly at 6.3°C, Meerut at 7.1°C, Ayodhya at 7.5°C and Kanpur at 7.7°C. Meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said - The rainy season has begun in the state. Rain may occur in several districts for 2 days. Weather is likely to clear from January 25. Weather fluctuations will continue due to active western disturbance in northern Pakistan. See the weather pictures- Hail possible in 18 districts Saharanpur, Shamli, Muzaffarnagar, Bulandshahr, Aligarh, Mathura, Hathras, Kasganj, Eta, Agra, Firozabad, Bijnor, Amroha, Moradabad, Rampur, Bareilly, Sambhal, Badaun and surrounding areas. Thunderstorm alert in these districts; Warning of lightning strikes Gonda, Balrampur, Shravasti, Bahraich, Lakhimpur Kheri, Sitapur, Hardoi, Farrukhabad, Kannauj, Kanpur Dehat, Kanpur Nagar, Unnao, Lucknow, Barabanki, Saharanpur, Shamli, Muzaffarnagar, Baghpat, Meerut, Ghaziabad, Hapur, Gautam Buddha Nagar, Bulandshahr, Aligarh, Mathura, Hathras, Kasganj, Etah, Agra, Firozabad, Mainpuri, Etawah, Auraiya, Bijnor, Agroha, Moradabad, Rampur, Bareilly, Pilibhit, Shahjahanpur, Sambhal, Budaun and surrounding areas. Why did the weather change, know here The effect of active western disturbance in north-western India is now clearly visible in Uttar Pradesh as well. Due to this, cloud movement has increased in many parts of the state. There has been a change in wind direction. Where easterly winds were blowing earlier, now westerly winds are taking their place. This has increased humidity in the atmosphere and conditions for rain are forming in some places. How will the weather be for 2 days Rain beneficial for wheat-lentils According to agricultural experts, this rain is beneficial for wheat, lentils and chickpea crops, but mustard and potato crops may be damaged. Farmers have been advised to keep track of weather information and spray medicines on crops when needed to prevent damage.

stories.title: Why do people keep 'shikha' in Sanatan Dharma?:From Vedic rituals and Chanakya’s vow to meditational energy beliefs
stories.summary: In Sanatan Dharma, many people keep a tuft of hair (shikha) on the head because the spot is traditionally linked with the Sahasrara Chakra. It is believed this area is connected to spiritual energy, and keeping a shikha helps keep it active, making meditation and concentration easier. As a result, followers feel it supports better control over the mind, intellect, and body, which is why the practice has continued. Chanakya's Shikha Pledge Question: What is the importance of keeping a choti (tuft of hair)? Answer: In Hinduism, there are 16 types of sacraments described from birth to the death of a person. Each has its own importance. One of these is the Mundan ceremony. The mundan (head-shaving ceremony) is performed in the first, third, or fifth year of a child. During this ritual, a small amount of the child's hair is left. The ritual of keeping shikha (tuft of hair) on the head is also performed during the Yajnopavit or Upanayana ceremony. According to Hindu beliefs, keeping a tuft of hair is necessary for performing worship, rituals, and yagnas. Maharaj Harichaitanya Brahmachari from Prayagraj explains - the place where the shikha is kept is traditionally considered a symbolic spot connected to the universe. It is believed that there is an interconnection between the shikha, navel, and heart. That's why the shikha is considered important. In many religious activities, while remembering or taking a sankalp (resolution), one first touches the shikha and pays respect. According to religious beliefs, every Hindu should keep a shikha. While it is considered especially necessary for Vedic Brahmins. However, detached Brahmins (who adopt the path of renunciation by separating from worldly life) sometimes do not keep a tuft of hair. Question: Since when has the tradition of keeping Choti (tuft of hair) been practiced in Sanatan Dharma? Answer: BHU Astrologer Prof. Vinay Pandey explains - The tradition of keeping Choti/Shikha in Sanatan Dharma is considered thousands of years old. According to historians and religious beliefs, this tradition has been continuing since the Vedic period. During that time, Gurukul education, Yagna, and Upanayan Sanskar held special importance. During that era, keeping a tuft of hair (choti) was considered a symbol of culture, discipline, and religious identity. Even today, many people adopt it by connecting it to their faith and tradition. Question: Is keeping a tuft of hair a religious rule or just tradition? Answer: In Sanatan Dharma, keeping a tuft of hair is not a strict religious rule. It is considered an ancient Vedic tradition and custom. According to religious beliefs, there has been a tradition of keeping shikha (tuft of hair) after the Upanayana ceremony. Especially among those who perform worship, yagya, and Vedic rituals. Question: How long should the shikha (tuft of hair) be? Answer: Vinay Pandey explains - According to religious beliefs, the shape of the Sahasrara chakra is considered similar to a cow's hoof (the lowest, hard, nail-like part of the foot). For this reason, many people keep their sikha (hair tuft) equal to the size of a cow's hoof. In astrology, it is said that if someone is experiencing negative effects of Rahu in their horoscope, keeping a sikha on the head is considered beneficial. This provides relief during Rahu's phase and starts bringing good results. Question: What is the scientific reason for keeping a sikha? Answer: Dr. Ashok Kumar Satpathy, Associate Professor in the Sanskrit Department of Lucknow University, explains - There is also a scientific reason behind keeping a sikha. The spot where the sikha is kept is the center of the brain. This location controls the body's organs, intellect, and mind. Keeping a choti (tuft of hair) keeps the Sahasrara chakra awakened. It helps in maintaining control over the intellect, mind, and body. The 7 chakras present in our body stay awakened. This maintains balance in our body. Where the choti is kept, there lies the Sushumna nadi, which provides positive energy to the body. The development of the entire body is considered to be related to the Sushumna nadi. Question: What are the rules for keeping a choti? Answer: According to Dr. Ashok Kumar Satpathy, there are rules for keeping a Choti (tuft of hair). While keeping a Choti, all hair from the head should be cut. The Choti should only be kept in the middle of the head. Religious scriptures describe the shape of the Choti to be similar to a cow's hoof. During charity, worship, and while eating, the Choti should be tied in a knot. Additionally, while performing daily activities, the Choti should be kept untied.

stories.title: UP CM Yogi gets lion-themed chair:Saffron seat made from Kedarnath, featuring carvings inspired by Uttarakhand temples
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will now sit on a special lion-themed chair. The chair is unique as it has been crafted from leftover deodar wood from the Kedarnath reconstruction project. It reflects intricate carvings inspired by temples in Uttarakhand and also emits a natural fragrance, meaning it spreads a pleasant aroma wherever it is placed. The chair has been gifted by Uttarakhand Minister of State (Colonel Retd) Ajay Kothiyal. He handed it over to Yogi Adityanath in Gorakhpur on January 15, on the occasion of Makar Sankranti. Presented to him in his capacity as Mahant, the chair was well received and has been installed in the main auditorium of the Gorakhnath Temple. Special chair made from leftover deodar wood from Kedarnath Colonel Ajay Kothiyal said that deodar wood was used on a large scale during the Kedarnath reconstruction project. Some of that wood was left over. He said that he got the idea to use this wood to make something related to a sacred and religious place. In this sequence, he decided to get a special deodar chair made for Yogi Adityanath. Temple-inspired cedar chair design The chair was designed by architect Krishna Kudiyal, who studied the architecture of Uttarakhand’s temples before finalising the design. It was crafted by a traditional wood artisan from Kota village near Chakrata after about 15 days of meticulous work. The chair features lion figures embossed on both armrests as symbols of power, while the back showcases carvings inspired by Uttarakhand’s temple architecture. Use of saffron colour, inclusion of Mahasu Temple's woodwork Colonel Kothiyal stated that an attempt has been made to primarily incorporate the woodwork art of Mahasu Temple into the chair. Additionally, Yogi Adityanath's favorite saffron color has also been used in the chair's form. He informed that this chair was presented to Yogi Adityanath as a Mahant, and he liked it very much. This is why it has been installed in the main auditorium of Gorakhnath Temple. Yogi's ancestral village in Pauri Another special feature of this particular chair is that due to the deodar wood, its sweet scent also spreads throughout the hall. Yogi Adityanath also has an old connection with Uttarakhand. He is originally a resident of Panchur village in Yamkeshwar block of Pauri district. Who is Colonel Ajay Kothiyal? Colonel Ajay Kothiyal has been the face of the Kedarnath Reconstruction Project. He played a crucial role in the reconstruction of the Dham after the 2013 Kedarnath disaster. After this, he contested the 2022 assembly elections as the chief ministerial candidate from the Aam Aadmi Party, but was unsuccessful. After that, he joined the BJP. Currently, he holds the status of a Minister of State in the Uttarakhand government.

stories.title: Forcibly retired IPS receives death threat in Deoria jail:Letter found hidden under stone; ex-officer on hunger strike
stories.summary: UP's forcibly retired IPS officer Amitabh Thakur received a death threat in Deoria jail on Friday. He found a letter, typed on a computer, hidden under a stone outside his barrack. He immediately informed the jail administration about this. The jail superintendent informed the DM-SP and initiated an investigation. However, jail officials are reluctant to comment. Amitabh Thakur has been imprisoned since December 10 in a fraud case. He has been on a hunger strike in jail for the past two days. Read the lawyer's letter Know in detail Advocate Praveen Dwivedi said that former IPS officer Amitabh Thakur has been lodged in jail since December 10 in a land allocation case related to the Industrial Area and has been on a hunger strike for the past two days. He is demanding CCTV footage and CDRs from the time of his arrest, which, according to him, have not been provided. Dwivedi stated that during his meeting, Amitabh Thakur appeared extremely frightened and revealed that he had found a computer-typed letter containing a clear death threat hidden under a stone outside his barrack. Following this, he has been feeling mentally distressed and insecure. Thakur immediately informed the jail authorities and handed over the threatening letter and the stone. The lawyer termed the incident very serious, especially in a high-security jail, and expressed concern that his client’s life could be in real danger. Court appearance on January 17 The decision on Amitabh Thakur's bail application is still pending. Advocate Praveen Dwivedi had demanded Amitabh Thakur's appearance during the hearing of the bail application in the District Judge's court on January 17. The court accepted this and ordered the accused to be produced. Sudden illness on January 6 Case in which the former IPS was arrested Former IPS officer Amitabh Thakur was arrested late on the night of December 9 from Shahjahanpur railway station. This arrest is related to a 26-year-old plot allocation in Deoria. Forcibly retired 7 years before retirement Outside Amitabh Thakur’s residence, a board reads 'Forcibly Retired IPS.' In fact, his retirement was due in 2028, but during his service, he faced several departmental inquiries. On the state government’s recommendation, the Union Home Ministry ordered his compulsory retirement. The central government had screened his service record and concluded that he was not fit to continue in government service. After this decision, Thakur put up the board outside his house. He later became active in politics and continued to frequently clash with the government on various issues.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:BJP nears victory in Mumbai civic body polls; UP leaders play key role in Maharashtra civic polls more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest updates from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. BJP nears victory in Mumbai civic body polls, Thackeray family's 30-year rule to end For the first time in Mumbai's history, the BJP may have a mayor. In the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) election results, the BJP alliance has a lead in 118 of the 227 seats. Of these, the BJP is leading in 90 seats, and the Shiv Sena-led Shinde is leading in 28. 2. Brawl over 'Prabhat Pheri' in Badaun: police-villager clash leaves women injured, procession allowed under supervision A clash erupted between police and villagers in Byor Kasimabad, Badaun, on Friday over a 'Prabhat Pheri' route dispute. Police stopped the procession, leading to pushing and shoving, and dispersed the crowd with batons. The procession was later allowed under supervision. 3. Where Shah Jahan and Mumtaz are actually buried: true graves 22 feet below Taj Mahal dome, entry restricted The Taj Mahal, famed for its marble, colored inlay work, and architecture, conceals the true graves of Shah Jahan and Mumtaz 22 feet below the main dome. Entry to this burial chamber is not allowed, though the structure continues to narrate their story. 4. Venezuelan leader, Machado, presents her Nobel Peace Prize to Trump Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado said on Thursday that she presented her Nobel Peace Prize medal to US President Donald Trump during a meeting at the White House. 5. UP leaders play key role in Maharashtra civic polls: 30 lakh migrant voters influence results UP leaders, especially from eastern UP, campaigned actively in Maharashtra civic elections to attract about 30 lakh UP-origin voters. The Samajwadi Party fielded candidates in high-density migrant areas, with prominent leaders staying in Mumbai for several days. 6. UP minister tries to touch commissioner’s feet during Lalitpur overbridge visit, stopped by officer Minister of State Manohar Lal Panth attempted to touch the feet of Jhansi Division Commissioner Vimal Kumar Dubey while inspecting an under-construction overbridge in Lalitpur on Thursday. The Commissioner stopped him and folded his hands, amusing the MLA and district officials. 7. Govt cracks down on illegal walkie-talkie sales citing threat to national security, ₹44 lakh fine on eight e-commerce companies The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed penalties totaling ₹44 lakh on eight e-commerce companies, including Amazon, Flipkart, Meesho, and Meta, for selling illegal walkie-talkies. The authority termed these sales a serious threat to national security. 8. Baba from masaura owns ₹50-crore ashram: brother murdered, story of Santosh Tiwari becoming Jagadguru Santosh Tiwari, from Masaura village in Lalitpur, Bundelkhand, lives in luxury with a ₹50-crore ashram, Land Rover Defender, Porsche Turbo, and Ray-Ban sunglasses. Often praised by UP CM Yogi, he rose to prominence despite his brother being murdered. 9. UP government promotes sports with basketball event: CM Yogi highlights jobs, rewards, and olympic culture In Gorakhpur, CM Yogi played basketball and inaugurated the inter-university women’s basketball tournament. He interacted with players, released gas balloons, and emphasised sports-related jobs, rewards, and fostering an Olympic culture in UP universities. 10. Kartik Aaryan returns ₹15 crore after failure of recent film ‘Tu Meri Main Tera Main Tera Tu Meri’ at Box Office Kartik Aaryan and Ananya Panday's film 'Tu Meri Main Tera Main Tera Tu Meri' was released in cinemas on December 25, 2025. However, the film did not perform as expected at the box office and proved to be a flop. Meanwhile, a report by Bollywood Hungama claims that after the film's failure, Kartik returned approximately ₹15 crore from his fees to the producers.

stories.title: Massive fire in Lucknow, man jumps from apartment:Hangs from balcony for 10 minutes, people flee as smoke chokes building
stories.summary: A massive fire broke out on Friday in Block 39 of the Basant Kunj Scheme in Thakurganj, Lucknow. The blaze spread rapidly and engulfed three floors of the building, filling the premises with thick smoke. Several people were trapped inside as panic gripped the area. In a desperate attempt to escape, some residents jumped from the building to save their lives. Eyewitnesses reported scenes of chaos, with people shouting for help as the fire raged. Four fire tenders were rushed to the spot and firefighting operations are underway to bring the blaze under control. Chief Fire Officer Anshu Mittal said a young man who was trapped inside the building was safely rescued by the fire brigade. The cause of the fire is yet to be ascertained. Fire breaks out in Thakurganj area A massive fire broke out in a house in the Thakurganj area at around 2:30 pm on Friday. Within minutes, the flames engulfed the entire house. Seeing thick smoke and rising flames, local residents alerted the fire station. Fire tenders rushed to the spot and safely evacuated the people living in the house. The fire was brought under control by three fire brigade vehicles. Eyewitnesses said the fire started due to a sudden short circuit near an air conditioner. Smoke appeared first, followed by intense flames. The fire quickly spread to another part of the house. The fire brigade team, which reached the spot promptly, rescued the family members. Reports also suggest that the fire spread to three neighbouring houses.

stories.title: Uttar Pradesh Police revises transfer policy:Home district and range postings barred; compassionate transfers restricted to spouse cases
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Police has made a major change to its transfer policy for Sub-Inspectors and Constables recruited up to the 2019 batch. Under the revised rules, transfers in general cases will now be considered only on compassionate grounds. Such transfers will be permitted exclusively in cases where both husband and wife are serving in the police force. The policy also makes it clear that no Inspector or Sub-Inspector will be posted in their home range, home district, or adjoining border district. For availing a compassionate transfer, both spouses must submit their police identity cards as proof. Officials said exemptions from the posting restrictions will be given only when both the husband and wife are working in the police department. The department has clarified that the changes aim to bring uniformity and transparency to postings. Transfers allowed for personnel recruited before 2019 The DGP said that for personnel recruited after the 2019 batch, transfers will be considered only in cases where both husband and wife are serving in the police department. As per the transfer policy dated June 22, 2018, no inspector or sub-inspector can be posted in their home range, home district or a district bordering their home district. Similarly, head constables and constables cannot be posted in their home district or a district adjoining their home district. Transfer policy was also changed before the Lok Sabha elections Ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the UP DGP had amended the transfer policy. Under this, police personnel who had completed three years in a district, or were due to complete three years by May 31, 2024, were transferred. Yogi government’s stand on posting husband and wife together Police couples posted in different districts face several difficulties, including family and practical issues. Keeping these problems in mind, and in line with the government’s transfer policy, efforts have been made to post husband and wife in the same district. On May 22, 2025, in the first phase, 101 constables were transferred under this policy. Female police personnel were posted in the districts where their husbands were posted, while male personnel were sent to the districts where their wives were serving. This was the first time that such a large number of police personnel were transferred under this policy.

stories.title: Leopard escapes during rescue, injures 4 in Kushinagar:Net tears as animal growls, forest staff loosen grip; search on with drones
stories.summary: Four people, including a forest guard, were injured in a leopard attack in Kushinagar on Thursday. The leopard was trapped in wire fencing laid in a sugarcane field. When a forest department team reached the spot to rescue the animal, they laid a net, but it tore during the operation. As the leopard growled, forest workers loosened their grip, allowing it to escape. After breaking free, the leopard first attacked a forest guard and then a forest worker. A local youth intervened and saved the forest worker by hitting the animal with a stick. The leopard later attacked another villager and an employee of Wildlife Trust of India. Around 50 forest workers, including DFO Arun Kumar, are currently searching for the leopard. Six nets have been laid in nearby fields, and drones are being used for surveillance. The administration has appealed to people to stay away from the area and avoid provoking the animal. The incident took place in Siswa Gopal village under the Khadda police station area. First see 3 pictures- How the incident unfolded Village head Suresh’s brother, Indresh, said he was on his way to cut sugarcane when he spotted the leopard in Rajesh Lal Srivastava’s field. “The leopard tried to pounce, but it was trapped in the wire and could not attack. I raised an alarm. On hearing the noise, the leopard started growling,” he said. He added that villagers ran back and informed others. Soon, hundreds of people from nearby villages reached the spot. A team of five to seven forest personnel from Maharajganj district arrived and threw a net over the leopard. They then began cutting the wire with a sickle. “When the leopard growled, the forest workers got scared and loosened their grip,” Indresh said. Leopard attacks forest staff and villagers The leopard escaped through a torn portion of the net and first attacked the forest guard, injuring his foot. He was saved when people nearby beat the animal with sticks. The leopard then pounced on a forest worker. Villager Krishnandan Kumar intervened and struck the leopard with a stick, saving the worker’s life. The animal also attacked Angad, a local youth, and Arshad Hussain, project head of Wildlife Trust of India in Maharajganj. All injured were taken for treatment. Villagers allege negligence by forest department After the incident, villagers accused the forest department of negligence. Nizamuddin, a local resident, said the leopard escaped because the team used a torn net. “The forest department came with a damaged net. The leopard escaped through the same torn section while attacking people,” he alleged. Angad, who was injured, said the situation worsened due to crowd noise. “People were shouting, and some children climbed trees to make videos. The leopard became uncontrollable and attacked me while escaping,” he said. Another villager said sugarcane peeling and cutting work was underway in nearby fields. “If the leopard had not been trapped, a major accident could not have been ruled out,” he said. Forest department says noise led to failure Forest officials said the rescue attempt failed due to heavy crowding. Nichaul Range forest worker Mahatma said villagers gathered at the rescue site despite appeals to stay away. “Because of the noise, the leopard attacked forest workers and fled. The team tried its best to capture it,” he said. DFO Arun Singh said a team from Gorakhpur Zoo has been called, and forest staff from Maharajganj are assisting in the operation. “The leopard is still in the area. Search operations are underway, and it will be caught soon,” he said.

stories.title: Scorpio runs over six at 100 kmph in Chandauli:5 vehicles crushed in 10 seconds, angry crowd assaults driver
stories.summary: A speeding Scorpio car went out of control in Chandauli and hit five vehicles within seconds, before running over six pedestrians. The impact was severe, leaving vehicles badly damaged and debris scattered across the road. Some people were thrown several feet away, causing panic at the spot. After the collisions, the Scorpio rammed into a divider. Locals pulled the driver out of the vehicle and thrashed him. Three other people were inside the car. All four were reportedly drunk. The crowd later handed them over to the police. Police reached the scene and shifted the injured to a trauma centre and Ramnagar Hospital. One young man died during treatment. The condition of the other injured remains critical. The incident took place near Padav intersection in the Mughalsarai police station area, about 23 kilometres from the district headquarters in Chandauli. 4 pictures of the accident... Now read step by step how the Scorpio created havoc on the road One dead, others in critical condition Six people injured in the collision were taken by ambulance to Lal Bahadur Shastri District Hospital. Doctors there declared cyclist Irshad Ahmad (25) dead. Four seriously injured persons were referred to the trauma centre for advanced treatment. The injured include Mohammad Islam (20), a resident of Kutban Shahid Peelikothi under Kotwali police station, Varanasi, and Salman (36), a resident of Sujabad under Ramnagar police station. After initial treatment, both were referred to Kabirchowra Divisional Hospital. Two other injured persons are yet to be identified. Police said Irshad, son of Jaleel, was a resident of Chaurhat village. He was returning home on his bicycle after buying medicine from a medical store. Irshad was unemployed and helped his father in farming. Search for car owner underway Arun Kumar Singh said the car owner has been identified through the registration number WB 02 8586. The Scorpio is registered in the name of Rakesh Yadav. The accused driver, Harish Yadav, a resident of Badi Piyari under Chowk police station in Varanasi, has been taken into custody. Police said the occupants of the vehicle were allegedly intoxicated at the time of the incident. The damaged Scorpio was removed from the spot using a crane and taken to the police post. Further investigation in the case is underway.

stories.title: Out-of-syllabus questions asked in ANM recruitment examination:Over 1,000 candidates protest in Lucknow, march towards CM’s residence
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission (UPSSSC) ANM (5272 posts) recruitment exam sparked anger among candidates in Lucknow. More than 1000 candidates protested outside the Pickup Building, alleging that questions were asked from outside the declared syllabus. They submitted a memorandum addressed to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath to the officials. Some candidates reached near the CM's residence. Gautampalli police is trying to reason with them and gathering information about their demands. 'Questions from outside the syllabus appeared in the exam held on January 11' Candidates say that the Health Worker (Female) ANM recruitment examination was conducted on January 11, 2026. Questions were asked from outside the official and declared syllabus issued by the commission. About 35 to 40 questions were included from General Knowledge (GK) and Computer subjects, while these subjects were not mentioned in the syllabus. 'Months of preparation wasted' The protesting candidates said that they had worked hard for many months according to the syllabus set by the commission. Not only did their hard work go to waste due to out-of-syllabus questions in the exam, but questions have also been raised about the fairness, transparency, and credibility of the entire recruitment process. High-level investigation demanded from Chief Minister The candidates submitted a memorandum addressed to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath to the officers. In it, they demanded that a high-level investigation be conducted into the GK and computer questions asked outside the syllabus in the UPSSSC ANM (5272) recruitment exam. Keeping in mind the future of candidates, the exam should be cancelled, and re-exam dates should be announced soon. Large crowd gathered outside pickup building During the demonstration, a large number of candidates gathered outside the pickup building, causing temporary disorder in the area. The candidates say that if their demands are not acted upon soon, they will intensify their protest. So far, no official response has come from the commission or administration on the matter, but amid growing pressure, all eyes are now fixed on the government's next move. Now read what the candidates said... Kanchan Yadav, a candidate who participated in the protest, said that the commission had given 38 topics. It was said that questions would come only from those topics. 40 questions in the exam came from outside the syllabus. We have only one demand - that the exam should be conducted again. Khushboo Pathak, a candidate from Varanasi, said that only 50 to 60 questions in the exam were from the syllabus. The remaining questions were out of the syllabus. The questions were of UPSC level. Our demand from the government is that the exam should be conducted again.

stories.title: UP Bar Council Elections begin in Agra:Voting will continue for 2 days, 4,900 advocates will exercise their vote
stories.summary: The excitement for Uttar Pradesh Bar Council elections is at its peak today. Voting for the state's largest lawyers' organization has begun today in four phases. Under the first phase, voting is underway in the Agra district on Thursday. Lawyers will exercise their voting rights to select 25 members. A total of 333 candidates are in the fray from across the state in the Uttar Pradesh Bar Council elections. Meanwhile, 11 candidates are contesting from the Agra district. The first phase of voting in Agra will be completed today and tomorrow, that is, January 16 and 17. Across the state, a total of 2,49,808 COP (Certificate of Practice) holding advocates are eligible to vote, while in the Agra district, a total of 4,900 advocates will exercise their voting rights. Voting arrangements have been made for two days at the District Court (Civil Complex) and Fatehabad Court (Bagh Badshahi) in Agra. ADJ-26 Amarjeet has been appointed as the election officer for voting at the District Court, and Civil Judge Kishan Chand Pandey has been appointed at the Fatehabad Court. At the Civil Complex, advocates practicing in Collectorate, Commissionery, Taxation, Tehsil Sadar, Kirawali, and Etmadpur are casting their votes. Uttar Pradesh Bar Council elections are being conducted in four phases. The first phase is today, January 16-17, the second phase January 20-21, the third phase January 27-28, and the final phase will be completed in Prayagraj on January 30-31. From the Agra district, Durg Vijay Singh Bhaiya, Arvind Mishra, Harjeet Arora, Saroj Yadav, Radha Yadav, Neha Gupta, Anup Sharma, Mukesh Sharma, Puran Singh Rajput, R.S. Maurya, and Tej Singh Baghel are candidates. All candidates have been visiting lawyers across 80 districts of the state for a long time, appealing for first preference votes. The nomination fee for the Uttar Pradesh Bar Council election is higher than that of the MP, MLA, and Presidential elections. Each candidate has deposited Rs 1.50 lakh as a nomination fee and Rs 25 thousand for voter lists of 80 districts with the Bar Council. During campaigning, new law books, diaries, calendars, etc., are also being distributed to lawyers. The civil court premises appear covered with banners and posters. This election is being monitored by a High Power Committee constituted by the Supreme Court. The committee is chaired by former Chief Justice of Jharkhand Justice Ravi Ranjan. Former judge of Allahabad High Court S.R. Masuri and former judge of Delhi High Court Rekha Palli are included as members. The state's election officer is former judge of Allahabad High Court Arvind Kumar Tripathi, while former judge Surendra Singh is appointed as observer. Former Chairman P.K. Singh's Appeal Former Chairman of Uttar Pradesh Bar Council, P.K. Singh, made an emotional appeal to Agra lawyers, saying that the lawyers of Agra honored him by making him a member five times and chairman once. He said that lawyers should give priority to local candidates because local members are the ones who help in times of need. P.K. Singh said that this time, 11 candidates are in the fray from Agra. Lawyers should first vote for candidates from their district in order of priority, then support outside candidates. He expressed confidence that if voting is done wisely, the number of members elected from Agra could increase.

stories.title: Protests erupt over Manikarnika Ghat dispute:Congress says, 'Kashi's heritage is being destroyed'; experts say good that PMO took cognizance
stories.summary: The alleged historical breaking of the jewel at Manikarnika Ghat in Kashi has now taken a political turn. The accusations of damaging religious sites and heritage associated with Maa Ahilyabai Holkar have further intensified the matter. Protests are happening from Kashi to Indore. On Friday, the Congress party also came forward openly. Congress officials reached the District Magistrate's office and submitted a memorandum demanding an impartial investigation of the entire matter. Party leaders say that cultural and historical heritage is being damaged in Varanasi in the name of development. BJP people destroyed age-old heritage- Ajay Rai On Friday, UP Congress president Ajay Rai spoke to the media in Delhi and levelled serious allegations over demolition being carried out in the name of Kashi heritage. He alleged that the Modi–Yogi government is engaged in completely destroying Kashi’s ancient heritage and one of the greatest legacies of Hinduism. Ajay Rai said Kashi represents the biggest heritage of Hindu religion, but the central and state governments have ruined it. He claimed that in the name of the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor, Baba Vishwanath’s courtyard has been turned into something resembling a modern mall and hundreds of ancient temples have been demolished. Referring specifically to the Akshay Vat tree, Ajay Rai said Hindu tradition considers Kashi, Gaya (Bodh Gaya) and Prayagraj as a single sacred trio. He said these places were home to thousands-of-years-old Akshay Vat trees, and Indian history speaks of three such sacred Akshay Vats. He added that even Prime Minister Narendra Modi pays obeisance to the Akshay Vat trees, and only two now remain at Gaya and the Prayagraj Sangam. The Akshay Vat in Kashi, he alleged, was completely sliced and cut down. Rai claimed the tree existed even before Baba Vishwanath and Maa Parvati came to Kashi, but it was destroyed by contractors from Gujarat. Religious places not being spared in Varanasi - Congress Congress Metropolitan President Raghavendra Chaubey said - In Prime Minister Narendra Modi's parliamentary constituency Varanasi, first hundreds of temples were demolished in the name of Kashi Vishwanath Corridor, then the Sarvaseva Sangh Ashram connected to the freedom struggle heritage was destroyed. Now in the Dalmandi area, where the livelihood of about ten thousand people is connected, demolition is being carried out. After this, allegations have now emerged about damaging religious sites, idols, and artworks built by Maa Ahilyabai Holkar at Manikarnika Ghat. Good that PMO took coznigence- Prof. A K Joshi Meanwhile, senior retired sociology professor at BHU, Dr A J Joshi, said the steps taken by the administration are part of the ghat’s mega makeover plan, but the exercise reflects a failure to learn from past mistakes and a lack of adequate groundwork before the demolition began. Notably, Dr Joshi has earlier been part of the Manikarnika Tirth Vikas Samiti that undertook the works and planning related ghat improvement. Speaking to Bhaskar English, he said the controversy forced the PMO and the local administration to come out with explanations after protests erupted. Dr Joshi added that it was reassuring the issue was addressed in time and that instructions have now been issued to reinstall the historic statues once the makeover is completed. Truth should be brought out through investigation Congress has demanded that the administration disclose the truth of the entire matter before the public. For this, a joint delegation has demanded a site inspection, which should include the district administration, local citizens, and Congress representatives. The party has warned that if action is not taken within a week, Congress members will be forced to start a relay hunger strike and then an indefinite hunger strike. State spokesperson Sanjeev Singh said - The administration should investigate the entire matter with transparency. If our heritage is not secured, Congress will not sit quietly, and the movement will be intensified. Rajeshwar Singh Patel, Raghavendra Choubey, Fasahat Hussain Babu, Sanjeev Singh, Dr. Rajesh Gupta, Satnam Singh, Ashok Singh, Dilip Choubey, Santosh Chaurasia, Hasan Mehdi Kabban, Piyush Srivastava, Khalid Siddiqui, Ramkesh Yadav, Santosh Maurya, Lokesh Singh, Manoj Verma, Manu, Rohit Dubey, and Arvind Kumar attended the program. All recovered artifacts have been preserved Meanwhile, the administration has given clarification regarding these allegations. The administration says that the first phase of construction work is ongoing, and during this time, whatever artifacts have been obtained have been safely kept in the Gurudham temple. The Culture Department is examining it, and in the future, it will be reinstalled with full reverence and respect. PMO and CMO have also taken cognizance of the matter Under the redevelopment project of Manikarnika Ghat crematorium, after a video surfaced showing the destruction of an ancient platform by a bulldozer on Tuesday, revealing the statue of Rajmata Ahilyabai Holkar and floral-leaf designs and other artworks on the steps in the debris, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) and Chief Minister's Office have taken notice of the resulting controversy. The administration has been directed to preserve heritage while pursuing development. The administration has already been saying that they will protect and reinstall the statues. Congress demands

stories.title: Brawl over 'Prabhat Pheri' in Badaun:Police–villager clash over route dispute; women injured, procession later allowed under supervision
stories.summary: A clash broke out between police and villagers in Badaun on Friday over a 'Prabhat-Pheri', leading to a tense situation and allegations of a lathi charge. The incident occurred in Byor Kasimabad, under the Islamnagar police station area. Police stopped the procession, citing a dispute over the route. This led to pushing and shoving, after which police dispersed the crowd using batons. Villagers alleged that police carried out a lathi charge in which women and youths were also injured. The situation remained tense for about an hour. On receiving information, SP Rural Dr Hridayesh Katheria and SDM Bisauli Rashi Krishna reached the spot and brought the situation under control. Later, the morning procession was taken out under police and administrative supervision. Villagers claimed they have been using the same route for the procession for the past 50 years. Know the full matter A morning procession of the Magh month was taken out in Byor Kasimabad village under the Islamnagar police station area on Friday morning. Villagers said the procession has been following the same route for nearly 50 years. However, after complaints from people of another community, police from Islamnagar reached the village around 5 am. Police attempted to stop the procession, declaring the route disputed. This led to a clash between villagers and the police. As tensions rose, police teams from Bilsi and Ughaiti were called to the spot, and a PAC unit was also deployed. The situation soon went out of control. SDM Bisauli Rashi Krishna and CO Bilsi arrived at the scene to manage the situation. Around 8 am, police resorted to a lathi charge, triggering panic in the village. Several women and young men were injured and were admitted to the community health centre for treatment. A day earlier, members of the other community had also objected to the procession and lodged complaints with the police. SP Rural convinced villagers and got the procession taken out Following the incident, heavy police deployment was made in the village to maintain law and order. After receiving information, SP Rural Dr Hridayesh Katheria reached the spot and tried to pacify the villagers. However, residents protested and demanded action against the police personnel and officials who had stopped the procession. After prolonged arguments, the police stepped back and allowed the morning procession to proceed under police and administrative supervision. Even after the procession concluded, families of the injured women and youths continued to press for action against those responsible. SP Rural Dr Hridayesh Katheria said the procession was initially stopped due to opposition from some people. Later, it was found that the procession had been using the same route for many years. After this, the procession was allowed to proceed safely. He added that there would be no restriction on the morning procession in the future and villagers had been informed accordingly. Villagers took out procession through old route According to villagers, the Prabhat Pheri has been taken out in the village for several decades. They said that about ten years ago, during the SP government, the route was changed following objections from a particular community. This time, when villagers resumed the procession on the old route, members of that community objected again and informed the police, leading to the confrontation.

stories.title: UP government boosts sports with basketball event launch:CM Yogi highlights sports jobs, rewards, and pushes for Olympics culture across UP universities
stories.summary: Yogi played basketball in Gorakhpur. Like players, he bounced the ball twice on the basketball court, then tossed it into the basket. Along with this, the CM inaugurated the inter-university women's basketball tournament. The CM also got acquainted with the players and released gas balloons in the sky. The CM said- Before 2014, sports competitions were not on the government's agenda. Players either migrated or sat frustrated and discouraged. Today we are conducting sports competitions in every village. All the means of life can only be obtained through a healthy body. A healthy body will only exist when it remains in discipline and restraint. The women's basketball tournament at Deendayal Upadhyay Gorakhpur University will be held from January 15 to 19. A total of 31 university teams from 14 states of the eastern region are participating in it. Read CM Yogi's 4 major points- 1- We have given jobs to more than 500 athletes CM Yogi said - We are building sports grounds in every gram panchayat in UP. Now, not only does the Government of India give awards to athletes who win medals in the Olympics, Commonwealth, and Asian Games, but state governments also give awards. So far, we have provided jobs to more than 500 athletes in different departments of the state. Deputy SP, Tehsildar, and Regional Sports Officer - 6 posts are being given directly to players. Sports activities should not just be a foundation, it should not remain just a formality, but should become part of daily routine. For this, more than 96 thousand sports kits have been given to youth clubs and women's clubs in the state. 2- All universities should prepare players Yogi said - I appeal to all universities to adopt at least one sport and prepare players for it. Develop healthy competition. If this happens, youth will stay away from drugs and all kinds of perversions. When youth play, they prosper. The state's first Sports University has been built in Meerut. The Chauri-Chaura incident in the freedom movement, which shook the foreign rule, was also connected to the land of Gorakhpur. This was the workplace of Munshi Premchand. 3- Government gives 6 crore rupees to gold medal winners Today, many families have made sports a part of their lives. Parents no longer discriminate between sons and daughters. When a player from UP qualifies for the Olympics, we provide them with Rs 10 lakh assistance and a sports kit. If they win a gold medal, the government gives Rs 6 crore for individual sports, along with a Class-1 job. For team games, the government gives Rs 3 crore for a gold medal. Silver medal winners receive Rs 3 crore for individual sports and Rs 1.5 crore for team games. Similar incentive amounts are given for bronze medals as well. 4- We wish for the 2036 Olympics to be held in India Whenever any Indian team goes anywhere, they receive all kinds of encouragement from the Prime Minister. When they return victorious, he personally meets everyone. We need to start preparing from today for the Commonwealth Games in India in 2030. Under PM Modi's leadership, we all wish for the 2036 Olympics to be held in India. We also hope that Indian athletes will win the maximum number of medals.

stories.title: Jeweler commits suicide in Lucknow:Body found hanging in courtyard, victim depressed over rising Gold and Silver prices
stories.summary: A jeweller in the Lucknow Chowk area committed suicide by hanging. He was depressed due to rising gold and silver prices. He was found hanging in the courtyard of his house. Police have sent the body for a post-mortem. Manoj Agarwal, a resident of Chauptiya, worked with silver. He had a shop in Kundan Market near Hari Masjid in Chowk Sarrafa Market. On Thursday, he was at the shop in the afternoon. He participated in the Makar Sankranti feast happening in Chowk. After that, he closed the shop and went home. At night, he was found hanging from a grill in the house's courtyard. Gold-silver should be freed from futures trading When family members saw him hanging, they started screaming. Hearing the screams, nearby people gathered. After this, the police were informed. Police arrived at the scene, took possession of the body, and sent it for post-mortem. Investigation reveals depression due to continuous fluctuation in gold-silver prices. Currently, police are investigating the matter. Chowk Sarafa Association General Secretary Vinod Maheshwari said that due to a price surge in the jewelry trade, he committed suicide by hanging due to depression. There is a demand from the Government of India to free silver-gold from futures trading. Artisan traders from Rajkot, Agra, Kanpur, and Lucknow are on the verge of ruin.

stories.title: Young man commits suicide by shooting himself in Lucknow:Cheated millions in the name of government job, took money from roommate also
stories.summary: A young man who cheated millions in the name of government jobs in Lucknow committed suicide by shooting himself. His blood-soaked body was found in a rented room. When his roommate arrived there, the door was locked from inside. When the police arrived at the information and broke down the door, his blood-soaked body was lying on the bed. When the shawl was removed, blood was flowing from his chest. A revolver was lying nearby. Police sent the body for a post-mortem. The incident took place around 8 PM on Thursday in Vikas Nagar Sector-L. Pradyuman Pathak was a resident of Jaunpur. In a preliminary police investigation, it has come to light that the young man had taken lakhs of rupees from many people in the name of getting government jobs. He had also taken money from his roommate in the name of getting a police job. Now people were asking for their money back. Shot in the chest, revolver found lying nearby Police said that in the evening, they received information on Dial 112 that a person had locked himself in a room in Sector L, Vikasnagar. Upon receiving the information, Vikasnagar police station immediately reached the spot. When the police team broke down the door and went inside, the young man was lying unconscious on the bed. Blood was coming out of his chest. An illegal revolver was lying nearby. He was immediately sent to the hospital for treatment, where doctors declared him dead. During police interrogation, it was revealed that Pradyuman previously lived in Mumbai. He had taken money from many people by claiming to influence government administration and promising government jobs. He had also taken about one and a half lakh rupees from his roommate, Divyanshu, for getting him a job in the police department. ACP said - CDR investigation will be done ACP Ghazipur Anidya Vikram Singh said that important evidence, including a revolver, mobile phone, has been seized from the crime scene. Call details will be obtained and investigated. The deceased was married and had a wife and a child. Further action will be taken after the arrival of family members. Roommate said - Called out, poured water from window Roommate Divyanshu said - I had been living with Pradyuman for 2 months. I had gone to Gomti Nagar's Patrakar Puram for some work. When I returned, the room was locked from inside. Knocked on the door for a long time. Called also, but got no response from inside. Then poured water towards Pradyuman's bed from the window, but there was no movement. After this, the police were informed. Pradyuman had taken money from many people in the name of providing government jobs. He would receive calls from creditors from morning to evening. People were asking for their money back when they didn't get jobs. He had been under stress for many days due to this matter.

stories.title: Fog returns in UP, eight accidents, 24 vehicles collide:Schools shut in 5 districts; rain alert from tomorrow
stories.summary: The weather has changed again in Uttar Pradesh, with intense cold and dense fog gripping large parts of the state. On Friday morning, thick fog covered at least 35 districts, including Lucknow and Barabanki. In many areas, visibility dropped to near zero, severely affecting road traffic. Schools of the 5 districts till 8th class will remain close till January 17. Due to poor visibility, 8 major accidents were reported across the state in a single day. As many as 24 vehicles collided at different locations. One person lost his life, while around 40 others were injured. Details of accidents reported from different districts: Why did the weather change? Find out Now, know the condition of cities- Lucknow: Fog appeared this morning after a week. The icy winds have increased the chill. There are chances of rain from tomorrow (January 17). On Thursday, the maximum temperature was 20.7°C and the minimum temperature was 5.5°C. This is 1.6 degrees below normal. Gorakhpur: Light fog and bitter cold were observed in Gorakhpur. The cold was so severe that people were seen taking refuge in bonfires and thick woolen clothes. Meteorologists have warned of dense fog for 2-3 more days. Due to fog, 22 trains are running late by 2 to 15 hours. Aligarh: Dense fog has enveloped Aligarh. Visibility dropped to just 10 meters. A cold wave moving at a speed of 8 km per hour increased the chill. The minimum temperature was recorded at 6 degrees and the maximum at 18 degrees. AQI was recorded at 207. Kanpur: Some areas experienced dense fog while others had light fog. People were seen shivering from the piercing cold. Cold winds increased people's difficulties further. Visibility remained low on Friday morning compared to the last six days. The minimum temperature was recorded at 9 °C. Weather experts say that the cold will continue to trouble for a few more days. Saharanpur: Dense fog prevailed in the morning. Visibility remained zero. The minimum temperature was recorded at 3°C and the maximum temperature at 12°C. AQI is 360. According to the meteorological department, fluctuations in the weather will be seen till January 20. Meerut: There was dense fog in the morning. Vehicle drivers faced difficulty on the road due to the visibility being 50 meters. The minimum temperature was recorded at 5.1 degrees. The sun is expected to come out during the day today. Agra: There was relief from fog, but icy winds increased the chill. Morning temperature remained at 6 °C. Many trains, including New Delhi-Khajuraho Vande Bharat and New Delhi-Bhopal Shatabdi, were delayed due to fog. AQI was recorded at 322 on Friday morning. According to the weather department, there may be fog on January 17 and light rain on January 18-19. Etawah: Fog knocked again after 7 days. Dense fog enveloped early in the morning, which severely reduced visibility. Due to fog, the city's historic Victoria Hall also became invisible. The minimum temperature in the morning dropped to 5 degrees Celsius, which affected rail and road traffic. Farrukhabad: The severe cold continues. The sun had been shining for a week, but now fog has been setting in for two days, which has increased the cold further. Fog remained since Friday morning, and visibility was around 30 meters. The minimum temperature was recorded at 7 degrees and the maximum temperature at 22 degrees. Farmers say that fog is beneficial for the wheat crop. Know how the weather will be for the next three days
