stories.title: Dhirendra Shastri makes tea in shop, :Completes Kamdagiri Parikrama in Chitrakoot; to begin 'Katha' in Banda for 5 days
stories.summary: Bageshwar Dham’s Peethadheeshwar, Pandit Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, will narrate the Hanumant Katha for five days starting today in Banda. The event, continuing until January 20, has been fully prepared, with the katha pandal set 300 meters from his 5-star hotel stay. Earlier, Shastri performed a parikrama of Lord Kamdagiri in Chitrakoot, visiting temples and meeting devotees, who offered flowers and sought blessings, while children presented him with their artwork. Visited Hanuman Temple, made tea himself, Kamdagiri Maha-aarti During the circumambulation, Dhirendra Krishna Shastri reached the Hanuman temple in Bahra. Here, after darshan and worship, he made and drank tea with his own hands. During this time, a crowd of devotees gathered, and people appeared excited to catch a glimpse of him. After this, he reached the Kamdagiri Maha-aarti site, where he performed the proper aarti of Lord Kamdagiri mountain. The priests who performed the aarti were given offerings. He also gave money as prasad to children standing nearby. Circumambulation completed in 1 hour 20 minutes Dhirendra Krishna Shastri completed the Kamadgiri circumambulation in about 1 hour and 20 minutes. After the circumambulation, he said that it was his good fortune to get the opportunity to circumambulate Kamadgiri. He mentioned that this is not the first time he has visited Chitrakoot, many times, and Bageshwar Dham has a special spiritual connection with Chitrakoot. Gave message of peace and love Pandit Dhirendra Krishna Shastri said the Bageshwar family promotes peace, love, and harmony, appealing to all communities to aid India’s development. He will deliver his first discourse in Bundelkhand on Friday in Banda, discussing social issues and personal guidance. On marriage, he said he will wed soon, urging people to live simply and naturally. After completing the Kamdagiri parikrama, he rested at Arogyadham, while devotees’ enthusiasm remained high late into the night. No VIP facility in the pandal It should be noted that under the guidance of BJP leader and Bundelkhand Youth Foundation founder Praveen Singh, the katha will begin today at Mawai Bypass ground, about 4 km from the city. A waterproof and fire safety-proof pandal has been set up using German hangar technology across 125 bighas for the katha. The pandal has seating arrangements for 50,000 devotees at once. The special thing is that there is no VIP facility in the pandal. All people will sit on the same carpet on the ground. A divine darbar will be held on January 18. See the pillar-less pandal The pandal is water and fire proof Praveen Singh said - The specialty of the pandal is that there is no pillar in its center, allowing thousands of devotees to have a direct view of the Vyaspeetha without any obstruction. This structure is completely waterproof and fire-resistant. Made of aluminum and high-quality synthetic fabric, the pandal is capable of withstanding strong winds and rain. Due to the increased height and modern design of the pandal, ventilation will remain even during crowding. This will prevent devotees from feeling suffocated. The pandal has been divided into 4 rows ABCD. In A, the organizing committee and other VIP guests will sit on the ground to listen to the katha. B is reserved for women coming as special guests. The C row will have a media gathering. And in D, all devotees will sit. Stage decorated with 50 kg flowers A grand stage has been prepared for Pt. Dhirendra Shastri in the pandal. A large picture of Lord Hanuman is placed on the backdrop. A sofa has been placed in front for Dhirendra Shastri. The stage has been decorated with 50 kg of flowers. The katha will start at 1 PM and continue till 5 PM in the evening. Bhandara will run for 24 hours Another pandal has been set up next to this one, where arrangements for 24-hour bhandara (food service) have been made for all devotees. The bhandara includes puri-sabzi and sweets. Additionally, accommodation arrangements have been made for devotees coming from outside. Entry will be with coconut and Hanuman Chalisa Devotees coming to listen to Pt. Dhirendra Shastri's discourse must bring a coconut and the Shri Hanuman Chalisa book. Entry to the pandal will be allowed only with these items. The entry for the discourse will be free for all devotees. Divine Court will be held on 18th During Pt. Dhirendra Shastri's discourse, a Divine Court will also be set up on January 18th. Here, devotees' slips will be drawn. The Divine Court will be set up within the discourse pandal itself. More than three thousand personnel deployed for security For the 5-day katha, around 600 police personnel from Banda as well as Hamirpur, Mahoba, and Chitrakoot, 2500 volunteers, and 200 Akhand Hind Force jawans have been deployed. These include 120 SHOs, 247 sub-inspectors, and the rest are constables. Grand Kalash Yatra taken out before the katha A grand Kalash Yatra was taken out on January 15 before the Hanumant Katha by Bageshwar Dham's Peethadheeshwar Acharya Dhirendra Krishna Shastri. 50 thousand devotees participated in it, with women being in the majority. Chants of 'Jai Shri Ram' continued during the Kalash Yatra that proceeded with music and drums. The Kalash Yatra started from Ramlila Ground and concluded at Rifle Club Ground after passing through major city roads. The 1-kilometer-long journey was joined by MLA Prakash Dwivedi from Banda Sadar. Flowers were showered from drones during the yatra.

stories.title: Mulayam Singh isolated as Mayawati claims CM seat:'Kacchi Chhori' pulled Mulayam's chair; how UP politics changed in 12 hours
stories.summary: In politics, there are days that determine decades of the future. This story is from an era when power was based not on sharing but on bargaining. On one side, Mulayam Singh saw power as a ladder; on the other side, Kanshi Ram saw it as the key to movement. In between was Mayawati, who was first kept away, then controlled, and finally, attempts were made to eliminate her. In today's 'Political Arena', read the story of when a guest house became a battlefield and one night changed UP politics forever... October 1993, Ashoka Hotel Delhi. Room number 324, there was intense activity in the corridor outside. This room belonged to industrialist Jayant Malhotra. Two political veterans were sitting face to face in the room, Mulayam Singh Yadav and Kanshi Ram. Industrialist Sanjay Dalmia was also present. Placing a glass on the table, Dalmia said- "Mulayam ji, the enemy is big. If we fight alone, the BJP's chariot will crush everyone." Mulayam Singh looked at Kanshi Ram with his small eyes and said, "If the enemy is one, there's no harm in joining hands. But the seats...?" A mysterious smile appeared on Kanshi Ram's face. Then he said- "Mulayam ji, I'm not hungry for seats. I'm searching for that 'master key' that will unlock the fate of Dalits. You contest the election, we will support you." Malhotra smilingly interrupted- "This alliance is necessary for the country's soft landing, Kanshi Ram ji. The gap between the rich and the poor has become too wide." Samajwadi Party (SP) and Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) were now in the same camp. Prime Minister Narasimha Rao had also given his blessing from behind the curtain. The strange thing was that Kanshi Ram had kept his most fierce disciple, Mayawati, away from this entire conversation. A close worker asked Kanshi Ram in a hushed voice- "Sir, didn't you call Behenji? She might feel bad." Kanshiram said in a low voice, "Mayawati has a fierce temperament. She could have broken the delicate thread of negotiation. It's better to keep her away for now." Mayawati was restricted to western UP. When the results came, there was an earthquake in the political corridors from Delhi to Lucknow. The combination of Mandal and Dalit politics had slowed down the pace of Hindutva's chariot. BJP was the largest party with 177 seats, but far from a majority. Meanwhile, SP got 109 seats, and BSP got 67 seats. This alliance was also well behind the magical number for a majority (212), but formed the government with support from Congress (28) and Janata Dal (27). Kanshiram's 10-year-old party was about to write the destiny of the country's largest state. Kanshi Ram had grabbed a part of the 'master key', but a question was still floating in the air - was this friendship out of 'compulsion' or 'necessity'...? Mulayam Singh Yadav was about to sit on the Chief Minister's chair for the first time. Out of 27 ministers, 11 were from the BSP. Kanshi Ram looked at Mayawati- "You will not join the government. You have to keep a check on the government." There was a different sparkle in Mayawati's eyes- "Don't worry, sir. The government will run on BSP's agenda. Not a single file will pass without my scrutiny." December 1993, that afternoon, Lucknow's streets were jammed. A new song was echoing in the air, which was written by a former associate of Indira Gandhi's close tantric Chandraswami, specifically at Mulayam Singh's request. Its lyrics were- "Brave Mulayam all around, Kanshi Ram's power has taken hold..." Mulayam himself had said- "The vehicle will only move forward when Kanshi Ram ji's name is in the song. It's important to keep the partner happy." This was a union of two different worlds. On one side were SP's aggressive and noisy supporters, who were dancing intoxicated with victory. On the other side were BSP people - quiet, intimidated, but with an amazing sparkle in their eyes. Even in Lucknow's harsh winter, many of them were barefoot. The foundation of this alliance rested on three different ideologies, which were merely tolerating each other. For Kanshiram, this alliance was a laboratory. He did not particularly like Mulayam's legacy. Kanshiram was confident that this UP experiment would create a stir across the country. He looked at Mayawati with a smile- "Now I will set out to tour the whole country. The command of Lucknow is in your hands. You will handle it, right...?" Mayawati assured him, saying, "Don't worry, sir. Lucknow will be in my fist." But Mulayam Singh Yadav was a seasoned player. He was called the 'wrestler' of politics. For him, this alliance was just a ladder to power. Mulayam quietly told his close associates, "Kanshiram and this girl are still raw." 'Girl' meaning Mayawati... Another move was playing out in his mind. He was confident that if not today, then tomorrow, he would break BSP's MLAs and merge them into his party and swallow Kanshi Ram's entire group. But a new echo began to be heard in the corridors of the secretariat. Mulayam Singh was certainly sitting in the Chief Minister's chair, but someone else had the real influence. Kanshi Ram had deliberately distanced himself from Uttar Pradesh affairs. He understood that his disciple was now ready to take flight. A new name emerged in newspaper headlines - "Super CM..." A journalist asked Mayawati, "Behenji, people have started calling you Super CM. Is this true?" A stern but satisfied smile appeared on Mayawati's face. She said - "The public is saying what they are seeing. BSP is the backbone of this government, and the backbone determines how the body will function." The Mandal Commission report was the adhesive between both parties. She also played the reservation card in the hilly regions of Uttarakhand. BJP and Congress leaders were left squirming - "Backward castes in the mountains are only two percent. Reservation politics there is madness." Mulayam Singh replied with his familiar smile - "We are concerned with social justice, not percentages." This alliance proved to be a lottery for Mayawati. After the defeat in 1991, Parliament seemed distant to her, but in January 1994, she was elected as a Rajya Sabha member. A supporter congratulated her, saying- "Behenji, now you will roar again in Parliament." Mayawati replied in a cold tone - "Parliament is fine, but now the real power is in Lucknow. I have to hoist BSP's flag in every district of UP." Meanwhile, the media started publishing reports that a 'cold war' had begun between Mulayam and Mayawati. Mayawati immediately took charge. In a press conference, she said- "This Manuwadi media is dancing to the BJP's tunes. There is no rift between Mulayam Singh ji. This is a conspiracy to create division." The journalist asked, "But Congress and Janata Dal are giving you unconditional support, are you calling them casteist too?" Mayawati slammed her hand on the table and said- "Supporting us is their compulsion, not a favor. Without us, they couldn't have stopped the BJP. BJP was dreaming of capturing the whole country; we have jammed the wheels of their chariot." Meanwhile, a new phrase had started circulating in the UP Secretariat - 'Behenji's order.' Mayawati liked being called the Super CM, and she proved it, too. She would often boldly say- "I don't discuss with the Chief Minister; sometimes I even give him directions." Mulayam Singh grew increasingly uneasy with Mayawati’s assertive leadership. Her demands, especially on Dalit atrocities, highlighted the coalition’s failures in social justice. Despite official mediation by PL Punia, tensions rose as backward caste violence against Dalits surged. Kanshi Ram further humiliated Mulayam Singh publicly, forcing him to wait while he appeared informally, underscoring the power struggle within the coalition. Mulayam Singh was swallowing this insult like poison. He didn't make any noise about it publicly, but internally, he started working on a dangerous plan. Mulayam Singh had realized that a direct fight would not work. He started reaching out to those old BSP veterans who were burning with jealousy over Mayawati's rising stature. The names that emerged were Dr. Masood Ahmad, Jung Bahadur Patel, and Raj Bahadur. Mulayam Singh sent his pawns - "Why are you wasting your political career behind Behenji? Come with us, you'll get both respect and power." This move of Mulayam proved successful. BSP's organization started cracking from within. MLAs were ready to defect. Kanshi Ram and Mayawati felt they were making Mulayam bend, but they didn't know that Mulayam was pulling their own ground from under their feet. The panchayat elections held in early 1995 came as a shock to Kanshi Ram and Mayawati. Mulayam Singh's SP captured 30 out of 50 districts. Congress and the BJP also grabbed some seats, but the BSP got only one district. In the intoxication of his victory, Mulayam Singh was forgetting a very big equation - the friendship between Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Kanshi Ram. When Kanshi Ram reached Parliament in 1991, Vajpayee was among the first major leaders who extended a hand of friendship. One evening, a tea session was going on at Vajpayee's bungalow. Kanshiram was sitting across. Vajpayee said with a gentle smile- "Kanshiram ji, there are no enemies in politics, only possibilities." Kanshiram replied, "Atal ji, we are in search of that master key which will unlock the fate of Dalits." Vajpayee's discerning eyes had sensed that if the BJP wanted to cross the threshold of power again in UP, Dalit support was necessary. RSS chief Rajendra Singh (Rajju Bhaiya) also endorsed this. Mulayam Singh was convinced that Hindutva and Bahujan ideology could never unite. He was confident, unaware that the death warrant of his government had already been written in Atal Bihari Vajpayee's drawing room. The summer of 1995 brought fire to Lucknow. Kanshi Ram was in a hospital bed. Old diabetes and high blood pressure had broken his body, but his mind was still working like electricity. The presence of industrialist Jayant Malhotra in that white hospital room was proof that a big game was about to unfold. Kanshi Ram played the card of his old friendship with Vajpayee. Vajpayee convinced Advani and Kalyan Singh on a plan that would pull the carpet from under Mulayam Singh's feet. Surprisingly, Mayawati had no inkling of this until the last moment. Kanshi Ram called Mayawati to the hospital. There were tears in Mayawati's eyes. Holding Kanshi Ram's hand, she said- "Sir, what will happen to us if something happens to you? Who will handle this movement?" Kanshiram signaled the nurse to go out and asked in a low voice, "Would you like to become Chief Minister?" Mayawati was stunned. She thought 'Saheb' was delirious in his illness. Kanshiram slid a bundle of files towards her and said- "Take these and go straight to the Governor. He will administer the oath to you." Afternoon of June 1, 1995 After Mayawati withdrew support and met Governor Motilal Vora, Mulayam Singh was left furious and shaken. On June 2, SP supporters stormed the State Guest House, assaulting BSP MLAs and forcing some to sign blank papers under threat. As chaos spread, several MLAs were abducted, while Mayawati and her aides barricaded themselves inside room number 1, narrowly escaping the violence. On June 2, SP supporters stormed the State Guest House, threatening Mayawati, cutting electricity and phones, and creating chaos. Brave police officers Vijay Bhushan and Subhash Singh protected her until District Magistrate Rajeev Kher arrived to disperse the crowd. The ordeal steeled Mayawati’s resolve, earning her the title “Iron Lady.” The next day, June 3, Governor Motilal Vora administered her oath as Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, making her the first Dalit woman to lead the state. June 19 Assembly Speaker Dhaniram Verma declared the Governor’s removal of the Mulayam government unconstitutional and adjourned the house. SP MLAs walked out, but the remaining 275 members supported Mayawati. With Congress, BJP, Janata Dal, and rebel SP MLAs backing her, Mulayam Singh Yadav was isolated. Mayawati proved her majority, taking charge with determination, and emerged as the “Iron Lady” of Lucknow, marking a historic political victory. *** References Behenji: A Political Biography of Mayawati Kindle Edition - Ajoy Bose | Crime, Grime Gumption: Case Files of an IPS Officer - O.P. Singh | My Struggle-filled Life and the Journey of Bahujan Movement - Mayawati | Contemporary editions of Maya Magazine, India Today. stories.title: UP leaders actively participate in Maharashtra civic polls:About 30 lakh UP-origin voters impact results; Samajwadi Party fields candidates in high-density migrant areas
stories.summary: Leaders from UP made their presence felt in Maharashtra's civic elections, especially leaders from eastern UP, who campaigned extensively. The reason was that there are about 30 lakh voters from UP there. To attract these voters, many prominent leaders camped in Mumbai for several days. Voting was completed yesterday, and the results will come today. Which UP leaders reached Maharashtra? How much influence do UP people have in Maharashtra elections? Why were leaders from Azamgarh and Jaunpur so active? Read the full report... First know how important Maharashtra's local election is Jafar Azmi from Azamgarh, UP, who is active in Mumbai elections, says - There are 227 seats under BMC. Out of these, 70 seats are where people from eastern UP and Bihar live in large numbers. Samajwadi Party has fielded its candidates on all these 70 seats. Azmi says - BMC is the richest civic body. Its annual budget is 70 thousand crore rupees. In such a situation, everyone desires to become a BMC corporator (councilor). Here, generally, a candidate getting 12 to 15 thousand votes also becomes a corporator. There are several seats here where the population of people from eastern UP and Bihar is up to 30 percent. These include districts like Bhiwandi, Malat, Andheri, and Kurla. Besides, a large number of people also live in the Mumbra area of Thane. This is why UP leaders have arrived in Maharashtra in large numbers for campaigning. Tussle... There was also competition to show dominance During the Maharashtra local body elections, Purvanchal's strongman leader Dhananjay Singh was seen wearing the BJP's badge. While in UP, he raises JDU's flag. Meanwhile, Samajwadi Party leader Abu Asim Azmi had called leaders from Azamgarh and surrounding districts in large numbers for party campaigning. During the campaign, there were sharp exchanges, taunts, and even instances of abuse. While addressing a meeting, Abu Asim Azmi challenged MIM leader Imtiaz Jaleel, saying 'I am from Uttar Pradesh, I will throw you down and your teeth will come out. You're going around boasting about having one MP. I have 37 MPs.' In the Maharashtra election, SP's firebrand leader and Machhlishahr MLA Ragini Sonkar, Leader of Opposition in Assembly Mata Prasad Pandey, Machhlishahr MP Priya Saroj, Kaushambi MP Pushpendra Saroj, Azamgarh MP Dharmendra Yadav, Jaunpur MP Babu Singh Kushwaha, Basti MP Ram Prasad Chaudhary, Ambedkar Nagar MLA Ram Achal Rajbhar, SP MLA Nafis Ahmad and other such leaders arrived for campaigning. Aparna Yadav also arrived for campaigning Mulayam Singh Yadav's daughter-in-law and BJP leader and Women's Commission Vice President Aparna Yadav also reached Mumbai to campaign for the BMC elections. In addition to her, BJP leaders, including Ramesh Mishra, MLA from Badlapur seat of Jaunpur district, and Ramesh Jaiswal, MLA from Mughalsarai seat of Chandauli, also reached Mumbai for campaigning. Why did Dhananjay Singh have to go to Maharashtra? Dhananjay Singh has been involved in Purvanchal politics, but this is the first time he has gone to Mumbai to campaign for the BJP and Shinde alliance leader. While Dhananjay Singh is a leader of Janata Dal United in Maharashtra, he appeared completely colored in saffron. He was also wearing a BJP band around his neck. Questions are also being raised about why Dhananjay had to enter the field despite Kripahankar Singh, one of Jaunpur's major leaders who had considerable influence in Mumbai politics. Kripahankar Singh is a senior BJP leader. He was also the BJP's candidate from Jaunpur in the last Lok Sabha elections. Dhananjay had also supported him. Why are only people from Azamgarh and Jaunpur so active? Moazzam, who has been living in Mumbai for a long time, told Dainik Bhaskar that people from two main districts of Purvanchal - Azamgarh and Jaunpur live in Mumbai in large numbers. There are many who have even built their houses and properties there. Moazzam says - Purvanchal voters have a good influence in BMC elections. They determine the win-loss on many seats. This is why big leaders from Azamgarh and Jaunpur came here to campaign in this election. Samajwadi Party Maharashtra State Chief General Secretary Meraj Siddiqui says - People from Eastern UP, or let's say North Indians, live in Mumbai in large numbers. There are many areas where it doesn't even feel like it's outside UP. According to Meraj, a large number of people from UP also contested in this election. However, when it comes to elections, we cannot ignore the conflict between the people of UP and Maharashtra. Sometimes opposition is also seen in terms of language. Maharashtra people allege that UP people are taking away their jobs. Senior journalist Anand Rai says - The opposition to North Indians in Maharashtra began during Bala Saheb Thackeray's era. However, his opposition was based on the argument that people from UP and Gujarat were taking away the rights of Maharashtra's people. His opposition continued in a very logical manner. But when Raj Thackeray's era came, he took an aggressive stance against North Indians. As a result, North Indians became organized wherever they lived across Maharashtra. A formal organization of North Indians was also formed. People from districts like Azamgarh, Jaunpur, Gorakhpur, Basti, and Gonda remained active in it. This was the reason why the influence of North Indians kept growing there. Whether it was the BMC election or the assembly election. People from here started going to create an atmosphere in favor of candidates contesting elections there.

stories.title: Minister Mannu Kori tries to touch commissioner’s feet in Lalitpur:During overbridge inspection visit officer stops him from doing so; folds his hands, as MLA and district officials began to smile
stories.summary: UP Minister of State Manohar Lal Panth tried to touch the feet of Jhansi Division Commissioner Vimal Kumar Dubey on Thursday. Seeing this, the Commissioner stopped him and folded both his hands. Commissioner Vimal Kumar Dubey had gone to inspect an under-construction overbridge in Lalitpur. Minister Panth arrived with a large garland to welcome Commissioner Dubey. The minister stepped forward to put on the garland, but the Commissioner put it on him instead. After this, the minister bent down to touch his feet. His hands had just reached his knees when the Commissioner stopped him and folded his hands. Seeing this unique relationship between the minister and officer, Sadar MLA Ram Ratan Kushwaha, DM Satya Prakash, and everyone present there started smiling. The minister and the commissioner were also seen smiling. Actually, on Thursday morning, Jhansi Division Commissioner Vimal Kumar Dubey arrived at Kelgunwa intersection on NH-44 to inspect the under-construction overbridge. Around 11:30, when the Commissioner arrived, State Minister Manohar Lal Panth and Sadar MLA Ramratan Kushwaha were also present there. The State Minister first garlanded the Sadar MLA. A little later, when the Commissioner arrived with DM Satyaprakash and SP Mohammad Mushtaq, the State Minister tried to garland him. The Commissioner took the garland and instead put it on the State Minister. After this, the State Minister attempted to touch his feet. DM said - Will soon be opened for traffic DM Satya Prakash said - The work on one lane of the bridge is almost complete. It will soon be opened for traffic. A little work is remaining, which will be completed by this evening, if not, then definitely by tomorrow. Traffic will be opened on one side of the bridge either tomorrow or day after. It will be made available to the public. Commissioner praised the State Minister and DM Commissioner Vimal Kumar Dubey said - This was one of our pending projects, which was causing a lot of inconvenience to people. The District Magistrate took cognizance of this. After that, I conducted an inspection. I congratulate the NHAI officers; they fulfilled what they had promised. Public representatives and the Minister also conducted regular visits. The DM remained continuously active. He had deployed his entire team. This is a big New Year's gift being given to the public. The bridge will be opened in a day or two.

stories.title: Where are Shah Jahan and Mumtaz actually buried?:Real graves lie 22 feet below Taj Mahal's main dome, entry barred
stories.summary: One of the world's most beautiful buildings, the Taj Mahal's true identity comes from its marble stones, unique inlay work with colored pearls, and beautiful architecture. Even today, these all appear to narrate the story of Shah Jahan and Mumtaz. The tombs of Shah Jahan and Mumtaz, located in the center of the main dome, are a testament to this. But do you know that these are not the real tombs of Shah Jahan and Mumtaz? Don't be surprised, the tombs that millions of tourists see every day while remembering the immortal love story are fake tombs. Actually, the real tombs are in a rectangular basement 22.2 feet deep, which is directly below the fake tombs. Dainik Bhaskar shows you through our camera the path to the real tombs and their current condition... 2 graves visible after descending 22 feet Mughal emperor Shah Jahan's 371st Urs (birthday) celebration has begun. On Thursday, ASI officials descended 22 feet into the basement at the Taj Mahal. Shah Jahan-Mumtaz's real graves were opened. After this, the Urs began with the ritual of Ghusl (applying sandalwood paste on the graves). Here lie the real graves of Shah Jahan and Mumtaz, which are in the basement below the main dome. This basement is beneath fake graves; its path also goes down through stairs in front of fake graves, which remains covered with a grating. No one can go here. During Urs, this grating was opened, and our team reached the basement after descending 21 stairs in the darkness. The real graves of Shah Jahan-Mumtaz were visible in front. Mumtaz's grave was not decorated, colored pearls were embedded on Shah Jahan's grave This basement is usually closed, but ASI employees occasionally open it for cleaning or other repair work. The basement remains closed for tourists; no one can come and go here. There is also no ventilation arrangement here, so it remains quite humid. Between the marble walls in this basement are only the real tombs of Shah Jahan-Mumtaz; nothing else is in this basement. There is no carving on its walls either. There is no decoration on Mumtaz's tomb here, whereas Shah Jahan's tomb is decorated, and it is studded with colorful pearls. Shah Jahan's tomb is 0.12 meters taller than Mumtaz's tomb. Fake decorated tombs made for tourists The height of the main dome of the Taj Mahal is 73 meters. The beautiful marble-carved tombs visible in the main hall are the fake tombs (cenotaphs) of Shah Jahan and Mumtaz Mahal. These tombs are built above the real tombs, and tourists can see them.

stories.title: Satua Baba owns ₹50 cr ashram, luxury cars:Brother was murdered; how CM Yogi's favourite saint Santosh Tiwari turned into 'Jagadguru'
stories.summary: Yellow attire, luxury vehicles like the Land Rover Defender and Porsche Turbo, worth crores for travelling. Branded sunglasses like Ray-Ban on the eyes. Someone who is often praised by UP CM Yogi. We are talking about Santosh Tiwari, who emerged from the small village of Masaura in Lalitpur, Bundelkhand. Santosh Tiwari is none other than Satua Baba, who has been making headlines in the Magh Mela. The elder brother who showed Satua Baba the path of spirituality 26 years ago is no longer in this world. He has been murdered. How did Santosh Tiwari reach Banaras? When did the family learn about him becoming a monk? Why did his mother insist on taking her last breath in his ashram? Read the untold stories of Satua Baba's life... Masaura village is located just 6 km away from the Lalitpur district headquarters, adjacent to National Highway-44. Santosh Tiwari alias Satua Baba is the youngest of 4 children of Shobharam Tiwari and his wife Raja Beti Tiwari, who live here. The eldest is Mahesh Tiwari, followed by Neeraj and Umesh Tiwari. Mahesh Tiwari is no longer in this world. He was murdered in 2007. Mahesh was the person who took Santosh Tiwari from Lalitpur to the Banaras ashram. Went to study in Banaras at age 13 Santosh Tiwari, alias Satua Baba's elder brother, Umesh Tiwari told Dainik Bhaskar that this was in the year 2000. He had passed 9th grade. At that time, he was barely 13 years old. Instead of regular studies, Santosh wanted to pursue spiritual education. So our elder brother, Mahesh Tiwari, took him to Manikarnika Ghat in Banaras. Bathed in the Ganges there. Nearby was the Satua Ashram. Here, too, there was a facility for Vedic Gurukul education. Santosh told his elder brother to get him admitted to this ashram. After this, they took Santosh to Satua Ashram. There, they met the head priest, Yamunacharya Maharaj of the ashram. He handed over his younger brother to him and said that from today, he is under your protection. Other children like him were also staying in the ashram to study. Santosh became one of the favorite disciples of the Mahant Umesh Tiwari recalls that Santosh Tiwari joined an ashram for studies and often came home during holidays. He quickly learned religious texts and became a favourite disciple of the Mahant. Around 2005, Santosh casually informed the family that he was taking sannyasa, which they initially dismissed as a joke. Days later, priests from Varanasi confirmed that he had renounced worldly life. The news deeply shocked the family, especially his mother, who questioned the Mahant. Though the Mahant tried to explain, the decision left Santosh’s parents grieving and worried about his future for the rest of their lives. Satua Baba's father, mother, and sister-in-law have also passed away Santosh Tiwari, alias Satua Baba's father, Shobharam Tiwari, passed away in 2019, and his elder brother Mahesh Tiwari's wife, Manisha Tiwari, died in 2023. Manisha Tiwari had served as the village head until 2021. In 2023, Santosh Tiwari's mother, Raja Beti Tiwari, also passed away. She took her last breath in Satua Baba's ashram. In her final moments, her great desire was to spend some time with her younger son, Santosh Tiwari. By then, Santosh Tiwari had become the head priest of this monastery. Currently, the families of all three elder brothers of Satua Baba are living separately in the village. All have built luxurious houses. The younger son of the eldest brother works as an accountant at Baba Ramdev's ashram in Haridwar. While the elder son is an outsourced worker at the block. Umesh Tiwari said that Santosh Tiwari got the village temple renovated by speaking with the tourism department. The last time they came to the village was in 2023 to attend their mother's thirteenth-day ritual. Became Mahamandaleshwar while Guru was still alive Yamunacharya Ji Maharaj declared Santosh Tiwari his successor and Mahamandaleshwar before his death in 2011. Since then, Santosh Tiwari has been managing the monastery and is known as Satua Baba. The Satua Peeth owns properties in several states, including Gujarat, and Satua Baba’s influence has steadily grown. In Mahakumbh-2025, he was anointed Jagadguru by Jagadguru Rambhadracharya in the presence of CM Yogi and senior saints. Satua Baba is the 57th Acharya of the Vishnu Swami Sampradaya, a lineage that began over 2,600 years ago and has continued through successive Mahants at the Satua Baba Ashram. Once ascetics in ashram used to drink sattu, today they have luxury cars worth crores There's also a story behind the name 'Satua Baba'. In 1998, the financial condition of Vishnu Peeth was quite miserable. At that time, there wasn't even a proper arrangement for food in the monastery. The ascetics survived only by drinking sattu. This is how this name came into circulation. Santosh Das, alias Satua Baba himself, says that 'Satua Baba' is not a personal name, but rather a prestigious position of the head priest in Vishnu Peeth. The ashram where ascetics once survived on sattu, today, the luxury life of its head priest is making headlines. In Banaras, this ashram has now spread over a large area. Its current value is said to be 50 crores. This monastery also has several properties in Gujarat. Those are also said to be worth crores. A luxury car worth 3 crores is parked outside Satua Baba's camp at the Magh Mela. The number UK 08 BG 8009 is from Uttarakhand, but it has Vishnu Swami Jagadguru Satua Baba Kashi written on it. Its on-road price is said to be more than 3 crores. Similarly, there is a luxury car like Porsche, which is said to be priced at 4.40 crores. Rule to report donations or property received This ashram is primarily an ancient religious seat of the Vishnu Swami sect, which operates through the guru-disciple tradition. According to the ashram's website, shrisatuababa.com, no trust deed, society number, 80G/12A certificate, or government registration details are publicly available. Property and operations run on donations from devotees. Senior High Court lawyer Jayendra Singh says that when it comes to rules, religious monasteries' property is monitored by the state government or the endowment board. When receiving large properties, it is often necessary to give notice or obtain permission.

The court noted that refunds are not the same as compensation. IndiGo is offering Rs 10,000 vouchers to some passengers. The court wants a detailed affidavit on compensation plans. Authorities have taken steps to prevent future disruptions.

stories.title: Meitei visiting Kuki fiancee shot dead on camera
stories.summary: A Meitei man visiting his Kuki fiancée in Churachandpur was abducted and shot dead on camera, sparking protests and an NIA probe. Graphic footage of the killing circulated widely. The incident occurred amidst ongoing ethnic tensions between Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities in Manipur, highlighting the fragile peace in the region.

stories.title: Lula discusses strategic ties with PM Modi, to visit in February
stories.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva will visit India from February 19-21 to strengthen the strategic partnership and discuss bilateral cooperation for the Global South. The leaders pledged to work together for UNSC reforms and peace in Gaza, with Lula also expected to attend the AI summit and a later BRICS summit.

stories.title: India condemns SFJ vandalism in Zagreb
stories.summary: India has strongly condemned the vandalism of its embassy in Zagreb by the Sikhs for Justice group, which attempted to replace the Tricolour with a "Khalistan flag." New Delhi has officially raised the matter with Croatian authorities, demanding justice for the perpetrators and emphasizing the inviolability of diplomatic premises.

stories.title: Basant Panchami, Friday prayers in separate areas of MP's Bhojshala today: SC
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has expedited the Bhojshala Saraswati Temple cum Maulana Kamal Maula Mosque dispute. Both Hindu and Muslim communities can now offer prayers simultaneously in demarcated areas. The court has lifted its stay on the Madhya Pradesh High Court proceedings. The ASI report will be unsealed and shared with both sides.

stories.title: Sajjan Kumar acquitted in a 1984 riots case
stories.summary: A Delhi court acquitted former Congress MP Sajjan Kumar in a 1984 anti-Sikh riot case, citing insufficient evidence. The judge emphasized the need for proof beyond a reasonable doubt, noting a lack of reliable testimony placing Kumar at the scene or proving his instigation. Kumar remains incarcerated due to life sentences in other riot-related convictions.

stories.title: Katy Perry faces heat for space trip while attending Davos climate talks: 'Burned 498 tons of fuel'
stories.summary: Katy Perry, renowned pop sensation, is under fire for her recent venture into space tourism, with critics pointing to contradictions in her environmental commitment. Although her sub-orbital adventure was hailed as a groundbreaking achievement for women, it also raised eyebrows due to the substantial carbon footprint associated with such flights.

stories.title: MHA notifies Census 2027 schedule, lists 33 questions
stories.summary: India's upcoming Census 2027 will collect detailed household information, including building materials, amenities like water and sanitation, and ownership status. For the first time since 1931, caste details will be gathered. The houselisting and housing phase runs April-September 2026, with population enumeration in February 2027.

stories.title: Supreme Court rejects privacy plea, allows ED to access I-PAC man's phone
stories.summary: The Supreme Court refused to stop the ED from accessing information from an I-PAC functionary's seized mobile phone, despite pleas of privacy violation. The court stated it knows how to protect innocent citizens. This comes as ED faced interruptions in Kolkata during a search, unlike in Delhi.

stories.title: 'Torture, rape, killing': Former Pakistani cop ordered to be deported earlier from Canada gets to stay
iShowSpeed responds to criticism over skipping creator collaborations during Africa tour
stories.summary: Popular streamer iShowSpeed addressed criticism regarding his Africa tour, clarifying its focus isn't on influencer collaborations but on showcasing local culture and talent. He explained that tight schedules and pre-arranged visits prevent spontaneous meetups, prioritizing respect for hosts and highlighting those without global platforms. Fans have lauded his mission to present an authentic image of African nations.

stories.title: Engineer shoots wife accidentally; distressed by death, he kills self
stories.summary: Tragedy struck in Ahmedabad as Congress MP Shaktisinh Gohil's nephew, Yashrajsinh Gohil, allegedly shot his wife Rajeshwari accidentally with a licensed revolver. Devastated by her death, he then reportedly took his own life. Police are investigating the incident, which occurred late Wednesday night in their apartment.

stories.title: New York boy walks miles for help: 6-year-old survives ice tragedy; father, friend die
SIR order makes no mention of citizenship verification: SC to EC
stories.summary: Not mentioned expressly, admits EC, but says process transparent

stories.title: Row over Trump’s hand bruise in Davos and ‘missing medical records’: ‘Two years of Biden’s health…’
stories.summary: During a high-profile ceremony at Davos, President Trump's visibly bruised hand ignited fresh discussions about his health transparency. The White House quickly explained the marks were due to a minor mishap with a table and that daily aspirin intake, which he increased for blood thinning, could lead to more bruising.

stories.title: Vyro offers $300,000 in fan rewards for clipping MrBeast’s Beast Games episodes
stories.summary: YouTube sensation MrBeast has launched Vyro, a new platform empowering fans to earn money by creating short clips from his content. Viewers, dubbed 'clippers,' can earn around $3 per 1,000 views, with payouts sent hourly. A major promotion for 'Beast Games' offers nearly $300,000 in rewards, incentivizing high-quality fan-generated content and expanding creator reach.

stories.title: Missouri man sells a car to eight people on Facebook, then steals it back within 24 hours every time
stories.summary: A Kansas City man faces 14 felony counts for allegedly running a Facebook Marketplace scam, selling vehicles to multiple buyers and then stealing them back. Prosecutors say Mamadou Diallo used forged paperwork, convincing victims to pay thousands before the cars disappeared. The scheme reportedly occurred across at least eight sales in May and June 2025.

stories.title: 'Canada thrives because...': Mark Carney's reply to President Trump's Davos dig
Is Europe ready to boycott the 2026 FIFA World Cup over Trump’s threats to Greenland?
stories.summary: Five months before kickoff, the 2026 World Cup is being pulled into geopolitics, as Donald Trump’s rhetoric over Greenland strains US–Europe relations. While no European federation has committed to a boycott, politicians and football officials are openly debating withdrawal, raising the once-unthinkable prospect of a politically fractured World Cup.

stories.title: CDS releases military quantum mission policy to prepare tri-services for future battlefield
Marvel Rivals streamer Kingsman265 surges on Twitch after being dropped from $40K event
stories.summary: A Marvel Rivals streamer named Kingsman265 saw a huge surge in Twitch followers and

stories.title: 10 soldiers killed, 11 injured as armoured carrier skids off mountain road in Jammu & Kashmir’s Doda
stories.summary: Ten brave Army soldiers lost their lives and eleven were injured when their troop carrier veered off a treacherous mountain road in Doda, Jammu & Kashmir, plunging into a deep gorge. The vehicle was en route to a counterterrorism operation. This tragic incident highlights the persistent dangers faced by military personnel in the region's challenging terrain.

stories.title: Brazilian President dials PM Modi: Reaffirm India-Brazil partnership; discuss global issues
Don Lemon not facing charge over Minnesota church incident now as judge refuses to sign
Don Lemon not facing charge over Minnesota church incident now as judge refuses to sign
Mata Vaishno Devi MBBS students offered seats in govt medical colleges in Jammu & Kashmir
stories.summary: J&K Board of Professional Entrance Examinations will adjust 50 MBBS students from the derecognized SMVDIME into seven government medical colleges. These supernumerary seats will be allocated based on NEET-UG merit and student preferences. Counselling is scheduled for Saturday, with provisions for authorized representatives.

stories.title: Piece or peace? Elon Musk takes a jab at Donald Trump’s ‘Board of Peace’ — watch
stories.summary: Elon Musk poked fun at Donald Trump's "Board of Peace," questioning if it was about "piece" of territory. Trump launched the board in Davos as part of his plan to end the Gaza war, with several nations joining. However, France and Slovenia declined, citing conflicts with international law and order.

stories.title: ‘Sorry I killed your daughter, hope you’re still a fan’: Shri Thanedar jibes at Trump over remarks on Renee Good’s death
stories.summary: In a passionate denunciation, Congressman Shri Thanedar has taken a stand against President Trump's controversial comments regarding the tragic death of Renee Nicole Good at the hands of an ICE agent. Instead of expressing sympathy, Trump chose to highlight the deceased's father's political views, prompting Thanedar to describe the President as a 'deranged sociopath.

stories.title: IMD predicts heavy snow in Jammu & Kashmir this week, 232 expectant moms hospitalised in Kulgam
stories.summary: Heavy snowfall is expected in Kashmir Valley and Pir Panjal regions starting Friday. Two western disturbances will impact the weather for nearly a week. Authorities are preparing for the harsh winter spell. Moderate to heavy rainfall and snowfall are forecast for south and north Kashmir. High-altitude areas may receive significant snow. Farmers are advised to postpone agricultural activities.

stories.title: Op Trashi-I Day 5: Gunfight erupts in Singhpora; searches continue
stories.summary: Security forces engaged in an intense gun battle with terrorists in Kishtwar's Chatroo belt, continuing Operation Trashi-I. Searches were also intensified in border areas and localities with a high concentration of foreign nationals as a precautionary measure ahead of Republic Day.

stories.title: 'Not just vandalism’: Statue damaged at Hindu temple in US, investigation under way
stories.summary: A sacred guardian statue at the Sri Venkateswara Temple in Cary, North Carolina, was vandalized on January 18. Hindu advocacy groups are condemning the act as an attack on their community, urging a thorough investigation into potential bias. Police are reviewing surveillance footage, and restoration efforts are underway, with no arrests made yet.

stories.title: Don't air internal issues in public: Congress warns Punjab leaders; no 'group activity' to be tolerated
stories.summary: Congress has issued a strong directive to its Punjab leaders, demanding an end to public displays of internal discord and factionalism. Party president Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi emphasized unity for the 2027 assembly elections, assuring no immediate leadership changes. Leaders must raise concerns internally, not through media, to present a united front for victory.

stories.title: 'Is CM so helpless': Bombay HC raps Maharashtra government; Sena minister's son evades arrest
stories.summary: The Bombay High Court sharply questioned the Maharashtra government's adherence to the rule of law, asking if the Chief Minister was too "helpless" to act against a minister whose son has evaded arrest for weeks. The court's remarks came after the police failed to apprehend the minister's son following the rejection of his pre-arrest bail plea.

stories.title: From arrest to deportation: Mahmoud Khalil’s journey from pro-Palestinian activist to anti-Israel spokesperson
stories.summary: In a dramatic turn of events, Mahmoud Khalil, an activist championing Palestinian rights and a one-time Columbia University student, finds himself on the brink of deportation from the United States. After enduring more than 100 days in detention, he was initially released by a federal judge.

stories.title: 'Operation Megaburu': 16 Maoists killed in Jharkhand; top leader Anal Da with Rs 2.35cr bounty neutralized
SUV driver in Kianna Underwood hit-and-run says he ‘did nothing wrong’
India’s hi-voltage transmission network crosses 5 lakh ckm mark
H-1B visa stamping delays continue in India, interview dates now being deferred to 2027
Uttar Pradesh steps up focus on religious sites and heritage
FBI arrests activist and school board member over St. Paul church ICE protest — who are Nekima Levy Armstrong and Chauntyll Louisa Allen?
stories.summary: Two activists, Nekima Levy Armstrong and St. Paul School Board member Chauntyll Louisa Allen, were arrested following a protest at Cities Church. The demonstration, which disrupted a service where an ICE official is a pastor, was in response to the fatal shooting of Renee Good by an ICE agent.

stories.title: Follow the path shown by farmers to compel govt to withdraw G RAM G law, Rahul tells MGNREGA workers
'Strong momentum in partnership': PM Modi speaks to Brazilian President Lula; invites him to India
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi held a productive phone call with Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, emphasizing the crucial role of their nations in advancing the Global South's interests. Both leaders expressed optimism about scaling new heights in their strategic partnership and anticipate further collaboration, with President Lula expected to visit India soon.

stories.title: Socialist vs Billionaire: Why Zohran Mamdani's relationship with NYPD chief is key for New York
stories.summary: Mamdani, 34, rode a wave of anti-establishment anger to City Hall, campaigning on taxing the rich, rethinking policing and shifting resources towards housing and mental health. Tisch, 44, is the scion of one of New York’s wealthiest families and a firm believer in proactive policing. She was appointed commissioner in 2024 and quickly earned plaudits from corporate leaders for driving down crime.

stories.title: UAE new child digital safety law puts parents at risk of fines up to AED 1 million
stories.summary: The UAE has enacted a new Child Digital Safety Law, holding parents legally accountable for their children's online activities. Effective January 1, 2026, the law mandates "Digital Due Diligence," requiring guardians to ensure age-appropriate platform use and prevent data sharing. Neglect can result in fines ranging from AED 5,000 to AED 100,000, with potential for mandatory digital rehabilitation courses.

stories.title: Singer Colin Hay slams use of 'Down Under' at rallies; urges unity, not division
'First trilateral meeting in UAE': Zelenskyy says US-Russia-Ukraine talks from tomorrow; peace documents nearly ready
Renee Good’s autopsy details revealed; Minnesota mother was shot in the 'side of the head'
Man caught in Canada for speeding in a car held together with a garden gate latch
'World’s biggest flop family': Assam CM Himanta takes dig at Gandhis; claims he is 'victim' of Rahul-Priyanka rift
stories.summary: Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma claims he was a "victim" of a rift between Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi during his Congress tenure. He also accused Assam Congress president Gaurav Gogoi and his wife of having links with Pakistan's ISI, emphasizing national security concerns.

stories.title: 'Acting like party agents': Stalin seeks to scrap governor's address; to consult 'like-minded opposition parties'
Trump’s ‘Board of Peace’ logo draws flak online, critics call it US-centric
French navy boards, searches tanker 'from Russia' in Mediterranean, says Emmanuel Macron
How ICE used a 5-year-old boy as ‘bait’ to draw family members out for detention
'Once-in-a lifetime' snowstorm alert issued for Texas, residents asked to prepare as if a hurricane is coming
'Everything hurts': Somali woman recalls 2-days of torture after ICE detained her; who is Nasra Ahmad
'Meeting was good': Trump after talks Zelenskyy in Davos; has a message for Putin
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy at Davos, stating the talks went well. Trump conveyed a message to Russian President Vladimir Putin, urging an end to the war, which has resulted in significant casualties. Despite previous efforts, no major progress has been made in resolving the conflict.

stories.title: What to know about the multiple train crashes in Spain this week
'Roving and fishing enquiry': Election Commission defends SIR in Supreme Court —what it said
stories.summary: The Election Commission defended its Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in Bihar before the Supreme Court, calling the process fair and lawful. Senior advocate Rakesh Dwivedi argued that the exercise, last conducted nearly 20 years ago, was necessary due to demographic changes and stricter citizenship requirements. The court is hearing petitions challenging the revision's legality.

stories.title: 63SATS bets big on mobile cybersecurity with insurance net in India
Murshidabad BDO office vandalised: EC orders FIR against TMC MLA Monirul Islam; cites poll-duty obstruction
Punjab: Kejriwal, Mann roll out 'Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojna'; free cashless treatment up to Rs 10 lakh
stories.summary: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann and AAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal launched the 'Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojna', offering free cashless medical treatment up to Rs 10 lakh to all 65 lakh families in the state. This universal healthcare cover, accessible to residents with Aadhaar and voter cards, includes over 2,500 procedures at government and select private hospitals.

stories.title: Can NRIs in UAE buy property on behalf of a friend in India? Legal ways to do so
stories.summary: NRIs in the UAE cannot legally pay property deposits for friends in India due to Indian foreign exchange laws. Attempting to do so risks serious violations of FEMA, leading to investigations by the Enforcement Directorate and hefty penalties. Buyers must use authorised channels like the RBI's LRS or local UAE financing for compliant transactions.

stories.title: Thousands of Chinese pilots trained every year in America: New book
stories.summary: The book argues that while the training provided is civilian in nature, the aviation skills acquired are inherently transferable. Schweizer writes that early-stage pilot instruction, including navigation, instrument flying, emergency handling, and multi-engine operations, forms the foundation of military aviation and reduces the time and cost required for later combat training.

stories.title: Delhi excise policy probe: Court acquits Arvind Kejriwal in ED summons case
stories.summary: A Delhi court has acquitted former Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal in two cases filed by the Enforcement Directorate. These cases stemmed from his failure to appear before the agency in connection with the Delhi excise policy probe. The ED had sought action against Kejriwal for not complying with multiple summons issued under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act.

stories.title: Who is Karishma Manzur? Bangladeshi-born Democrat calls to defund ICE, says agents may be from ‘extremist groups’
Barron Trump called UK police after FaceTime assault; woman says call saved her
Delhi-NCR air pollution: GRAP Stage-III curbs revoked; quality likely to stay moderate to poor
stories.summary: Air quality in Delhi-NCR has improved significantly. The Commission for Air Quality Management has lifted Stage-III restrictions under the Graded Response Action Plan. This means some construction and demolition activities can resume. However, measures under Stage-I and Stage-II remain in effect. Citizens are urged to follow guidelines to maintain better air quality.

stories.title: "He wants to be like Kanye so bad”: Kai Cenat faces backlash online after being called “performative” at Paris Fashion Week
stories.summary: Kai Cenat went viral at Paris Men’s Fashion Week 2026 after a video showed him carrying a Vivet journal showcasing his fashion ideas. While some fans praised the move, others called it “performative,” accusing him of forcing authenticity. The clip crossed 10 million views, sparking debate and comparisons to Kanye West’s creative persona.

stories.title: 'Real estate person at heart': At Board of Peace event, Trump calls Gaza beautiful piece of property
“It’s a death sentence”: MrBeast warns fans that slow photo requests can turn dangerous in seconds
stories.summary: MrBeast says taking photos with fans in public can quickly spiral into chaos if not done fast. He explained that slow photo requests draw attention, form crowds, and ruin outings. To avoid being mobbed, he takes the phone himself, snaps the picture instantly, and leaves, stressing that speed is essential despite his appreciation for fans.

stories.title: 'We'll talk': Trump says Tehran wants discussion; guards chief warns against 'miscalculations'
Evening news wrap: 10 Army personnel killed as vehicle plunges into gorge in J&K; two more builders arrested over Noida techie's death & more
stories.summary: Ten Army personnel were killed and 11 injured in Doda, Jammu and Kashmir, after their vehicle fell into a gorge. In Noida, two more builders were arrested over a software engineer's death in a construction pit. Meanwhile, a Meitei man was shot dead by suspected Kuki militants in Manipur.

stories.title: Women sway polls, men take charge: Why Nari Shakti remains a distant dream - explained
Can Dubai tenants let family stay? What law allows for relatives; what can cause legal trouble
stories.summary: Dubai tenants hosting relatives face specific rules. Short family visits are generally fine, but extended stays or co-residency require landlord permission. Article 24 of Dubai's tenancy law mandates written consent for subletting or significant occupancy changes. Ignoring these rules can lead to disputes and eviction. Always check your contract and inform your landlord.

stories.title: 'Taken up strongly’: Trespassing and vandalism at Indian embassy in Croatia— what MEA said
stories.summary: India has strongly condemned the trespassing and vandalism at its embassy in Zagreb, Croatia, by anti-India elements. The Ministry of External Affairs has urged Croatian authorities to hold the perpetrators accountable, emphasising the inviolability of diplomatic premises under the Vienna Convention. This incident follows a similar event at the Indian Consulate in Seattle last year.

stories.title: Denmark just uncovered a 600-year-old ship, the largest medieval cargo vessel ever found
‘Policing our plates’: TMC attacks Centre over Vande Bharat sleeper's veg-only menu; alleges cultural imposition
US-Greenland Talks: Denmark says 'Arctic security a NATO issue'; 'sovereignty not negotiable'
Maverick Macron vs Top Gun Trump: How French Prez's shades stole the show in Davos
stories.summary: In the thin Alpine air, amid the annual earnestness of the World Economic Forum, Macron looked less like a central banker and more like a man who had wandered in from a fighter jet. The memes followed instantly. Europe’s philosopher-king, suddenly recast as Maverick.

stories.title: Zohran Mamdani administration: Who is evironmental protection chief Indian-origin Rohit Aggarwala and why did he step down?
stories.summary: New York City's Department of Environmental Protection Commissioner Rohit Aggarwala has resigned, with his final day expected to be January 30, 2026. Aggarwala, who was appointed by former Mayor Eric Adams, focused on combating climate change and increasing flooding during his tenure. His departure follows that of Emergency Management Commissioner Zach Iscol, who also announced his resignation.

stories.title: Trump unveils 'Board of Peace': India absent from stage; Pakistan's Shahbaz Sharif joins US President
stories.summary: Former US President Donald Trump launched his "Board of Peace" initiative at the World Economic Forum in Davos. India received an invitation to join this effort aimed at resolving global conflicts. However, India was not present on the stage during the unveiling. Several countries, including some from the Middle East and Asia, were listed as participants in the initiative.

stories.title: 'America not ready for woman president': Gretchen Whitmer clashes with Michelle Obama
stories.summary: Obama’s view is shaped by electoral memory rather than abstraction. The defeats of Hillary Clinton in 2016 and Kamala Harris in 2024 still loom over the party, particularly because both contests ended with victories for Donald Trump. From that perspective, Obama’s argument is not that sexism explains everything, but that it explains enough to make denial untenable.

stories.title: This is the driest place on Earth where rain may not fall for centuries
Noida techie death: NGT takes suo motu cognisance after fatal drowning; flags environmental violation
'Pain completely disregarded': Sajjan Kumar acquitted in 1984 anti-Sikh riots case; victims’ families vow to keep fighting
stories.summary: Families affected by the 1984 anti-Sikh riots expressed deep disappointment and anger after former Congress MP Sajjan Kumar was acquitted in a case linked to alleged incitement of violence. Despite this acquittal, Kumar remains in prison serving a life sentence in other related murder cases, leaving victims' families feeling their long search for justice is still unfulfilled.

stories.title: How China created artificial islands by dumping sand into the sea in just one decade
J&K: 10 killed as army vehicle plunges into 200-feet gorge; PM Modi offers condolences
'BJP wants king's rule': Rahul Gandhi urges 'poor' to unite against VB-G RAM G Act; links it to repealed farm laws
stories.summary: Addressing the National MGNREGA Workers’ Convention organised by the Rachnatmak Congress, Rahul Gandhi said PM Modi wants to finish the concept of Panchayati Raj and alleged that the ruling BJP wants an India "where the King decides everything". With the new law, the Centre will decide the work and allocation of funds with BJP-ruled governments always getting precedence, he said.

stories.title: Why healthcare still fails millions—and how India can fix it: Lancet Commission’s citizen-centred roadmap
Manipur violence: Militants kill Meitei man visiting Kuki wife; shooting caught on camera
Drone attack: Russian oil port blasts, fuel tanks damaged in attack by Ukraine; 3 killed
stories.summary: A Russian oil terminal near Volna was hit late Wednesday. The strike caused a major fire, killing at least two people and injuring several others. Four oil product tanks caught fire. Emergency services extinguished the blaze by Thursday morning. This marks the second consecutive night of attacks on Krasnodar Krai. Ukraine considers Russian energy infrastructure legitimate military targets.

stories.title: No Permit, No Repair: Kuwait mandates pre-approval for all exhaust repairs
stories.summary: Kuwait's General Traffic Department has implemented a new procedure requiring official approval before exhaust system repairs for vehicles and motorcycles. Owners must obtain a repair permit from Technical Inspection Departments for violations, then get a follow-up inspection after repairs at authorized facilities. This aims to streamline services, ensure compliance with technical standards, and reduce noise pollution.

stories.title: MP: SC allows Hindus, Muslims to offer prayers at Bhojshala on Basant Panchami — what was the dispute?
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has permitted Hindu prayers at the Bhojshala-Kamal Maula Mosque from sunrise to sunset on Basant Panchami, while Muslims can offer namaz between 1 pm and 3 pm. The court also mandated sharing the ASI's expert report on the site's religious character with both communities.

stories.title: Summer 2026 travel crunch: UAE residents race for Schengen visas
stories.summary: UAE travellers are booking summer 2026 getaways unusually early, with enquiries starting in January. This shift is driven by significant visa appointment backlogs for Schengen and UK travel, alongside rising airfare and hotel costs. Residents are adopting a more strategic approach, booking early to secure deals and avoid potential delays.

stories.title: Operation Trashi-I: Day 5 sees fresh encounter in J&K's Kishtwar; JeM terrorists holed up in dense forests
stories.summary: Security forces engaged in a fresh gunfight with holed-up terrorists in Jammu and Kashmir's Kishtwar district on Thursday. The ongoing "Operation Trashi-I," launched Sunday, intensified as a search team encountered a group of two to three foreign terrorists, believed to be Jaish-e-Mohammad operatives, in Singhpora's dense forests.

stories.title: Ice in the desert? UAE records its lowest temperature of the season at 0.2°C
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates recorded its coldest morning of the winter season as temperatures dropped to 0.2°C early today, according to the National Centre of Meteorology. The reading was logged at 5.45 am amid a January cold spell, with other areas also reporting low temperatures, highlighting unusually chilly winter conditions across mountainous and inland parts of the country this morning nationwide today.

stories.title: Dubai crash leaves Indian biker with Rs 1 crore hospital bill: What happened on E311 and what expat riders should know about insurance, road safety
stories.summary: An Indian expat in Dubai faces a staggering Dh400,000 hospital bill after a motorbike crash on E311 left him with multiple fractures. Avinash Sequeira, uninsured, underwent emergency surgeries and faces more, highlighting critical issues of road safety, high healthcare costs, and insurance gaps for freelancers in the UAE. His family seeks community support.

stories.title: Skip the layover: SpiceJet launches direct Ahmedabad–Sharjah flights this February
stories.summary: SpiceJet will launch non-stop flights between Ahmedabad and Sharjah from February 5, 2026, adding its second UAE destination after Dubai. Operating five days a week, the service targets business travellers, tourists, and expatriates. The route strengthens connectivity between India and the United Arab Emirates, with fares starting around Dh900 and bookings now open across official channels using available bilateral capacity for passengers.

stories.title: You’re 'not addicted' to screen: What is Doomscrolling and why it feels impossible to stop?
stories.summary: Late-night scrolling through distressing news, known as doomscrolling, is a stress response, not a lack of discipline. Our brains, wired for survival, interpret constant negative information as a threat, leading to anxiety and sleep issues. Understanding this helps shift focus from self-blame to managing stress and practicing digital hygiene for peace

stories.title: ‘Ridiculous’: Sanjay Raut takes ‘picnic in Davos’ jibe at Fadnavis; CM’s wife Amruta Fadnavis hits back
stories.summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut criticized Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis' Davos visit as a 'picnic,' questioning the WEF's relevance for India and suggesting agreements could be made in Mumbai. CM's wife Amruta Fadnavis dismissed the remarks as baseless, highlighting the summit's importance for investment and employment.

stories.title: ‘Nobody rescued yet’: Several feared missing in landslip at New Zealand campsite; minister calls it ‘war-zone’
stories.summary: A devastating landslide at a New Zealand campsite has left several people missing. Emergency crews are searching through debris after the slip swept through campervans and tents. Difficult conditions and unstable ground are hampering rescue efforts as authorities work to account for everyone.

stories.title: Guru as ‘parent’, elephants on the road: Voter-roll fixes in Bengal get inventive
stories.summary: How to avoid jumbos? And how does one obtain proof of residence from someone who doesn’t have any? During Bengal’s SIR, involving more than 7 crore voters, election officials came up with novel solutions — to solve problems faced by, among others, monks, tea garden labourers and sex workers

stories.title: Texas AG candidate’s anti-Indian post backfires as community note flags Pakistani scammer among his top donors
stories.summary: Texas Republican AG candidate Aaron Reitz faced backlash for a social media post comparing Texas counties to Indian cities, sparking accusations of targeting a specific community. A Community Note highlighted a major donor, a Pakistani-American doctor indicted in a healthcare fraud case, raising questions about Reitz's campaign funding and alleged hypocrisy.

stories.title: Trust set up without my informed consent, revoke it: Sunjay’s mom
stories.summary: Rani Kapur has filed a plea in the Delhi High Court seeking the cancellation of the Rani Kapur Family Trust. She alleges the trust, which holds a stake in Sona Comstar, was created and operated without her knowledge or consent while she was medically unwell.

stories.title: EC seeks WB reply for defying its order against poll officers
Meet Jens Kjeldsen: 70-year-old man who protests outside the US Consulate in Greenland every morning in freezing cold
stories.summary: A 70-year-old retiree, Jens Kjeldsen, stages a daily protest outside the US Consulate in Greenland, holding flags of Denmark, Greenland, and the Faroe Islands. His quiet, routine demonstration signifies resistance against President Trump's renewed interest in acquiring Greenland, emphasizing the territory's sovereignty and the right of its people to decide their future.

stories.title: Display West Bengal discrepancies, unmapped list by Jan 24: EC
stories.summary: Following a Supreme Court directive, the Election Commission has instructed the Bengal CEO to display names of electors with 'logical discrepancies' and 'unmapped' status by January 24. People in these categories can submit documents via authorized representatives, with authorities ensuring smooth proceedings and no law and order issues.

stories.title: CEC cites success of SIR in Bihar at global meet
World must show zero tolerance for terror, EAM tells Spain counterpart
stories.summary: India and Spain have pledged to strengthen international cooperation against terrorism, with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar emphasizing a "zero tolerance" approach. The two nations reviewed bilateral ties, including trade, defense, and culture, and discussed regional developments. Spain also acceded to India's Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative.

stories.title: Need to strengthen development trajectory in Manipur: PM
